articleTitle: Innovations in Virtual Reality for Treating Acrophobia: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Acrophobia is an intense fear of heights that plagues a substantial segment of the world population. Classic treatments such as cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure therapy help the patients but come with the constraint that they are not accessible to everyone and not all patients stick to them. This paper explores the design and implementation of virtual reality (VR) in treating acrophobia through an immersive and controlled setting for graded exposure. New avenues for patients to confront their fears have been opened up by the integration of multisensory feedback and customizable scenarios in VR. This paper details a comprehensive analysis of the design, implementation, results, and comparative effectiveness of treatments designed based on VR for acrophobia.

articleTitle: Green Mobility Solutions Through Intelligent Fleet Management and Smart Logistics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Smart logistics and green mobility are the future-oriented solutions to improve efficiency, sustainability, and environmental responsibility in transportation and logistics. Advanced technologies like IoT, AI, and data analytics are utilized by smart logistics to optimize the supply chain process, remove inefficiencies, and ensure real-time tracking and monitoring. Such intelligent use of technology makes the logistics ecosystem's operations more streamlined and leads to better decision-making. Green mobility is an environmentally friendly mode of transportation that aims to decrease the ecological footprint of logistic operations. In this paper, it is seen in the form of electric and hybrid vehicles, alternative fuels, and sustainable transport modes. The green mobility concept focuses on reducing carbon emissions, less dependence on fossil fuels, and promoting environmentally friendly transport.

articleTitle: Order Abatement Technique for LTI MIMO Systems Based on Squirrel Search Algorithm & Dominant Pole Retention
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The hybrid order abatement technique for MIMO High Order Linear Dynamic Systems (HOLDSs) is presented in this research. In this study, the original HOLDSs' denominator is lowered using the Dominant Pole Retention Technique and the reduced numerator is obtained using the Squirrel Search Optimization Algorithm (SSOA). The abated system is the result of combining the benefits of the two mentioned strategies. The recommended approach aims to minimize the Integral Square Error (ISE) while preserving the HOLDSs' characteristics. The suggested approach guarantees both the conservation of transient stability and the steady state stability of the original HOLDSs. A comprehensive comparison study of two high-order linear dynamic systems (HOLDSs) has been conducted. Simulink/MATLAB is used for the calculation and plotting of the step response. The findings are compared with several reduction techniques found in the literature. The results demonstrate that the suggested strategy gives a lower ISE in comparison to alternative methods. The comparison is also done for IAE & ITAE which also provides the proposed technique better than others.

articleTitle: IoTs Applications in Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: IoT technologies cater to several applications and benefits in supply chain management (SCM), like real-time visibility, data analytics, and automation. IoT sensors and devices can be attached to assets, which include containers, pallets, and vehicles, to track their location, condition, and status in real-time. Asset tracking enables supply chain stakeholders to monitor the movement of merchandise at any point in the supply chain, recognizes delays or disruptions, and allows for logistics operation optimization. The process of integrating IoT devices with blockchain technology allows a secure and translucent data sharing and transactions along the supply chain. IoT platforms based on blockchain enable immutable records of product provenance, authenticity, and ownership that foster supply chain participants' transparency, traceability, and trust. The case study explored in this research examines such practical implementation. Organisations can create a more visible, efficient, agile supply chain by leveraging IoT applications for better customer satisfaction, cost reduction, and a competitive dimension in the market.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality for Sustainable Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Currently, in a transitioning world to sustainable energy systems, the need for technologies that facilitate the design, deployment, optimization, and maintenance of renewable energy systems has grown. A powerful tool that offers deep immersiveness and simulations has emerged in the form of Virtual Reality (VR). This paper examines the applications of VR in the energy sector to optimize renewable energy systems, enhancing energy efficiency, and facilitating workforce training. The paper contextualizes the role VR is playing in energy transitions and its contribution to global sustainability goals.

articleTitle: A Recent Advancements in Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion Techniques using SWT, NSST, NSCT, and CNN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Image fusion is a method used in image processing to provide a more complete representation by amalgamating features and data from many images. Multimodal medical image fusion involves the integration of medical images from many imaging modalities, including computed tomography (CT) scans, positron emission tomography (PET), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), into one single dataset. This integration enhances the visualisation of anatomical structures and clinical situations, hence improving diagnostic accuracy by leveraging the strengths of each medium. This study employs MRI, CT, and PET scans as experimental modalities. This review aims to compare various multi modal medical image approach based on Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT), Non-Subsampled Shearlet Transform (NSST), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and NonSubsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT). This study examines the latest conventional and non-conventional research conducted within these disciplines. It further evaluates these approaches according to diverse image quality metrics and many quantitative assessments. According to this comparison, CNN-based fusion demonstrates superior results, as the overall visual and parametric quality of the fusion outcomes surpasses that of the other approaches evaluated.

articleTitle: Optimizing Drug Discovery Using Computational Databases and Bioinformatics for Terminalia Arjuna Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Ayurveda is a very important part of the ancient Indian medical system, and all the research related to medicine that has been done in the world till date has its roots in Indian scriptures as well as texts. Plants have been known for their medicinal properties since the mediaeval period, and the phytochemicals produced by plants act as a defense mechanism against pathogens. Traditional plants can treat metabolic, neurological, and immunological disorders in human beings. In the 21st century, the medical sector is searching for medicinal plants as an influential source for the development of new drugs due to their pharmacological effects. The field of medicinal plant research has greatly advanced with the integration of bioinformatics and computational databases, especially in terms of improving drug development and toxicity prediction. This study is related to computational tools for the prediction of different physicochemical and toxicity profiles of phytochemicals from selected medicinal plants. Therefore, the importance of bioinformatics has transformed the study of medicinal plants by facilitating the discovery of novel, lowtoxicity therapeutic chemicals and providing access to the development of safe and effective herbal treatments. Main objective of this study is to explore various phytochemical databases, toxicity predictive nature and docking studies of different phytochemicals of Arjuna plant via computational databases and bioinformatics.

articleTitle: Lumbar Spine Segmentation Based on Sagittal View Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Spine diseases have taken rise in numbers these days There are many diseases affecting the Lumbar part of the Spine like stenosis, herniated discs, and many more. Sometimes condition of the patient becomes so bad that they need spine surgeries. artificial intelligence algorithms and various Image processing methods can be efficiently used to study MRI and CT Images and diagnose these diseases in the early stages. Traditional methods of Image segmentation are having many drawbacks including time consuming, the accuracy of results not good as well as tough to segment complex structures. This study presents the Implementation of deep learning methods on a small dataset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T 1$</tex> weighted MRI images in sagittal view. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$U$</tex> net shows best result of DC 92.23, precision 92.14, and recall as 91.56 as compared to SVM and FCN.

articleTitle: Green Energy Achieve Via High Deployment of Renewable Energy Technologies and the Implementation of Smart Grid Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The study describes theses of the renewable energies and the developmental process of power grid technology for the management of energy. The aim of the research is to analyze and represent the value of green energies as well as the processes to obtain that energy from nature. The primary objective of creating green energy technology is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and waste while producing energy in a sustainable way, resulting in lowering the total carbon footprint of energy production. In this paper the processes and methods of the research has been explained such as qualitative research methods. Thematic analysis based on the research objectives are done to evaluate the impact of green energy and its process implication related to smart grid technology. The discussion includes all the matters of renewable energy and the processes of utilisation.

articleTitle: Insight on Ge-Si0.4Ge0.6 Hetero Structured Tunnel field Effect Transistor for Energy Efficient IOT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative device architecture aimed at augmenting drive current, reducing ambipolar characteristics, and improving subthreshold slope, referred to as Hetero junction Ge source TFET (H-Ge-TFET). This device employs hetero dielectric material at the source-channel junction along with bandgap engineering to enhance performance. The improvement in subthreshold swing within the device pertains to an inclusion of high-k dielectric at the source-channel junction, whereas the ambipolar current is effectively mitigated by utilizing low-k dielectric material at the drain channel junction. In order to evaluate the performance characteristics of the device, a range of parameters has been meticulously calculated, encompassing capacitances (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> and Cgd), and transconductance (gm). Eventually, an investigation has been conducted comparing H-Ge-TFET and High-K C-TFET, revealing their notable impact on analog and RF parameters. All simulations of the proposed device have been executed utilizing the SILVACO 2D device simulator.

articleTitle: A Multiband, Wideband Wearable Textile Antenna for Body Area Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A novel multi-band wearable textile antenna is designed, fabricated, and tested for functioning in the NB-IoT (Narrowband-IoT) 1.8 GHz, ISM (Industrial Scientific Medical) 2.4 GHz, and 5.8 GHz frequency bands. The suggested antenna is an upgraded version of the conventional triangular patch antenna constructed on a flexible substrate made of inexpensive and widely available denim cloth. This antenna's top patch has uneven meandering slots and a partial ground plane, leading to compact size and multiband functioning. This textile patch antenna has an area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.375 \lambda_{o} \times 0.375 \lambda_{o}$</tex>. The designed antenna has wide impedance bandwidths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$370 \text{MHz}, 1600$</tex> MHz, and 1240 MHz at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.8,2.4$</tex>, and 5.8 GHz and sufficient gains of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.4,3.3$</tex>, and 7.6 dBi, respectively. The results from simulations and measurements show excellent agreement to prove its usefulness in practical applications.

articleTitle: Design of Square Ring Triple Band Planner Antenna with DGS for WLAN/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In the present endeavor, a tiny, multi-band embossed monopole antenna is proposed for WLAN and WiMAX applications. The antenna configuration is modest with a small size of 22×32mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0.176λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.256λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). The presented antenna is made of a plus-shaped strip surrounded by a reformed square ring on a defect ground structure and equipped with a microstrip feedline. The presented antenna generates three different bands I from 2.4 to 2.63 GHz, II from 3.2 to 4.0 GHz and III from 5.1 to 5.89 GHz, clearly covering the full WLAN (2.4/5.2/5.8 GHz) and WiMAX (2.5/3.5/5.5). Parametric studies have been completed to analyse the characteristics of this antenna. As a result, excellent antenna performance has been achieved.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Prediction Using AHP and Fuzzy TOPSIS Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The heart is undeniably the most vital organ in the human body, essential for sustaining life through its proper and continuous functioning. A healthy and well-functioning heart is crucial to overall well-being, and any dysfunction can pose serious risks, potentially leading to life-threatening conditions. The early detection of heart disease is critical, as it can significantly impact a person's chances of survival. In this study, we focus on identifying the key attributes that influence the onset and progression of heart disease. To achieve this, we apply the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Fuzzy TOPSIS methods to evaluate and rank these attributes. These decisionmaking techniques allow us to systematically analyse and prioritize the various criteria that contribute to heart disease prognosis. By assigning ranks to each attribute, we identify which factors carry the greatest weight in determining heart disease risk. The attribute ranked highest-assigned the rank of 1 -emerges as the most critical risk factor, providing valuable insights for improving heart disease prediction and prevention. This approach enhances the accuracy of medical diagnostics and helps in identifying key factors that require immediate attention in managing heart health.

articleTitle: The Smart Optimization of Anomaly Detection in Video Image Processing using Swin-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The video snapshot processing undertakes the critical assignment of anomaly detection that enables the identification of any unexpected or unusual events that can take place in a current video flow. Traditional systems for anomaly detection in this space face borders that encompass a sluggish processing pace and coffee accuracy. We recommend using this transformer-based neural network architecture, SwinTransformer, to overcome the above challenges. This method has sustained promising gains throughout numerous computer idea tasks, such as object detection and image classification. Our method leverages the self-attention mechanism of the SwinTransformer to explore the spatiotemporal relationship in video sequences, providing a promise that anomaly detection performance can also be significantly improved. Further, we include a clever optimization strategy that uses a pre-trained model and fine-tuning to speed up the training time and boost performance. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our method, outperforming the state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Education Loan Approval Automation Using Logistic Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This article presents a logistic regression-based approach to automating education loan approval processes in the context of Indian banks. Our methodology is distinguished by its focus on education loans, a niche area that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been previously explored. We achieve an accuracy rate of approximately 88%, outperforming existing studies that employed logistic regression for general loan prediction. The superiority of our algorithm can be attributed to the judicious selection of attributes and effective data preprocessing techniques. Notably, our approach does not rely on credit scores, making it particularly suited for education loan applicants who often lack established credit histories. By consulting loan application forms from various Indian banks, we identified key attributes that inform our predictive model. This study's novelty lies in its ability to accurately predict loan approval without relying on credit scores, offering a valuable tool for lenders and borrowers alike.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Sustainable Water Management: Empowering Communities for Clean Future
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The availability of safe and healthy water is of utmost importance for sustaining life, and addressing the global issue of water purity is crucial. Water contamination is primarily attributed to industrial activities, which discharge substantial pollutants, including heavy metals, chemicals, and organic compounds. Other factors are using fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides in agriculture, inadequate sewage treatment infrastructure, and improper wastewater disposal from households and commercial places. Public participation can play a vital role in reducing these issues, and a public-private partnership with a secure blockchain-based model offers a possible solution. Some instances, like the Philippines, have adopted a blockchain- based water conservation reward system solution. To assess water quality, researchers use various water quality metrics like pH, turbidity, temperature, electrical conductivity, and oxidation-reduction potential to measure through the Internet of Things (IoT). Nonetheless, it is essential to establish a secure platform for storing all these metrics, allowing the results to be shared with the public and enabling community involvement in water cleaning efforts. In this regard, the paper proposes a system for cleaning water bodies and rewarding volunteers who successfully participate in cleaning drives. This system ensures trust and transparency in record-keeping

articleTitle: Marine Current Energy Coupled with a VSC-HVDC Link Integrated with the Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The increase word electricity demand has forced a shift to renewable energy, which is pollution-free, emission-free, and helps mitigate climate change. Ocean energy considered a renewable energy source proves a unique solution due to its large availability, predictability, pollution-free, and no storage problem. The scope of ocean energy generation is wide in countries having large coastal areas. Nowadays VSC-HVDC is a more advanced and efficient technology for power transmission and distribution systems for offshore renewable s due unique capability of controlling active and reactive power, Providing asynchronous link multi terminal link and technical improvements in the field of VSC -HVDC. This paper reviews an offshore marine turbine with a VSC-HVDC link and its grid integration.

articleTitle: Advancing Precision in Heart Disease Detection and Prediction: Leveraging Cutting-Edge Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The latest government statistics reveal a 12% increase in heart attack deaths in 2022, with 32,457 fatalities reported by the National Crime Records Bureau [1]. Heart attacks, part of the broader category of cardiovascular diseases (non-communicable diseases), experienced a sharp rise after a decline from 28,579 in 2020 to 28,413 in 2021, before escalating to 32,457 in 2022. This paper employs Naïve Bayes and Logistic Regression, two commonly used algorithms in supervised machine learning, for classification tasks. The data was analyzed using these methods, and their performance was quantified through metrics like sensitivity, accuracy or exactitude, positive predictive value, F1 score, specificity, and misclassification rate. The uncovering prudent that the put forward classification methods enhance the accuracy of medical diagnoses. The objective of this paper is to predict true positive rates while minimizing misclassification errors. The proposed model has demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy, true positive rate, specificity, and misclassification error reduction.

articleTitle: The Impact of AI on Human Psychology: A User Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into many human activities has produced a growing conversation about its psychological consequences on users. The main focus of the comprehensive responses of AI users in this research is the cognitive and emotive aspects of its influence on human psychology. Using the data collected from a varied group of users, this study exposes the influence of AI interactions on user perceptions, emotions, and mental processes. Key results show that although artificial intelligence technologies can significantly boost productivity, inspire innovation, and simplify decision-making, they can also cause anxiety, reliance, and changed social behaviors. The paper investigates essential concerns, including the psychological consequences of deepfake technology, the possibility of artificial intelligence recording human rights violations, and the consequences of AI-driven monitoring. It stresses both positive and negative effects. Furthermore, under evaluation are consumers' degrees of adaptation to the growing influence of artificial intelligence and the variations in psychological reactions among different user groups. This study underlines the need for transparency, user autonomy, and ethical AI deployment by pointing out ways that AI developers and stakeholders might apply to lower unexpected psychological effects. This thorough investigation helps to clarify how artificial intelligence shapes human psychological experiences and supports a sensible approach that maximizes benefits and reduces possible risks. The research aims to guide the path of following artificial intelligence developments, thereby ensuring technologically conscious and user-centric technological innovations.

articleTitle: CSRR Based Decoupled Dual Port MIMO Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: An inverted S-shaped dual-port antenna for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is designed. The suggested design measures 28 ×20 ×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>in total. Better isolation is achieved by placing a CSRR (complementary split-ring resonator) between the inverted S-shaped patches. With a good isolation of> 20 dB, this design exhibits a frequency range variation of 3.5-4.7 GHz. The proposed design shows a range of realized gain and radiation efficiency 1.9 to 2.92 dBi and 80% to 90%, respectively. The effectiveness of the MIMO design is evaluated by examining important diversity metrices. To get theoretical insights, the MIMO setup is modelled with the simulation using CST Microwave Studio. A physical prototype of the design is manufactured in order to validate the experimental results. Moreover, this study is extended to four port MIMO antenna design, which effectively covers the 5G spectrum, enabling high-speed data communication.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling in Forecasting Water Levels for Sustainable Resources Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Water, sometimes called blue gold, is an important resource for ecosystems, industry, habitats, and ecosystem ser-vices. The board's water asset is fundamental given the increasing demands of today and the emerging problems brought forth by environmental change. This analysis provides insights into data-driven solutions to address this problem by creating predictive models that measure water accessibility in various types of water bodies, such as lakes, streams, and springs. These recurring water sources have unique behaviours that are impacted by several factors, including location, environment, and sporadic changes. This study uses information-explicit approaches, with a focus on time series demonstrating and information science, to overcome this entanglement. The goal is to develop precise numerical models that capture the unique characteristics of each type of water body and result in significant water supply expectations. This endeavour, which sits at the intersection of ecological stewardship and information science, aims to provide chiefs with reliable estimations that will assist in supporting the board's water assets. Our models, which estimate monthly water levels or daily fluctuations, are an important tool for protecting these water bodies by providing a consistent supply of water. By harnessing the power of knowledge, we strengthen the defence of the “blue gold” that sustains life and the ultimate destiny of our planet.

articleTitle: Analysis Ethical and Social Implications of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has progressed significantly in recent years, revolutionizing various industries and influencing numerous aspects of everyday life. This research paper aims to explore unique insights into AI, focusing on its advancements, challenges, and future implications. Through an in-depth analysis of the existing literature and cutting-edge developments, this study presents an original perspective on AI and its role in shaping the world. The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in manipulating images, videos, and voices has led to the rise of AI-based voice scams. This research paper aims to shed light on the alarming rate at which Indian individuals are falling prey to such fraudulent activities and the lack of awareness and information that contributes to their victimization. Through a comprehensive analysis of a recent study by McAfee, this paper emphasizes the urgent need to educate and inform individuals about the risks associated with AI-generated voices and provides recommendations for prevention.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Hurst Exponents in the Multifractral Detendrated Fluctuation Analysis (MFDFA) of ASD Patients' EEG Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The EEG signal measured by a particular channel electrode in a certain brain region is a collective behavior of the population of neurons around that channel electrode and exhibits complex patterns. We study these complex EEG data from individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using the Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MFDFA) technique to understand the changes in fluctuations-driven correlation compared to normal. We used data from publicly available ASD patients for analysis and focus on the behavior of multifractal parameters h_q^+ and h_q^-, representing the generalized Hurst exponent with positive and negative values of q, respectively, which correspond to large and small fluctuations in the collective behavior of neurons. Our results provide insights into different levels of complexity across different brain regions, providing a deeper understanding of the neurological system of autism.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Technologies for Electric Vehicle Charging Application: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: With the fusion of fossil fuels coming to an end, we are transitioning towards sustainable powers like Electric Vehicles (EVs) which have no emissions. EVs can take a long time to charge and plug-in chargers are slow and hit-or-miss. A plausible solution to this problem is Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) as it can charge devices without any physical connection and thus easier, convenient and safer. Wireless power transfer has existed, in theatrically demonstrated form (thanks to Nikola Tesla) since at least the 1890s and is currently used for EV charging while static or even dynamic. This is all good and well, but dynamic charging adds cost. Additionally, coil misalignment and efficiency loss are challenges to be faced by WPT but security measures have been developed throughout the years that make it more effective. This solution also offers safe and low-cost handling, but operates optimally over short distances. With continued advancements, it could fundamentally change how our EVs are charged for a cleaner and greener future. With ongoing technological progress, it has the potential to overcome its current limitations and become the leading charging solution for EVs, ultimately contributing to a cleaner and greener future. As advancements continue, it could fundamentally transform the way we charge our EVs.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms on Credit Card Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Fraud detection is a crucial area not only for credit cards but also for industries handling financial transactions where fraud detection is crucial. Machine Learning (ML) had come up powerfully with a variety of tools that can process large amounts of data and can find complex hidden patterns from the data. This abstract provides the usage of ML Algorithms in Fraud Detection with different types of techniques used. In this paper a comparison has been made between different algorithms based on their Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. Algorithms Used are SVM, KNN, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression. Dataset was collected from Kaggle and it contains 284806 rows and a total of 31 columns.

articleTitle: System Reliability Modelling Under UGF and Intuitionistic Fuzzy Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Many physical-world systems are complex and consist of inter-connected elements. The idea of series-parallel reliability is important in the field of reliability engineering, especially when analyzing the reliability of complex systems. In this study, the authors have utilized the techniques of Universal Generating Function and Intuitionistic Fuzzy Numbers to evaluate reliability. As an example, an Electronic Stability Control system with two sub-systems, mainly a sensor system and an actuation system with multi-components is considered. The authors model the reliability of the complete system considering a general system of the same and further calculate the reliability of the series-parallel positioning of the components as an application to the above-mentioned analytical techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis of Detailed-Phasor and Phasor-Phasor Model of Phase Shifting Transformer Using On-load Tap Changer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The paper deals with the development and analysis of the MATLAB model of a phase-shifting transformer (PST). Two separate cases of delta-hexagonal transformers are taken to be built and their performances are compared to analyze the gain in speed of simulation due to differences in the type of PST model used and developed. In the first case, one transformer is phasor type and the second transformer is detailed type thus using the detailed-phasor simulation method whereas in the second case, both transformers are built using the phasor-phasor simulation method-based model. Simulink model cases are built twice and on-load tap changers are specifically used for the operation of phase shifting of the deltahexagonal PST. In both cases of simulation, phase shifting transformers are interconnected to two networks of 120 kV with a rating of 1000 MVA. The impact of phase shifting on the transfer of power is observed and results are obtained for various tap positions, phase current, superposition of voltage at different buses, phase shift of voltage at output terminals, and active power. The aim of the experiment is to analyze the abovementioned parameters and how fast the model runs when the detailed model of the detailed-phasor case is replaced by the phasor model to give phasor-phasor model-based simulated outputs.

articleTitle: A Contemporary Approach to Acknowledge Vehicle Registration Numbers Using Deep Learning-Based Edge Detection Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: It might be challenging sometimes to recognize car owners who drive excessively fast and against the regulations of the road. Therefore, number plate recognition of the vehicles can be one of the best solutions to this problem. Number plate recognition is the emerging technology in this modern era that is based on the optical character recognition to recognize the registration number of vehicles. Sometimes it's seen that the data is misread because of poor edge detection technique used. In this paper we try to figure out the best edge detection technique among the present detection techniques that are Sobel operator, Canny Edge Detection and Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG). This study employed a variety of image processing techniques, including morphological transformation, Gaussian smoothing, Gaussian thresholding, and Sobel edge detection methods. Then Plate segmentation is performed, contours are drawn, and the contours are filtered based on character size and spatial orientation. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is the final step in identifying the retrieved characters. The database stores the identified texts, which are then sorted and made searchable.

articleTitle: Frontal Brain Hyperconnectivity: An Effective Neural Marker for Schizophrenia Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Schizophrenia is one of the most serious mental health conditions, characterized by difficulties in thoughts, feelings, and behavior. Electroencephalography (EEG) is one of the important tools that can capture brain activity at milliseconds scale. This study aims to develop a machine learning algorithm based on functional connectivity to distinguish between schizophrenic and healthy controls. The dataset used in this research is obtained from the Institute of Psychiatry and Neurology in Warsaw, Poland. Initial data preprocessing involved notch filtering and decomposition of EEG signal through Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to extract alpha band spectrum. A non-overlapping window of 1-second duration is used to compute correlation-based connectivity between all EEG electrode pairs. These features were then used to train multiple machine-learning models. The cubic Support Vector Machine (SVM) model demonstrated a testing accuracy of 96.87%. Further, to reduce the dimensionality of feature space, training was focused on specific brain regions (frontal and occipital areas). It is found that frontal lobe connectivity is highly abrupt for schizophrenic people, achieving an outstanding testing accuracy of 99.97% with reduced network nodes. Moreover, it is observed that schizophrenia is related to higher localized connectivity, specifically, in the frontal area of the brain compared to healthy controls, which signifies disorganized thinking due to emotional imbalance in schizophrenic people.

articleTitle: Adaptive Load Frequency Control Using Artificial Neural Networks for Enhancing Grid Stability in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to Load Frequency Control (LFC) in power systems using machine learning algorithms, specifically artificial neural networks (ANNs). Traditional LFC methods, such as PID controllers, often struggle to maintain optimal performance in the face of increasing grid complexity and renewable energy integration. Our proposed ML-based LFC system addresses these challenges by leveraging the adaptive capabilities of ANNs. We present a comprehensive methodology encompassing data collection, model design, training processes, and real-time implementation strategies. Extensive simulations demonstrate the superiority of our approach over conventional PID controllers, achieving significant improvements in settling time, frequency deviation, and control efficiency. The ML-based system shows remarkable adaptability to varying system conditions, including scenarios with high renewable energy penetration. These results suggest that ML-based LFC systems could significantly enhance grid stability, efficiency, and reliability in modern power systems. Our work contributes to the ongoing evolution of smart grid technologies and offers a promising solution for the challenges faced by power systems in the renewable energy era.

articleTitle: A Computational Outlook on the Potential of Cyanobacteria in Cancer Treatment and Drug Discovery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Cancer remains a global health crisis, with millions of new cases and deaths reported annually. Various factors, including genetic defects, lifestyle choices, and environmental exposures cause the disease. Different types of cancer, such as carcinomas, sarcomas, leukemias, lymphomas, and brain tumors, affect other organs and have distinct causes. Treatment methods typically involve a combination of surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, immunotherapy, and stem cell transplants. However, each treatment has its side effects, which can sometimes be severe and impact patients' quality of life. To address these challenges, researchers are exploring the potential of natural products, such as compounds from red clover, turmeric, green tea, soybeans, garlic, and fruits, in cancer therapy. Of particular interest are cyanobacteria, which produce bioactive compounds with anticancer properties. Cyanobacteria- derived products show promise in targeted drug delivery, reducing side effects, enhancing immune responses, and potentially improving cancer treatment outcomes. Molecular docking studies have revealed the efficacy of cyanobacterial metabolites in inhibiting breast cancer-related proteins, highlighting their therapeutic potential in cancer treatment. Further research is needed to harness the full potential of natural therapies in managing cancer and its side effects.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Networks for the Development of Efficient Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Digital technologies have facilitated instant communication and global access to information via social media platforms. However, this connectivity has also led to the widespread dissemination of fake news, which poses significant risks by undermining public opinion, disrupting political processes, threatening public health, and contributing to economic instability the adverse impacts of fake news range from influencing elections to exacerbating crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. Thus, identifying and mitigating fake news is critical. Traditional detection methods have relied on content relationships and social context features, but these approaches are often vulnerable to adversarial attacks and struggle to address the complexities of information propagation. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), present promising solutions for fake news detection. GNNs can effectively model complex relationships and dependencies in social networks, allowing for automatic learning of intricate patterns from raw data, potentially outperforming traditional methods. This study examines cutting-edge fake news detection techniques, explicitly focusing on GNN methodologies. The reported results show better efficacy and aim to inform researchers, practitioners, and policymakers about current methodologies in online social networks.

articleTitle: Differentiation of Gut Microbiome Profiles Between Healthy and IBD Individuals Using 16S rRNA Sequencing and AI-Enhanced Analysis: Insights from Indian Cohorts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Gut microbiome plays a major role in human health, and its dysbiosis is associated with diseases i.e. inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This study investigates microbial differences between healthy individuals and IBD patients using 16S rRNA sequencing data from various BioProjects within the Indian Microbiome Database. Data from projects PRJNA397112, PRJNA422434, PRJNA515526, PRJNA559123, and PRJNA637482 were analyzed and taxonomic classification was performed using Qiita (Gonzalez et al. 2018) with the picking method of closed reference Operational Taxonomic Units (OTUs) through SortMeRNA (Kopylova et al. 2012). Additionally, 16S PIP (Miao et al. 2017) was used for pathogenic bacteria identification. To enhance the analysis, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based methods such as machine learning (ML) clustering and predictive modeling were employed to identify microbial patterns linked to health outcomes. Significant differences were observed in microbial diversity and composition between healthy and IBD samples, with an increase in pathogenic species in IBD patients. These findings, combined with AI analysis, provide insights into microbial markers of gut health and disease, offering potential applications in personalized medicine. This research underscores the potential of AI in identifying microbial markers for personalized treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of Coir Fibre Reinforced CaCl2 Crosslinked Starch-Chitosan Films
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this research work, calcium chloride crosslinked starch-chitosan blended films are reinforced with coir fibres. Such films are prepared for food packaging purposes, but the prepared films are highly hygroscopic, soluble and brittle in nature. Therefore, the films are reinforced with processed coir fibres. Processed coir fibres are treated with alkali medium. Fibres are then grinded and sieved for uniform and inclusive distribution of coir fibres in the blend or composite films. Inclusive distribution of coir fibres in the blends provides the flexibility to the films. Starch-chitosan blends are added with different ratios of grinded coir fibres (i.e. 1%, 2 %, 3 % and 4 %) to cast the films. Different properties of the prepared films are then observed, including the solubility along with swelling behaviour, by measuring the percent Total Soluble Matter (% TSM) and Percent Swelling Ratio (%SR). Finally, the prepared films are characterized by FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared), SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy) and TGA (Thermogravimetric Analysis).

articleTitle: Analyzing Traffic Behavior Across Hybrid Topologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper studies the performance of different hybrid network topologies on the parameter of average time and complexity. The physical and logical configuration of nodes in a network, which typically includes switches and routers to establish connections between end devices, is known as the topology. The study uses Cisco Packet Tracer to demonstrate the installation of many topologies, and it defines a metric based on the average time (Sec.) it takes a packet to travel from source to destination in various hybrid topologies. The outcome shows a hybrid network design that is effective in terms of complexity and packet delivery time to the end devices.

articleTitle: Non Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II) Modelling for AZ 31 Magnesium Alloy Composite
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The rolling process has proven to have a significant effect on the mechanical properties of metallic alloys especially in their strength. In the present research work, process parameters are optimized with a view to maximize hardness and tensile strength of experimental alloy by employing a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II) along with linear regression. The experimental data used in this predictive modeling was from fabricated magnesium AZ31 alloy composite produced through stir casting. As-cast alloys were homogenized at 500°C for 12 hours, followed by quenching in ice water. The as-quenched material was then hot rolled at different rolling temperatures, number of rolling passes, and initial stock thickness to study the process. The rolled materials were subjected to hardness and tensile strength measurements as dependent variables. Instead of training an artificial neural network to specify the objective function for NSGA-II, we created a mathematical model using regression analysis. This equation is used as the objective function for multi-objective optimization with NSGA-II. The NSGA-II predicted value for the maximum hardness of 107.41 VHN, is in close agreement with the obtained result of 106.6 VHN. Similarly, the maximum experimental tensile strength was 266.82 MPa whereas NSGA-II said that it will be approximately 253 MPa for this value. Under these circumstances, the predictive accuracy of NSGA-II was within 1-5% deviation from experimental results (i.e. good correspondence between the optimization strategy with experimental data).

articleTitle: Study of Artificial Intelligence Integrated AlGaN/GaN HEMT for Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) forms the core technology of these biosensors, offering distinctive advantages. HEMT-based biosensors have the capability to revolutionize the landscape of biomedical applications, particularly in the field of health monitoring and diagnostics. Leveraging the high electron mobility of HEMT, these biosensors exhibit enhanced sensitivity and precision in detecting biological markers. This emphasizes the potential impact of HEMT-based biosensors on advancing medical technology and underscores the need for further exploration and research in this promising domain. The present study aims to spark interest and engagement among researchers, inviting them to delve into the intricacies of HEMT-based biosensors and unlock their full potential for transformative applications in healthcare. It is studied that the ANN model can be used for device modeling and the neural network architecture can be used for the electrical characterization of HEMT.

articleTitle: Predicting K-Coverage in Wireless Multihop Networks with Boundary Effects Using Support Vector Regression: A Feature Sensitivity Analysis for Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Achieving the optimal network coverage is very essential for wireless multihop networks (WMNs), mainly in finite rectangular shape areas where the boundary effects (BEs) can distort the coverage metrics. Traditionally the simulations approach many times struggle very much to scale effectively as the network parameters grow increasingly complex. In this study, we used a Support Vector Regressor (SVR) model for prediction of the k-coverage probability in those scenarios where we see both with and without boundary effects. The model we used is trained using key features such as region dimensions, sensing ranges, and the density of node. Compared to other models like GRNN, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, the SVR is demonstrating superior performance. It is acquiring a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.1287 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> value of 0.7752 in the scenarios with boundary effects, and an RMSE of 0.1371 with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> value of 0.7610 in scenarios without them. Additionally, our feature sensitivity analysis gives valuable insights for the optimization of network. This makes the proposed framework not only scalable but also highly accurate for multiple applications, including urban sensor networks, disaster management, proving effective for applications and other critical infrastructure monitoring.

articleTitle: Nonlinear and Transient Analysis of Rectangular Fin Using MLPG Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study investigates the transient thermal behavior of an aluminum fin with a rectangular profile, considering both constant and temperature-dependent thermophysical properties, using the MLPG method. The MLPG approach is applied to conduct transient, linear, and nonlinear analyses, examining temperature variation along the fin's length and its thermal response over time. Moving Least Squares (MLS) approximants are utilized to approximate the unknown temperature function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T(x)$</tex> with Th(x), while essential boundary conditions are enforced via the penalty method. To address nonlinearity, an iterative predictor-corrector scheme is implemented. Unlike traditional models that neglect radiation effects, this study incorporates a convective-radiative environment, allowing for variations in the convective heat transfer coefficient. This approach enhances accuracy by providing results that closely resemble real-world conditions for fin surfaces. The reliability of the MLPG results is verified against numerical solutions, demonstrating their accuracy. The findings from this study offer valuable insights for designing fins in heat transfer applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of Era5 Reanalysis Datasets in Analysing Escs ‘Mocha’ Over the Bay of Bengal
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Extremely severe cyclonic storm (ESCS) 'Mocha' (2023), formed over the Bay of Bengal, has been analyzed using the ERA5 reanalysis datasets. The track, mean sea level pressure (MSLP) and maximum sustained wind (MSW) datasets were arranged from India meteorological department (IMD) observational datasets during the life cycle of ESCS 'Mocha'. The available IMD observations along Bay of Bengal (BoB), and the GPM rainfall observations are used to compare ERA5 reanalysis datasets. The parameters, viz. track, MSLP, MSW have been analyzed and compared with IMD observed datasets. It is seen that up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1 6 8} \mathbf{- h}$</tex> ERA5 reanalysis datasets of track and intensities have significantly improved during intense stages and the MSLP and MSW parameters analysis is reliable for up to 48 h. The ERA5 reanalysis datasets showed that the low value of MSLP in the range 961.1807-1004.849 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h P a}$</tex> along the track of the TC, MSW range of 21.88056183-64.25743103 kt. Intense rainfall along vertical direction of the quadrant of the system favored the rapid intensification of ESCS 'Mocha'. The MSW variation during the intense and system's landfall is also captured, and ERA5 agree with the observed data before ESCS stage and around the time of landfall.

articleTitle: Impact of Charging Infrastructure on Cost-Benefit Analysis of Electric Truck Fleets
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The electrification of freight transport represents a significant advancement in the optimization of a supply chain, particularly for rising environmental concerns and the need for cost-effective logistics solutions. This paper investigates the variation in charging infrastructure and charging cost sensitivity on the cost-benefit analysis of electric truck fleets, focusing on the total cost of ownership (TCO) and operational efficiency. By analyzing various charging techniques, including conductive charging and battery swapping, the study highlights the critical factors influencing the adoption of electric trucks at the fleet level. A comprehensive methodology is proposed, incorporating organizational requirements such as delivery schedules, payload, and driving behavior, alongside a Monte Carlo simulation to examine the reliability of the model under varying energy costs. The findings indicate that a rigorous and simplified cost-benefit analysis is essential for fleet managers to make informed decisions regarding the transition to electric trucks. This research contributes to the understanding of how strategic charging infrastructure can facilitate the adoption of ETs, ultimately leading to reduced emissions and enhanced operational efficiency in the freight transport sector.

articleTitle: VSG-DC-Based Grid Forming Inverter Control for Standalone Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The modern power system integrated with inverter-based resources (IBRs), such as solar and wind utilizes complex control strategies to preserve grid stability. This paper introduces an improved control structure of a gridforming inverter (GFMI) for a standalone (SA) microgrid system. The control strategy VSG-DC, emulates the inertial and damping characteristics and provides more virtual inertia to reduce the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). A common cascade current and voltage controller is used to maintain and stabilize the voltage and current levels, by which improving the dynamic frequency and voltage response. simulation performed in MATLAB/Simulink, the proposed control structure maintains the voltage and frequency according to grid standards during transient or specific load changes. the result shows that the control structure is successful in improving microgrid stability.

articleTitle: Optimizing Skin Cancer Detection: A Review of Hybrid Algorithms and Deep Learning Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Melanoma is a skin cancer, where early detection is important for successful treatment and survival. Recent advances in AI and machine learning have revolutionized the detection of melanoma by enabling more accurate and faster diagnosis through automated analysis of0020dermoscopic images. This paper explores a range of AI-based approaches, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and hybrid optimization algorithms, that have been developed to enhance the accuracy of melanoma classification. Various researcher's work has been reviewed and analyzed the strengths and limitations of each method which is shown in the paper. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art AI techniques in melanoma detection, focusing on their potential for improving early-stage diagnosis and contributing to more personalized patient care. By synthesizing findings from recent research, this review underscores the importance of continued innovation in AI-driven dermatological tools and the challenges that remain in making these technologies accessible and reliable in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Intelligent PDF Query System for Document Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A system based on artificial intelligence has been built to enable readers' interactions with PDF files through queries and responses in regular language. The system also utilizes advanced natural language processing techniques such as document-level contextualized representations to aid in effective document analysis so that users can locate information easily and precisely. The use of such document parsing and the vector storage mechanisms combing with the generative AI models and also the transformer based architecture offers an innovative approach to querying about the content within PDF documents overcoming the hurdles posed by conventional document retrieval systems. From the qualitative approach it is evident that the system improves the accuracy of responses and the level of user satisfaction significantly more than conventional methods of document retrieval. Such system efforts not only augment productivity with source of AI but the intelligent search options also help the general audience attract examine and consume complicated and heavy materials. Such improvements result in ease of information extraction and lessen the amount of attention that would have been used when dealing with large loads of information.

articleTitle: Enhanced Network Experimentation with Machine Learning-Driven Analysis of Beaulieu-Xie Fading and κ-μ Co-Channel Interference Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to study how to improve large-scale network experiments with machine learning (ML) algorithms, thereby studying the two typical fading models, Beaulieu-Xie model and k-µ co-channel interference. Methods like comparison between the conventional static configuration and ML-based adaptive algorithms were evaluated in terms of traditional performance metrics such as Bit Error Rate (BER), Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), throughput, and latency. Simulations employing the Beaulieu-Xie model accurately reproduced real-world fading environments in urban, suburban, and rural settings with more fidelity than conventional Rayleigh and Rician models. Our sensitivity analysis of k-µ interference parameters revealed their marked impact on SINR over ranges, thus underlining the importance for careful parameter identification in interference codelength results showed that ML-powered adaptive algorithms always did better than a static configuration in dynamic network situations. These transmission parameters were set in real-time based on online predictions, provided by dynamically adapting algorithms which improved performance network metrics over time. Moreover, sensitivity analysis results pertaining to study parameters further underscored potential improvements in the predictive power and confidence of network simulations via ML models. In summary, the integration of ML for network analysis has great potential in terms of accuracy adaptability and efficiency, so that ML is viewed as a corner stone to drive the design and operation features of wireless networks under complex an evolving environments.

articleTitle: EfficientNetB4 to EfficientNetB7 for Pepper Bell Plant Leaf Disease Detection: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of the economic system as well as in other countries. Leaf disease is a primary cause of disease and is one way to disease detection. Today, about 50 % of the damage to agriculture is happening only due to pests and leaf disease in plants. However, today we have been able to integrate ML and DL to enable early detection as well as categorization of leaf diseases, especially image-based detection of infected leaves. But despite the applications of these techniques, there is still a huge gap in plant disease detection. The main aim of the paper is to focus on various approaches of the ML and DL for plant disease detection, focusing on the advantages and the limitations of different models and the need for more extensive research in detecting leaf diseases as early as possible. This paper discusses Efficient Net, a very powerful and efficient model of the DL that gives good image classification performance in limited computational resources. In this paper, we present the comparison among various edition of Efficient Net on account of performance metrics such as accuracy, recall, F1-score and precision (from Net (B4 to B7)) in Google CoLab environment and discuss autonomous systems for future. The EfficientNetB7 model achieves a good accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 8. 1 2 \%}$</tex> among them.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Approach for Skin Cancer Detection and Classification Using Machine Learning and Deep Neural Network Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide are affected by skin cancer each year, making it a serious public health issue, caused by environmental and genetic factors. In the United States alone, 5.4 million [1, 2] people are affected by skin cancer and diagnosed every year. The worldwide figures are equally alarming [3, 4]. The deadliest type of skin cancer is melanoma. Early detection of skin cancer is a difficult and expensive process. Early diagnosis and detection are crucial because treatment at early stages can increase the chance of cure, recovery, and survival rates. Traditional approaches have long been plagued by issues including biased outcomes and imprecision due to the similarity of skin cancer lesions. Therefore, this study developed an approach that uses conventional camera images from a dataset to identify and classify skin abnormalities as benign or malignant. We have used techniques to develop a model that detects and classifies seven kinds of skin cancer specifically Vascular Lesions, Dermatofibroma, Basal Cell Carcinoma, Melanocytic Nevi, Melanoma, Benign Keratosis-Like Lesions, and Actinic Keratoses with an accuracy of 98.56% by a combination of deep neural network and machine learning algorithms with image processing technologies using a dataset from Kaggle. There are 10,015 dermatoscopic images in the dataset. Additionally, we have created a web application with an intuitive user interface that enable users to rapidly upload dermatoscopic images to identify and classify skin cancer.

articleTitle: RPL Protocol Performance Analysis Across Multiple IoT Topologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) network topology model is categorized as a Low-Power and Lossy Network (LLN). With the advent of IoT., the need for specialized protocols to address the unique challenges of LLNs, such as constrained nodes (e.g., battery-powered sensors), unreliable and dynamic wireless links, and scalability requirements for dense networks, became increasingly apparent. In 2012, the IETF ROLL (Routing Over Low Power and Lossy Networks) working group officially standardized RPL in RFC 6550, titled “RPL: IPv6 Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks.” RPL is designed to provide efficient routing solutions for LLNs across various application domains, including industrial automation, smart cities, and home automation. It employs objective functions, such as OF0 (Objective Function Zero) and MRHOF (Minimum Rank with Hysteresis Objective Function), to determine routes from source nodes to destination nodes based on metrics like ETX and energy. Previous studies on RPL were limited in their exploration of topological variations, which constrained the understanding of RPL's adaptability to different network structures. Additionally, earlier works lacked detailed analysis of hybrid topologies and did not adequately address the balance between energy consumption and routing efficiency. Performance assessments were frequently confined to a narrow set of metrics, neglecting crucial factors such as control traffic overhead, end-to-end delay and throughput, which are essential for practical IoT deployments. This study bridges these gaps by evaluating RPL under diverse topologies, proposing a novel hybrid topology, and incorporating a broader range of performance metrics for a holistic analysis. The proposed work introduces a hybrid star-tree topology, offering an innovative approach to optimize routing efficiency, by combining the hierarchical structure of the tree topology with the robustness of the star topology, the hybrid model achieves improved scalability, reduced control traffic overhead, and enhanced energy efficiency. This work also extends the evaluation of RPL to a variety of network configurations, providing comprehensive insights into its behavior under different conditions. Testing and evaluation were conducted using the Cooja simulator within the Contiki operating system and performance metrics achieved by wireshark network analyser. This paper explores the challenges encountered in IoT networks and investigates how different topologies effectively address and overcome these issues.

articleTitle: Optimization of Titanium Nitride and Zirconium Nitride Nanorods for Enhanced Solar Absorption in Plasmonic Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Photovoltaics (PV) has emerged as a key technology for directly converting solar energy into electricity, addressing the world's growing energy demands. Thin-film solar cells, despite their potential, face challenges in light absorption due to their limited thickness. Surface Plasmon (SP)mediated nanosystems, particularly nanorods, have shown significant promise in enhancing light absorption and trapping. This study focuses on the plasmonic properties of Titanium Nitride (TiN) and Zirconium Nitride (ZrN) nanorods as costeffective and efficient alternatives to noble metal gold (Au). TiN and ZrN nanorods exhibit strong plasmonic responses across the UV-IR spectrum, significant overlap with solar spectra, and superior properties such as low cost, thermal stability, and fabrication compatibility. The role of geometrical parameters including rod length, aspect ratio, and embedding medium is systematically analyzed for their impact on solar absorption. A comparative analysis with Au nanorods highlights the potential of TiN and ZrN as viable materials for photovoltaic applications. Numerically optimized nanorod designs are presented, showcasing their ability to enhance solar absorption. This study provides critical insights into the use of transition metal nitride nanorods for next-generation solar cells.

articleTitle: Text Categorization into Emotional States Using Enhanced Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The growing reliance on online platforms in our daily lives has made sentiment analysis a crucial area in pattern recognition and natural language processing (NLP). In this field, user feedback on various topics is evaluated and analyzed. One of the key challenges in modern NLP is identifying emotions within text. The proposed model aims to extract emotions from text using BERT, which is built by integrating transformers with bidirectional encoder representations. While sentiment analysis helps by identifying the polarity of messages, certain applications require emotion detection, as sentiment analysis alone may not capture the full range of emotions. To truly understand human psychology, it is essential to analyze data as quickly as it is generated. BERT is employed to train the model, and a comparative study showed that BERT outperforms other state-of-the-art models by better understanding word context. The findings of this study revealed that the BERT model achieved an impressive accuracy of 96%.

articleTitle: Vita Prediction: Leveraging Machine Learning for Life Preservation and Suicide Prevention
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A serious worldwide health concern is suicide, according to the World Health Organization (WHO) claiming that one suicide occurs every forty seconds, totaling nearly 800,000 deaths each year. This represents 1.4 of all fatalities globally, putting a significant financial strain on healthcare systems that spend $51 billion annually on them. For those who are having suicide thoughts or symptoms, prompt and efficient therapies are essential. In the healthcare sector, a wealth of data is accessible for use in machine learning (ML) models that can improve prognosis, diagnosis, and therapy, leading to better patient outcomes. In this study, we employed a variety of machine learning methods to predict suicide risk across different genders. Ten models were utilized, including k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN), Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and ensemble methods such as voting and bagging. The dataset was separated into two categories: education and social status. For Social Status, k-NN achieved 91.6% accuracy, but Bagging achieved 80.0% for Education Status. Our results emphasize the significance of variables in predicting the risk of suicide in different genders, including a history of attempted suicide, race, religion, suicidal thoughts, and the degree of clinical depression. These findings imply that machine learning models, particularly ensemble approaches, have great promise for enhancing the accuracy and predictive value of suicide risk assessments, which will lead to more successful interventions for those who are at-risk.

articleTitle: A Review on State of Charge (SoC) Estimation Methods of Li-Ion Batteries Used in Electrified Transportation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Nowadays the storage of energy become one of the core issues of today technology in the society of electric vehicle because electric vehicles are dominating the automobile market. In that scenario, Li-ion batteries have manifest potent as a storage choice as compare the other batteries parameters of operation. For the optimization in its execution, operation and increase the lifespan of the battery it is very necessary to check the battery's State of charge. Since the batteries have strong Time-Varying and Nonlinear characteristic during their operation because of this the real monitoring to the state of charge calculation is rigorous. Over the past years, many tried for the effectively analysis and comparisons to the State of charge SoC estimation methods for Li-ion battery. Although they rarely told on the SoC calculative method are depend on control-oriented criteria of a battery system. In this comprehensive reviews we have to focus on the battery (SoC) estimation technique applied on battery systems. In fact, the advancement on the battery management system is very foremost, when it comes to batteries. The Estimation of SoC is very complex for the monitor and the accurate idea of the state of charge is a difficult job in the battery

articleTitle: Computational Approaches Based Evolutionary Analysis to Identify the Genetic Variation Among Kelch 13 Gene Linked to Artemisinin Resistance in Plasmodium Falciparum
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Malaria is an ancient and common health manifestation in humans, worldwide. It poses a significant socioeconomic challenge in most developing countries, including India. Plasmodium species are the causative agents of malaria, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. falciparum and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. vivax being the most prevalent in the Southeast Asian subcontinent. Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ART) is the most advanced therapy to cure malaria, in most malaria-endemic regions. However, the emergence of ART-resistant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. falciparum isolates is becoming increasingly frequent globally. Recent research has identified mutations in the Kelch 13 (K 13) gene linked to resistance to ART and involved in delayed parasite clearance. This study is designed to explore the genetic diversity of the K13 gene in P. falciparum isolates worldwide. To this end, we retrieved 101 sequences of the K13 gene from NCBI GenBank and performed a comparative sequential analysis using computational approaches to identify the conservation and variabilities among the genes. Our findings suggest that the K13 gene of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. falciparum isolates have mutations and variability among their sequences. Additionally, phylogenetic analysis has been conducted to understand the genetic distance and variability among the K13 protein gene of P. falciparum.
