Accordingly, the current study aims to contribute in modern research strategies by exploring the K13 gene's pathways, which may help to inhibit the pathogenesis of ART-resistant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. falciparum strains and provide potential approaches for malaria control.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion Techniques using MSVD, WPD, PCA, and DWT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Image fusion is a technique used in image processing to create a more comprehensive representation by combining features and data from several images. Incorporating medical images from several imaging modalities, such as computed tomography (CT) scans, Positron Emission Tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), into a single set of data is what multi-modal medical image fusion is all about. Better visualization of anatomical structures and clinical conditions is the outcome of this integration, which increases diagnostic accuracy by using the strengths of each modality. In this paper, MRI, CT, and PET scans are used as experimental modalities. This review aims to compare various multi modal medical image approach based on Multi-resolution Singular Value Decomposition (MSVD), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), and Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD). This paper focuses on exploring latest conventional and non-conventional research being done using these domains. It also compares these methods based on various image quality parameters, and various quantitative checks. Based on this comparison, PCA shows the best results in the comparison as the overall visual and parametric quality of fusion results are better than compared methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent, and deadly cancer impacting women globally. Therefore, diagnosing it as soon as possible is crucial to improving patient health outcomes. Conventional diagnostic techniques mostly rely on the knowledge of radiologists and pathologists, which can make it difficult to identify cancer in their early stages and cause subtle symptoms to go unnoticed. By evaluating genetic, molecular, and clinical data to forecast how particular tumors could react to different treatments, artificial intelligence (AI) provides a promising answer and makes treatment methods more efficient. This study investigates the classification of breast cancers as benign or malignant using comparative analysis of machine learning (ML) based algorithms. Although the accuracy of all the classifiers was excellent, the ANN performed better with highest accuracy. The study highlights the capability of machine learning in enhancing the diagnosis of breast cancer and stresses the significance of carefully choosing classifiers based on the particular requirements of medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Return Loss and Insertion Loss of RF MEMS Shunt Switches With Innovative Hfo2 and Sio2 Materials for Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Aim: The main intention of the research is to compare the Return Loss (R.L) and Insertion Loss (I.L) of RF MEMS Switch with two different dielectric materials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{ (H f O}_{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex>) for Ka-Band Applications. Materials and Methods: The performance of R.L and I.L of RF MEMS Shunt Switches with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{HfO}_{2}(\mathrm{n}=44)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}(\mathrm{n}=44)$</tex> materials and the total group values <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n=88$</tex> were contrasted within the frequency range of up to 20 GHz. Sample calculations are done using the clinical tools, and the anticipated mean of Group 1 is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.20+/- 0.1$</tex>, Group 2 is 0.14, the value of alpha is 0.05, beta is 0.02 and g power value is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8 0} \%$</tex> respectively. Optimized dimensions for the RF MEMS switch performance were Length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=820 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex>, Width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=275 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex>, Beam Thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.8 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and Anchor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=1 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex> for the beam. Result: The return loss of the Silicon dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{SiO}_{2}\right)$</tex> dielectric material, at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{- 1 7. 2 7 1 2 ~ d B}$</tex>, is substantially lower than that of the Hafnium dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{HfO}_{2}\right)$</tex> dielectric material, which achieved a better return loss of −19.8584 dB. The attained insignificant value obtained in return loss is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0. 0 6 8}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}<0.05$</tex>) and the significance in insertion loss is 0.001 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}<0.05$</tex>). Conclusion: In conclusion, Hafnium dioxide (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H f O}_{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>) demonstrated superior performance with a return loss of 19.8584 dB compared to Silicon dioxide (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex>), indicating its suitability for Ka-band applications.

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using IoT and Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Modern detecting innovations, with a specific spotlight on manageability related issues, are impacting the fate of farming as the globe turns out to be more interconnected. The majority of emerging countries' economies is based on agriculture. The agricultural industry is one of the most vital industries, and crops are a necessity for providing food to people all over the world. The agricultural sector depends heavily on early disease detection and recognition. Crop fields are susceptible to the outbreak of plant diseases, either as a result of spreading viruses and fungus or unfavorable weather conditions, due to the lack of trained labor and enough supporting infrastructure. Owners of community gardens that want to use affordable strategies for sustainable agriculture through a sustainable. This model's suggestion offers a practical means of identifying various ailments in a range of plant species. Using the recently created dataset, an improved variant of the best deep learning (DL) model, has been suggested. In this unique circumstance, think about the possible utilization of the Social Internet of Things for detecting and interchanges, deep learning for the identification of plant sicknesses, and crowd sourcing for the collection and grouping of pictures, drawing in ranchers and local area garden proprietors and specialists. Across data fusion and deep learning, the created structure can take utility of the information gathered and estimate with a certain level of accuracy when a plant would (or would not) contract a disease. The user application must be able to interface with the virtualization layer and must be able to assess the health of the plants using images, data from garden sensors, and Internet access. Take some photos of the plant to assess its health and to provide feedback on any photos of the plant that haven't yet been tagged for the classifier data set. In addition to the user's smart phone's photo, the diagnosis of a crop disease necessitates collecting all the information from the sensors owned by other users and keeping track of various environmental conditions in the garden. It consists of three steps: tuning the sampling frequency, sending a request for cultivation-related sensors, and aggregating the sensor data. Additionally, it aids in forecasting plant diseases based on previously observed environmental variables. Additionally, the model demonstrates here the effectiveness and accuracy of the deep learning model used for plant identification, as well as the benefits of utilizing Social IoT engineering. The majority of the suggested DL frameworks in the literature have decent detection performance on their own datasets, but the performance is subpar on other datasets. In reality, once data are provided for a specific plant illness, the pattern for anticipating a upcoming infection of the plant is prepared.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Median Filter Hardware Chip for Image and Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The median filter is a valuable image processing tool that can be used in many applications to advance picture quality, and inferior noise, and acquire data ready for more analysis. The median filter, a non-linear image processing technique, has excessive application in many diverse fields because of its capacity to remove noise while preserving edges. The filter is significant for both simple and complex imageprocessing occupations since it is together easy to comprehend and fast to use. An active method to attain real-time performance is to devise a median filter on a FieldProgrammable Gate Array (FPGA) for image signal processing and machine vision applications. FPGAs are well-suited for photo filtering due to their capability to achieve parallel processing, which is one of their prominent advantages. The research article meets with the design and simulation of the average filter in HDL and synthesis on the FPGA for assessing the performance indices.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Detection Techniques for Defective Fasteners in Railway Track
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Railway track fasteners are critical components ensuring track stability and alignment. Defects in these fasteners, such as missing bolts or broken parts, can compromise railway safety, making early detection essential. This paper presents a comparative study of various image processing techniques to detect defects in railway fasteners by analyzing track images. Techniques evaluated include the variance Projection Method, wavelet Transform, thresholding, Morphological Operations and Connected Component Analysis. These techniques were assessed based on their detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to variations in lighting and angle. The results provide valuable insights into the most effective image processing techniques for fastener defect detection.

Author Keywords: Morphological Operations and Connected Component Analysis

articleTitle: Simplified Implementation of Histogram Equalization Using Approximation Offset
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified implementation of Histogram Equalization by adding offset values to the Histogram bins. The proposed approach helps to simplify the division/multiplication operations in Histogram Equalization calculation using shift operations. This approach is tested on different resolutions of gray images. The image quality comparison of this approach with conventional Histogram equalization shows that the proposed simplified implementation is effective for lower values of approximation offset.

articleTitle: Secure and Scalable Software-Defined Router for High-Throughput Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Scalable and secure Network programmability is the foundation of the cloud networking computing paradigm known as Software-Defined Router for High Throughput Networks. With a novel method of building and deploying router software, it therefore becomes one of the rapidly expanding new technologies in the internet world. The control plane and the forwarding routing data plane are two distinct modules (planes) that house the router's control and data forwarding functions. Special Software Defined Router switches on the data plane are made to either forward incoming packets to the controller or to their destination by encrypting the data according to the preconfigured routing table (flow table). Software-defined router switches' routing capability is controlled by a controller program on the control plane. Software Defined Router is a centralized network paradigm thanks to this distinctive program. The core feature of a software-defined router that can introduce attack vectors such as spoofing, denial service, man-in-the-middle, and other malicious attempts is routing. We will be examining the current state of secure routing in software in this paper. We will go over some potential security issues with secure and scalable routing, along with some current solutions. Ultimately, we will point out the drawbacks and provide alternative options.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Depression Detection and Their Comparison
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Depression is one of the most common mental health disorders that afflict people and productivity in society. This paper explores automatic depression detection using user-generated content on social media. Using machine learning and deep learning models, we thus design an efficient classifier system trained on a balanced set of depressive and non-depressive social media posts. We put together in our study techniques that have been learned from the SVM, random forest classifier, multinomial naïve Bayes, and long short-term memory network as well as the advanced methods of word embeddings such as Word2Vec and BERT. The models are classifying with accuracy ranging between 70% and 81.79%, offering scalability for the early stages of identification for depression. This result brings up the potential of AI to help advance diagnostics in mental health.

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy of Financial Fraud Detection in Mobile Transactions Using Xgboost Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: With the growth of modern technology, there has been a significant rise in fraud instances. Every year, billion dollars are disappear as an outcome of the growth on a global level. However, using preventive technologies seems to be the most effective approach for fraud detection. The authors focus on an advanced and innovative fraud detection solution using machine learning technique. Machine learning models such as Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, XGBoost Classifier and Random Forest are used in this paper to compare performances. The result indicates that XGBoost Classifier and Random Forest offers the best accuracy, with percentage around 99.9% and 99.14% respectively. These result shows that machine learning could greatly enhance the security for online transactions.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Severity of Parkinson's Disease Using Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A neurodegenerative disorder, Parkinson's disease worsens with time and significantly lowers the quality of life for people who have it. It largely affects how humans use their motor systems. Parkinson's disease symptoms encompass trembling stiffness, slowness of movement, and trouble walking. It also causes changes in thinking and behavior. In contemporary times, an extensive study in this area have yielded promising outcomes, surpassing conventional approaches., machine learning (ML) techniques offer good solutions in the medical industry by processing and analyzing data with high accuracy and a shorter processing time. This paper employs voice samples, a very accurate automated method utilizing machine learning was developed to identify Parkinson's illness. The author suggested leveraging a variety of machine learning classifiers Naïve Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), K-nearest neighbor (KNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) to balance a Parkinson's disease dataset combining an enhanced hybrid SMOTE methodology. The study highlighted the importance of dataset balance in medical classification. Different classifiers with and without SMOTE were assessed using performance metrics. With unbalanced data, the suggested method classified Parkinson's disease with 97% accuracy. The goal of this non-invasive method is to more accurately diagnose patients and identify their ailment at an affordable stage.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Transparent High Data-rate Antenna for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: For high data rate applications, a novel flexible circular-shaped miniaturized Ultrawideband (UWB) microstrip antenna is being developed. To accomplish miniaturization and UWB features, a modified ground plane and a circular-shaped patch have been used. The ranges of frequencies between 3.1 GHz and 12.54 GHz are obtained by the proposed antenna with maximum operating bandwidth of 9.44 GHz. This antenna's whole dimensions are 15 x 25 x 1 mm3. A wide range of performance parameters, including scattering features, surface current density, Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR), good impedance matching, Peak gain, and stable radiation pattern features for the operating band. Over the whole frequency range, the greatest gain of this antenna is about 3.2 dB. Additionally, this proposed antenna's transmission characteristics and more tolerable omnidirectional radiation patterns show that it is an ideal match for portable devices.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Ride Analysis for Grid Connected PVsystem
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper deals with a critical issue of voltage sag ride in grid PV systems. As renewable energy sources, particularly solar power, play an increasingly important role in the global energy landscape, the need for robust and reliable integration into existing grids becomes paramount. The objectives of this paper include modeling of two control techniques, SRF control strategy and DSOGI control strategy for grid connected PV system and compare them in terms of Total Harmonic Distortion percentage to address the voltage sag ride capability. Additionally, the paper will explore potential future scope.

articleTitle: Improved Regression Models for Solar Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The rising demand for renewable energy sources underscores the importance of efficient solar photovoltaic (PV) power plant operation. Accurate power output prediction plays a key role in optimizing energy management and ensuring the reliability of power systems. This research focuses on comparing the performance of regression models for predicting power output, in PV power plants. The models examined include Linear Regression, Poisson Regression, Lasso Regression, Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) regression, and Decision Tree Regression. The study utilizes a comprehensive dataset based on real world parameters for evaluating the efficacy of each regression model. Preprocessing steps, such as data cleaning and feature scaling, are implemented to ensure the robustness of the models. The data is partitioned into training sets and testing sets, and various performance metrics, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), R-squared (R2), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) are employed to estimate the accuracy and generalization capabilities of these models. The results obtained reveal nuanced insights into the highlights and challenges of each regression model, providing insights into their suitability in predicting power output in real-world PV power plant scenarios. The findings of this study contribute to the expanding field of research on solar energy prediction and offer valuable guidance for practitioners and researchers seeking optimal regression models for PV power plant power prediction

articleTitle: Generative AI Applications for Robust Shop Floor
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper examines the transformative potential of generative AI technology in the manufacturing environment. It is primarily focused on its application in shopfloor scenarios. In this paper, it is discussed how generative AI technology optimizes productive processes, ensures quality control, improves the efficiency of operations, and supports sustainability. The detailed application of generative AI to achieve shopfloor robustness has been presented here through case studies, simulations, and comparisons. The paper discusses the latest innovations, technical details, modeling and results that give the reader practical and theoretical advancements in the field.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Snow on Free Space Optical Communication Using Artificial Neural Networks for BER Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Free Space Optical (FSO) communication provides high bandwidth and secure data transmission, which may be of immense importance to substitute wired systems in zones that are not environmentally appropriate for fiber optics. But the performance of FSO is highly sensitive to climate conditions, especially snow precipitation, which has an adverse impact on the signal strength and disturbances in the link. This work aims to study the impact of snow on FSO communication by analyzing changes in BER across various snow visibility ranges. MATLAB simulations have been done to validate the impact of link distance and visibility in different snowy conditions, and BER is predicted with high accuracy using the ANN model. The ANN model in this study uses a feed-forward neural network with one hidden layer containing 10 neurons, and with link distance as the input, the model predicts BER across four different visibility levels as outputs. The mean squared error (MSE) of 0.0011537 is achieved by ANN, proving learning capability and ability of generalization without overfitting. Regression analysis provides additional evidence on the accuracy of the BER estimates for snowy FSO systems with correlation coefficients close to 1 in all data subsets.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Integration to Weak Grid Under Changing Operating Conditions of Solar and Wind
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The integration of hybrid renewable energy systems, particularly solar and wind, into power grids presents unique challenges and opportunities. This paper examines the operational dynamics, technical constraints, and optimization strategies for integrating hybrid energy systems into the grid under varying environmental, load, and grid strength conditions. By analyzing performance data and employing conventional control strategies, this study highlights methods to enhance grid stability, efficiency, and reliability. The findings contribute to the growing need for sustainable energy solutions in the face of increasing global energy demand and climate change.

articleTitle: Mutually Inhibiting Neural Networks with Second Order Neuronal Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose new mathematical second-order model to replicate neuronal activities of mutually inhabiting neural networks. The inclusion of second order differential equations captures complex neural behaviour more accurately instead of first order differential equations. A non-autonomous system of coupled second-order differential equation is proposed in this paper to govern the neuronal dynamics of a neural network of N neurons. Simulation results of single neuron and network of two neurons are shown graphically. The results provide insights into oscillatory patterns, stable states, and variation in the behaviour of neurons with respect to time. It is found that the neural system exhibits oscillatory response that can be used to govern various motion gaits and cyclic activities.

articleTitle: Two-Loop Controlled Buck Cuk Converter for Power Management in Dc Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A new power management approach is proposed, which uses a two-loop controlled Buck-Cuk converter to regulate the power from the input source. This method improves the conventional Buck-Cuk converter structure by adding an external voltage loop and an internal current loop. The inner current loop regulates the output current, while the outer voltage loop maintains the stability of the output voltage. The converter operates more efficiently transiently and steadily under a variety of input source conditions with the dual-loop control strategy. Simulation results are shown to be effective in terms of regulating input power and maintaining stable output voltage using the proposed method. For any combination of input and output variables, the discrete-time model of the system is used to manage source current and load power by optimizing load allocation. This research further uses RGA theory for improvement in the understanding of dynamics control loop and input-output decisions for efficient power management. The performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$48 ~\mathrm{V}, 177 ~\mathrm{W}$</tex> converter is evaluated against simulated results, including its steady-state and dynamic behavior. PSIM and MATLAB tools are used for the analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Code Modularity and Game Mechanics in Modern Game Development
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In the modern era of technologies, game development encounters substantial challenges in warranting scalability, code modularity, and maintainability because of several issues like tight coupling, code duplication, and inconsistent architectures. Due to these problems, it becomes difficult to integrate new features, increase error rates, and lengthen development cycles. Further, adaptability is limited due to the inflexible codebases, which makes scalability difficult. These issues are resolved by design pattern methodologies which provide structured and reusable solutions for code organization. Patterns like Singleton, Observer, and Factory facilitate developers to create modular and adaptable codebases. These patterns are very helpful in reducing errors, supporting system scalability, and eliminating the necessity for wide rewrites. In this paper, the practical applications of design pattern in game development have been investigated. These patterns improve code flexibility, maintainability, and scalability. By employing these techniques, developers can increase productivity, rationalize workflows, and create strong, game architectures. It has been observed that design patterns work as indispensible tools in dealing the growing complications of modern game development, permitting teams to meet the growing demands of players preserving high standards of quality and performance.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Indian Agriculture: A Direct Marketplace with AI-Based Crop and Disease Management Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the most vital sectors in India which faces daily challenges due to lack of market access, poor allocation of resources and insufficient provision of timely information or crop health. This paper proposes a solution through the help of an AI enhanced digital marketplace connecting farmers directly with consumers and buyers, thus ensuring fair trade and improved profit. The marketplace integrates advanced AI tools for crop recommendation and disease prediction for further assisting farmers. The disease prediction feature leverages ResNet-50, trained on a large dataset from Kaggle, to detect plant diseases and provide preventive measures. Through fine-tuning the model achieved an accuracy of 99.17%. Furthermore, the model could successfully predict diseases for unseen data as well. This overall approach aims to empower farmers in our country and provide a better livelihood to them.

articleTitle: A Computational Model of Voltage-Gated Sodium Ion Channel in Human Pulmonary Artery Smooth Muscle Cell
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) and hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction (HPV) are associated with the abnormal contraction of the pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell (PASMC). The cellular electrical activities due to the interaction of various ion channels are the most important determinants of the generation of the vascular tone. We have developed a mathematical model to elucidate the quantitative contribution of the voltage-gated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Na}^{+}$</tex> ion channel to PASMC membrane potential. The voltage-gated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{N a}^{+}$</tex> ion channel is built using the classical Hodgkin and Huxley formalism, with the model parameters estimated using experimental data from published literature. The ion channel is then incorporated into a previously published PASMC model to investigate its' modulating effects on the membrane potential. The voltagegated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Na}^{+}$</tex> ion channel conductance alters the resting membrane potential and consequent depolarizations in PASMC. This computational model supports the application of voltage-gated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Na}^{+}$</tex> ion channel inhibitors as new pharmacological targets for PH and HPV.

articleTitle: Self-Healing and Auto-Responsive Coordinated Control Systems: Leveraging AI and Real-Time Data for Optimal Asset Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In current times where automation, IoT, and AI are converging, the need for more intelligent, coordinated and resilient systems has become more important than ever. This paper introduces an innovative framework for self- healing, auto-responsive coordinated control systems that utilize real-time and historical data in combination with artificial intelligence to optimize asset management and operations. The proposed system discussed in this research paper consists of a multi-layered architecture, with an edge gate- way layer for localized data collection and instantaneous response, a supervisory layer for predictive analytics and coordinated control, and an enterprise AI layer that offers long-term tactical management. When technologies such as edge analytics, machine learning, and AI-driven decision- making are combined, the systems deploying them can self- diagnose and correct anomalies, predict failures efficiently, and optimize resources autonomously. This process reduces downtime and operational costs by a substantial margin while also increasing overall efficiency. There are several key features to factor in, such as, real- time data collection, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and centralized control policies which are deployed across operational layers in a coordinated manner.

articleTitle: Use of AI in Selected Financial Institutions: A Double-Edged Sword Effect
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In the contemporary era, our nation is progressing towards increased integration of advanced technologies, and these innovations are influencing various facets of our daily activities. Notably, artificial intelligence (AI) has become pervasive across all sectors and functions within organizations. Its impact is particularly evident in financial institutions where AI plays a crucial role in activities such as accounting transactions and fraud detection. The relationship between AI and the concept of a ‘Double Edged Sword’ is explored in this paper. The primary objective is toexamine and assess the utilization of AI in diverse financial institutions and its connection to the ‘Double Edged Sword’ phenomenon. Additionally, the paper delves into the pros and cons following the implementation of AI in the accounting industry, incorporating insights from selected Chartered Accountants regarding their perspectives on AI application.

articleTitle: State-of-Charge Estimation of Li-Ion Battery in Electric Vehicles Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Electric Vehicles are no longer the future; they are the present. To ensure proper management and efficient working of these new-age vehicles, the battery management system (BMS) for the Li-ion batteries is necessary. State of Charge (SOC) is a major component of BMS. This paper proposes a State of Charge Estimation using a Deep Neural Network (DNN) on a battery dataset. The training data consists of a series of charge and discharge cycles for a Panasonic 18650PF Li-Ion battery. The model is trained and validated using the Unified Driving Schedule (LA92) drive cycle and its accuracy is validated using a range of temperatures. The final model gives a mean absolute error (MAE) between 0.7 % and 1.1 %

articleTitle: Functional Brain Dynamics of Medial Anteroposterior Network for EEG-Based Depression Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is the major cause of the global burden of diseases. So, objective diagnosis via simple methods like electroencephalography (EEG) is essential for the development of efficient diagnostic solutions. We propose a novel functional brain network based on medial anteroposterior connectivity dynamics to distinguish between healthy and depressed controls. Pearson's correlation coefficient is used to capture connectivity dynamics using 2 minutes of the EEG record. The classification performance is obtained using a linear support vector machine with 10-fold cross-validation. The proposed FBN has achieved the highest accuracy, recall, and precision of 99.85%, 99.86%, and 99.82%, respectively. Notably, weak anterior-to-posterior links within depressed individuals were more significant in the beta band. This implies a lack of stable thinking ability, which might play a key role in complex thought processes like emotional intelligence and meditation, necessary for sound mental health.

articleTitle: Analysis of Component Reliability Through Fussellvesely Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In a functional system, certain components within a system have more importance in terms of its reliability than others as well. Compared to a component that is in sequence with the remaining components of the system and initially represents a cut set of orders, a component that is part of a cut set of higher orders is frequently more essential. A component's reliability can be increased by using a more reliable component, adding redundant components, lowering the operational and environmental demands on the component, or improving the component's accessibility. In this manuscript, we consider <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i=1,2,3, \ldots, n$</tex>, and, take into consideration a structure consisting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2-o u t-o f-3$</tex> independent components with component reliabilities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_{i}(t)$</tex>. The FussellVesely approach analyses the structural reliability with respect to a given system function, which is represented by the symbol <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h\{p(t)\}$</tex> which measures component significance, to rank the components in ascending or descending order of importance. The measurements may also be applied to the categorization of significance, which divides the components into two or more categories based on predetermined standards. The component with the lowest level of reliability is the most important for the desired functioning system since the significance of measurement can be used to identify weak points and parts that need to be updated to increase the system's reliability.

articleTitle: Unveiling Deception: Machine Learning Strategies for Fake News Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this study, a system is developed to detect and classify fake news whose proliferation significantly threatens information integrity, public trust, and societal stability. This study presents a comprehensive list of ML strategies for fake news detection and classification. It investigates the efficiency of different ML algorithms such as Logistic regression, Decision tree, and Random Forest, in distinguishing between factual and deceptive content. The findings reveal that some algorithms demonstrate high accuracy and reliability in identifying fake news articles. Moreover, a novel approach is proposed for the manual testing of news articles thus enabling real-time verification of information authenticity.

articleTitle: Predicting the Students' Performance Using Machine Learning Tools- A Survey on Jalandhar City (Punjab)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Among SDGs17 goals, to achieve the 4th goal Quality Education, educational institutions play very important role. In today's competition world, it is very crucial task for any institution/organization to forecast the student's performance. With the advancement of technology, like Artificial intelligence and its subset like machine learning (ML) and data mining (DL) help the researchers to identify the unknown patterns in large amount of already existing data. The hidden/unknown patterns or data may be helpful for analysis and making prediction. Educational data mining (EDM) is the latest technique used by various researchers to predict the students' performance as various factors affecting on their performance. Student performance prediction helps students as well as teachers to keep the track of students' progress. We have collected the data from students studying in various Government and Private Schools of Jalandhar city. Total sample size is 463. Study hours, ICI facilities, student's interest, teaching facilities available in school and family background are the major components that affecting the students' performance. To study the factor affecting the students' performance ANOVA is applied to test the hypothesis and all the experiments were held in Python language.

articleTitle: Firefly Optimized Battery Energy Storage for Microgrid Operation Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Energy storage system is a key technology to accommodate the uncertainties of renewable sources. Microgrids play a significant role in meeting the world's rising energy demand and offer an efficient way to incorporate small-scale distributed generation sources (DGs) into the electricity grid. And to ensure reliable, resilient, and cost effective operation of micro grids, the connected Battery Energy Storage (BES) must be optimally sized. This research proposes the cost-based formulation for evaluating the optimum size of the BES in the Microgrid operations management. In this work, Bio inspired Firefly Algorithm (FFA) is proposed for the development of corrective strategies and least-cost dispatches. Four different operating scenarios of varying BES sizes are being tested and the outcomes are compared to the recently developed Spider Monkey Optimization (SMO) to validate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm. The performance of the approach is evaluated with a grid-connected IEEE33 bus test system to reveal the superiority of the proposed FFA over the SMO algorithm in finding optimal battery size.

articleTitle: Advanced Temperature & Ratio Control System For Small Scale Dyeing Industries
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Many small-scale chemical dying industries use manual labour to measure, evaluate and mix the desired chemical solvents and solutes in the required ratio. They often consider that using some automatic big machines for mixing of these chemicals may not be economical for them. Hence, they train their labour through instructions in their presence and make them follow it accordingly. This may not be accurate since this is based on manual or mind calculations and may have some error. They usually keep time as a parameter for their measurement. For some textile dyes hot water should be used as a solvent. For this water from the tank is heated with a small boiler. For this also time is used as a parameter of measurement. They usually allow the water to be heated in the boiler for specific amount of time so as to reach the desired temperature. After this process, the hot water from the boiler is directly used as solvent. This water is not checked whether it has reached the desired specific temperature. There may be chances of error associated with this as the whole process is done on the basis of approximation. This small error done during the mixing of the solvent with chemicals may affect the quality of the fabric. This may lead to even major issues such as fabric damage or skin infection to the consumers who use the fabric. This affects the reputation of the company and spoil their business. To reduce these kinds of errors and to improve the quality of the product an automatic ratio calculator is used here. This ratio calculator gives the exact amount of solvent to be used for the given amount of textile chemical. Also, a temperature specifier is used so as to display the temperature of the water in the boiler. This will help them to achieve the desired range of temperature for the required amount of product. This will improve the fabric quality. Improved fabric quality will increase customer satisfaction. This paper introduces a novel Temperature Specifier and Ratio Calculator developed to address challenges in achieving precise temperature control and accurate mixing ratios in chemical processes. The calculator utilizes predictive algorithms and a user-friendly interface to guide operators in optimizing conditions for various chemical reactions. Through extensive testing and validation, this tool has demonstrated its potential to revolutionize industrial safety across multiple processes, enhancing product quality, efficiency, and domains.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Inference Model for Alzheimer's Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a neurological disorder which can lead to memory loss. So early detection of this disease is very important. So, we have developed a model for early detection of Alzheimer's disease, which looks into several factors causing AD and decides which factor is the major reason behind AD. The Fuzzy Techniques such as Fuzzy TOPSIS method, Fuzzy AHP method and Fuzzy Synthetic evaluation is used. On comparing all the three methods Fuzzy TOPSIS and synthetic evaluation has givien same results for the good numbers of criterion. This research contributes to early diagnosis of AD helping the improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Intricacy of CNN and RL with Substantiation of CNN Model in Simulated Self-Driving Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has emerged as a technological revolution that has incarnated advancements across various domains. Incorporating machine learning in technology opens a new paradigm for technology innovation. The convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) paradigm of machine learning technique has a remarkable capacity to automatically extract significant characteristics from inputs. The key attributes of CNN make it indispensable in disciplines like pattern recognition and computer vision. This paper explores the architecture and functioning of CNNs, emphasizing their unique attributes which contribute to their superior performance in complex tasks. Building on the foundation of CNNs, the study also explores Reinforcement Learning (RL), a technique that empowers agents to learn optimal policies through interaction with an environment. By implementing the CNN technique, this paper investigates the potential of the CNN model in autonomous systems, particularly in self-driving vehicles. A CNN model is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness of these techniques. The results highlight the model's ability and the improvements to accurately classify and predict outcomes, underscoring the practical applicability of CNNs in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of Portable Electric Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The paper focuses on the construction and analysis of a foldable, portable, and lightweight electric bicycle that is continually integrated with solar panels and uses solar energy to charge the battery. This makes the vehicle essential for efficient municipal transit. Current research on urban air pollution shows the growth in carbon emissions and the need to solve environmental issues. The goal is to create a user-friendly, zero- emission foldable electric bicycle that is also economically viable, as well as to analyze the folding frame and chassis. The design is intended to be appropriate for both genders. Using an electric solar power system on this bike helps to manage pollution and reduce carbon footprints. The paper includes crucial themes such as market research, literature review, design, analysis, observation, and correction. The integration of solar panels to replace the battery as a secondary source is consistent with the larger objective of creating an ecologically friendly electric bicycle that requires less maintenance and produces less noise. This novel solution satisfies the need for urban bicycles by providing small and convenient transportation that allows people to move freely. The installation of a pivot in the frame to produce a foldable design is an effective technique to improve urban mobility and sustainability.

articleTitle: A Study on Challenges and Solutions on Power Optimization Techniques in 5G Nr Communication for the Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The emergence of 5G NR communication has also contributed to the challenges for the power consumption and the various work towards the solution for this problem. Although the 3GPP Rel 16 and further has addressed this problem as well, but the efforts are also being made to handle the same from the device side. In this direction various know techniques are DRX, WUS, EPI, history based SSB synchronization and traffic classification models etc. The final goal is to save the power without affecting the quality of service. The modern techniques of artificial intelligence and machine learning can also contribute to this goal very effectively. We explore various issues and their corresponding solution in this survey work and lastly discussing the open area and future scope.

articleTitle: Link Facilitation Model for Better Connectivity in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this paper, Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANET) has been adopted for analysing connectivity among vehicular nodes in a mobile environment. It is assumed that the nodes travel through a multi lane and unidirectional highway path through multiple entry points without any crossing with each other. The nodes are distributed along the whole area by Poisson Distribution process. These mobile nodes communicate with each other through a specified distance and transmission range. However, since transmission is prone to interference thus a probabilistic approach has been proposed in this paper for better inter-communication between the nodes. Also, it is very essential that the knowledge of highway distribution should be pre-known before travel. This should be done in order to prevent and minimize any kind of collision or other tragic situations. Probability Density Function (PDF) has been used to extensively distribute the nodes based on better and reliable communication links through wireless channels. Since in this paper a multi lane headway path has been considered therefore the distribution of travelling nodes in each considered segment should be such that it prevents any collision or accident and also provide better interconnectivity and reliable link duration. The main contribution of this paper is to enhance the link duration performance between inter-nodal mobile communication while the vehicles move towards their exit points. The simulation results have shown 15% better improvement in keeping long link duration and better Poisson-based nodal distribution. The proposed approach will definitely help in better travel experience and road safety. The extensive simulations performed have successfully validated and confirmed the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Advanced Predictive Modeling Techniques for Early Detection of Diabetes Mellitus
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study aims to develop advanced predictive machine learning modeling techniques for early detection for diabetes mellitus with enhanced accuracy. Early diagnosis and treatment of diabetes can reduce the risk of complications and serious diseases, demonstrating the potential of machine learning in diagnosis. The proposed Approach develops a model integrating four advanced machine learning models -KNN, Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost (XGB) Classifiers. Datasets have been evaluated for high-performance metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 Score. The Pima Indian Diabetes Dataset has been used for testing and evaluating the proposed model that included 768 Native American women (500 without diabetes, 268 with diabetes), was used. This data includes eight characteristics: pregnancy, diabetes, stress, triceps, insulin, BMI, genetics, and age. These results show that the XGB is the best model for diabetes mellitus diagnosis, followed by random forest models, demonstrating the ability of machine learning to improve the accuracy and performance of diabetes mellitus testing.

articleTitle: Implementation of Flyback DC-DC Converter Topology for DC Power Supply Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The power DC-DC converter has been fascinated as a very significant part in the form of different topologies in numerous applications. It is pertaining to the regulation, successful change, and conditioning of electrical power between its obtainable input form and the necessary electrical output form. They are divided into two types: non-isolated and isolated. Multi-phasing is done to allow for high power processing by splitting the overall load current into many phases and distribute the processed power equally among the phases and reduces ripple through load current by interleaving. The state-space averaging method is applied here to analyze a multiphase interleaved DC/DC converter. Consequently, small-signal and steady-state models of a multiphase converter are obtained. A two-phase interleaved flyback converter has been analyzed. The mathematical derivations are shown and simulations are carried out using MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the performance of the proposed multiphase (up to four phases) flyback dc-dc converter.

articleTitle: Exploring Anticancer Potential of Some Commonly Used Pteris Plants Through Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Objective: The study aimed to explore the anti-cancer potential of commonly utilized Pteris species (family-Pteridaceae) through network pharmacology and molecular docking studies. Methods: Various databases like ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, PubMed etc. were used for identification of common Pteris plants and their already reported bioactive constituents via GC-MS analysis. Swiss ADME software were used to screen the bioactive constituents present in the plants. Network pharmacology which includes common target prediction between drug and disease, PPI network formation, GO and KEGG analysis and lastly formation of constituent-target-pathway network was done. Molecular docking studies were performed to calculate the binding affinity with obtained targets to validate the predicted outcome. Result: A total of 353 active targets of P. cretica, P. excelsa, and P. vitatta and 19224 targets of skin cancer (SC) were identified via different databases. 340 mutual targets of active compounds and SC were used to form PPI network. Compound target network analysis revealed presence of 340 nodes and 4050 edges. KEGG and GO analysis revealed presence of 92 pathways, 128 biological processes, 17 cellular components and 31 molecular functions. IL-17 signaling pathway & TNF signalling pathway were the main links in the amelioration of skin cancer with Pteris species. Results obtained from molecular docking showed that bioactive components of P. cretica, P. excelsa, and P. vitatta had good binding with the target proteins i.e. IL-6, TNF, JUN and PTGS2. Conclusion: the study concluded with a potential probability of having anticancer potential in Pteris plants and opening a new research area for exploration of Pteris species in-vitro and in vivo for their use as an anticancer molecule.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Loss Functions in BigGAN for Medical Image Synthesis: A Case Study on Brain MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Acquiring high-quality medical images such as MRI scans is essential for diagnostics and treatment planning but remains challenging due to high costs, health risks, and data scarcity. To address this, we propose the use of Generative Ad-versarial Networks (GANs) to synthesize MRI images, alleviating the limitations of medical data availability. This paper presents a fine-tuned BigGAN model, optimized to generate MRI scans representing different stages of Alzheimer's disease. We explore the impact of various loss functions, including Adversarial, Hinge, and Mean Squared Error (MSE) Loss, on model performance. While the outputs showcase the potential of GAN s to generate high-quality medical images, challenges such as mode collapse and overfitting remain. The synthesized images offer significant promise for enhancing AI model training and medical research, particularly in scenarios where acquiring real medical images is difficult.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Study of Thunderstorms Over Uttar Pradesh, India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Thunderstorms (TS) are primarily short-lived mesoscale phenomena which is occurred with rainfall and lightning. It is an extremely damaging weather event that has an impact on all the sectors of the society such as human lives, floods that affect the agriculture sectors and infrastructure. This work is attempted to study of the TS occurrence over Uttar Pradesh, which is a very fertile and the most populated parts state of India. Using ERA5 reanalysis data, stability indices (KI, TTI, HI, CAPE, CIN) were used to determine precursors and prediction lead times. To identify the thunderstorms occurrence day rainfall data from (IMD) were used. To fix location K-Index (KI) from ERA5 and daily gridded maximum rainfall from IMD were used. To evaluate the predictability and precursors four cases of thunderstorms cases were examined. This finding demonstrated that thunderstorm location and intensity could be predicted with a few hours lead time, which would be helpful for real-time thunderstorm prediction. This is a prelude study for the understanding and identification of the thunderstorms in Uttar Pradesh.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Studies on the Effect of White Rice Husk Ash and Alccofine on the Strength of Concrete Cubes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Concrete structures are often exposed to forces from loads and environmental factors, leading to changes in their condition over time. It is important to monitor these structures to detect any issues, allowing for simpler and more cost-effective evaluation and repairs. To achieve this monitoring, there are tools available for assessing the condition of concrete elements. Nondestructive testing (NDT) methods have emerged as an approach for monitoring and visual inspection of concrete structures. This study has examined the use of white rice husk ash (WRHA) & alccofine in concrete and analyzed their effects on its properties. has selected four replacement levels of WRHA, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%, for fine aggregate, along with a 15% replacement of alccofine for cement. It observed an enhancement in the strength and durability of concrete after adding alccofine. with the addition of 15% of alccofine as replacement of cement, gives more improvement in concrete strength. According to the equation representing the relationship between compressive strength and the rebound hammer test. These quantities can be considered of good quality when the value of the coefficient of determination R2 > 0.7. This means that all the equations found can be used to describe the relationships between the relative parameters with good accuracy. This is clear from the high value of R2.

articleTitle: Analysis of Extreme Rainfall Trends Over 75 Locations (District Wise) of Uttar Pradesh, India using Daily Gridded Rainfall Data (1973-2023)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study analyzes rainfall patterns in selected districts of Uttar Pradesh, India, using daily gridded rainfall data from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the period 1973 to 2023. Trends in severe daily rainfall occurrences were identified using the Mann-Kendall (MK) test. The inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation method was used to visualise the geographical distribution of rainfall patterns. The results demonstrate that while monsoon patterns were declining in certain areas, they were increasing in others. The study sheds light on how Uttar Pradesh's agricultural planning and water resource management are affected by rainfall unpredictability.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Haemorrhage Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Recently, deep learning calculations have been used for picture identification and detection, with excellent results in the pharmaceutical industry, such as clinical image research and analysis. For patients with brain haemorrhages, prompt diagnosis of the drain type and application of the appropriate therapy is essential to enhancing their chances of long-term survival. It has been shown that machine learning models are incredibly useful for assisting doctors in the management of intracranial haemorrhages. We evaluate a few 2-dimensional (2D) convolutional neural organisations (CNNs) in this research. In order to identify cerebral haemorrhage in computed tomography (CT) images, this research will use convolutional neural networks (CNN) and deep learning computations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Drug Sensitivity Prediction in Cancer Cell Lines Using Multi-Omics Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study integrates diverse omics datasets, including proteomic, transcriptomic, and miRNA profiles from cancer cell lines, with drug sensitivity (AUC) data for 285 drugs. We identified that combining proteomics, transcriptomics, and miRNA data provides the best predictive model. Using the k-means clustering algorithm, we grouped cell lines based on these multi-omics data. Subsequently, drug sensitivity (AUC) for 285 drugs was predicted using a 5-fold cross-validation Random Forest Classifier for each cluster separately. The resulting five clusters were thoroughly evaluated, leading to drug suggestions with over 75% accuracy for further investigation. Our findings indicate that high-quality clusters derived from the optimal set of multi-omics features improve the performance of the Random Forest algorithm in predicting drug responses, compared to low-quality clusters obtained from a random set of features. We also compared drug similarities within clusters 0, 1, and 2, analyzing the results with a heatmap. Our findings show improved similarity between drugs in cluster 0 compared to clusters 1 and 2, based on hydrogen bond donor, hydrogen bond acceptor, and molecular weight properties. This aligns with the silhouette scores, which is higher for cluster 0 compared to clusters 1 and 2. These results suggest that, in high-quality clusters, drugs with high prediction accuracy tend to exhibit greater similarity in their properties compared to those in low-quality clusters. This supports a cluster-centric approach in precision oncology, as high-quality clusters, indicated by high silhouette scores, lead to more accurate and consistent drug response predictions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Oxide Confined VCSEL for Optical Interconnects at 1550 nm Wavelength
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The structure and performance of oxide confined Vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) for optical interconnects at 1550 nm was presented. As the optical guiding medium is optimized for shorter wavelengths, the researchers have restricted it to wavelength between 850 nm to 1310 nm to obtain stable temperature performance with optimum output power. But the advancement in optical fibers which are optimized for longer wavelength requirements to fulfil the future demand of high bandwidth capacity at longer distances possible at 1550 nm. We employed VCSEL at longer wavelength i.e. 1550 nm operating at single mode. The impact of oxide aperture diameter and Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) on total power emitted is determined by varying the oxide aperture diameter between 1 to 5 μm, The static characteristics of VCSEL like output light, photon density, current, voltage, gain and loss in cavity are studied in detail. The important parameters of VCSEL analysed mathematically are power emitted by VCSEL and number of photons emitted and compared with simulated results. The number of photons generated analytically are 3.02×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> photons per second whereas simulated results show 2.3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> photons per second. It is also observed that VCSEL emits total power of 5.8 × 10^-6 mW at oxide aperture diameter of 2 μm and operating at 300 K temperature.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multimodal Biometric Authentication Using Bi-LSTM Deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In recent years, biometric systems have gained immense popularity for secure authentication and identification due to their ability to capture unique physiological and behavioral traits. However, unimodal biometric systems often face challenges such as noise, intra-class variations, and spoofing attacks. To address these limitations, multi-modal biometric systems have emerged as a robust solution by combining multiple biometric traits, such as fingerprints, face, iris, and voice, which enhances accuracy and reliability. This paper presents a novel multi-model biometric system leveraging deep learning (DL) techniques. To classify data from various biometric sources, the suggested framework uses Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). When developing the multi-model biometrics system (Face-Iris-Palm print), they consulted the MULB database. The experimental outcome was determined by several performance matrices, including,, , and. The results establish that the recommended model achieved the best results in terms of multi-model biometric system performance, with an of 98.91%, of 98.11%, of 97.07<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and of 98.89%.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Systems of Renewable Energy: A Concise Overview of its Uses and Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The primary aim of this work is to analyze the current advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies and tools pertaining to the management, maintenance, and regulation of renewable energy systems (RES), with a particular focus on solar power systems. The findings would enable researchers to advance existing technology and potentially use established and effective methods in the development of AI-driven renewable energy systems, particularly in solar energy. We analysed a range of peerreviewed scientific publications to assess the status and progress of AI techniques in the domain of renewable energy systems, specifically in solar energy systems. The Artificial Neural Network (ANN), the Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS), and the genetic algorithm (GA) are some of the most common and welltested theoretical and experimental AI methods. The results of this review indicate the extensive use of these methodologies in various forms of solar forecasting. Nonetheless, ANN emerged as the superior strategy among these options. Artificial neural networks have distinct advantages over their competitors, including reduced computation time, enhanced accuracy, and superior generalisation capabilities compared to alternative modeling techniques. This would result in cost efficiency compared to alternative modeling methodologies.

articleTitle: LoRa Based Low-Cost Real-Time Air Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A low-cost indoor and outdoor air quality monitoring system is implemented using LoRa technology to measure parameters like temperature, humidity, PM 2.5 and Formalde-hyde in real-time. The system is designed in a star topology where the sensor nodes are connected to a routing node which in turn is connected to a gateway node. The sensor nodes are implemented using low-cost off-the-shelf sensors interfaced with a microcontroller unit. A LoRa hat module SX1268 is used to transmit the sensor data to the routing node, which is again implemented using a low-cost microprocessor (like Raspberry Pi). A time-series database and a server is implemented on the gateway device for data storage, visualization and processing. Using LoRa technology, the transmission range achieved is around 3 kms with zero packet loss and 4 kms with 20% packet loss.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements on Intelligent Multi-focus Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Recently deep learning approaches are more popular for multi-focus image fusion. In this review article, non-conventional multi focus image fusion techniques recently published were analyzed in detail and current advances as well as impending trends were discussed. The push for ever increasing image quality in multi focus imaging has raised the desire for non-conventional techniques as possible substitutes to conventional techniques. In this review, we systematically examine state of the art research in deep learning models, hybrid methodologies combining multiple transform domains, and adaptive thresholding strategies. We conducted a comparison evaluation of visual data against different strategies utilizing the complementary fusion capabilities of each. In addition, quantitative metrics of these values were used to objectively measure the performance of each strategy. In the paper, important ongoing developments, such as integration of deep learning techniques with transformer methods and adaptive fusion filters to enhance image details while avoiding artefacts are stressed. The implications of this review for academics include a comparison of the progress in the field to date and the potential of non classical techniques to realize higher accuracy and reliability in image fusion. The results suggest that further investigation of more sophisticated hybrid and adaptive techniques will yield improved diagnostic quality in a clinical setting.

articleTitle: Inception V3 and GRU Fusion: A Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Deepfake Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: As there is a huge rise in the prevalence of Deepfake videos continuously from last few years due to the power being leveraged by some powerful deep learning techniques. Therefore, there is a huge promptness in the global community to develop certain effective methods for Deepfake video detection methods. In this work, the combination of Inception V3 and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) for spatial feature extraction and temporal dependencies across video frames respectively. Several performance parameters has been used for the quantitative analysis of the models. The result shows that there is notable increase in the accuracy and other parameters which can actually provide a solution to the problem of Deepfake detection.

articleTitle: Exploring the Knowledge Structure of the Information Domain (2014-2023) in Five Selected Journals Using Topic Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study explores the knowledge structure of the information domain by analyzing the publication records (n=3.,383) of five selected journals obtained from Scopus. BERTopic modeling was used to identify key topics from the abstracts of the publications and their evolution over time. The results reveal popular topics and emerging trends in the field. Most of the topics are aligned with the integration of technology., consumer behavior., AI., organizational innovation., privacy., governance., and social media. Although this study is based on limited journals., it opens room for future research to explore a broader range of journals with more data. The results can be useful for researchers in the field.

articleTitle: A Review of Digital Forensics Techniques and Emerging Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A scientific approach to investigating digital attacks and crimes is employed in digital forensics, commonly referred to as computer forensics. The field of digital forensics requires a lot of work. Investigators begin by searching electronic devices for evidence and storing the information on a safe drive. The information is then examined and recorded. Next, they hand over the digital evidence to the police, who can use it to solve crimes or use it as evidence in court to establish the guilt of the accused. Analysing every device that can store digital data is now included in the enlarged definition of digital forensics, which was first coined as a synonym for computer forensics. The foundation of behavioral forensics can be regarded as machine learning, which has strong ties to artificial intelligence. For the purpose of stopping any unlawful activity, software-based pattern recognition can handle enormous volumes of data using machine learning. Using networked software and tools for remote analysis is one way to employ machine learning.

articleTitle: Applications of Gaming in Security Division for Training and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study investigates the applications of game development in security division training and simulation, examining its theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and empirical evidence. The adoption of game-based training methods in security contexts has gained prominence, driven by advancements in technology and the need for immersive and effective learning experiences. Drawing upon a multidisciplinary approach, this research synthesizes literature from educational psychology, instructional design, human-computer interaction, and organizational psychology to provide a comprehensive overview of the topic. Through case studies, surveys, interviews, and experimental studies, the study assesses the impact of game development on learning outcomes, skill acquisition, and performance improvement among security personnel.
