The findings highlight the benefits of game-based training, including enhanced engagement, retention, and transfer of knowledge, while also addressing concerns such as cost, technological complexity, and resistance to change.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Cyber Defense: A Study of Modern Security Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: AI is transforming cyber security with its creative methods for identifying, thwarting, and lessening cyberthreats. The growing complexity of attacks is too much for traditional security measures to handle. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in contemporary cybersecurity is examined in this article, with particular attention paid to AI-powered solutions for threat identification, automated incident response, and intrusion detection systems (IDS). Combining machine learning and deep learning techniques improves artificial intelligence's ability to evaluate massive datasets, spot irregularities, and predict possible security breaches. This study also discusses important issues including data privacy, explainability of AI-driven solutions, and adversarial attacks on AI systems. Problems The report highlights how AI has the potential to transform cybersecurity and how further developments are necessary to address emerging security vulnerabilities. To summarise, AI is an effective tool for protecting intelligent systems, but continual innovation is required to guarantee reliable protection against emerging threats.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Models on MRI-Based Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Brain tumors are one of the deadliest medical disorders that can be treated if identified early. Manually interpreting MRI scans is mostly challenging, time-consuming, and error prone. Deep learning techniques have emerged to automatically detect and classify brain tumors with high accuracy, mitigating existing limitations. This work mainly focuses on EfficientN etBO, an advanced transfer learning model, simultaneously examining various deep learning techniques for the identification of brain tumors. The model was trained on a publicly available MRI dataset comprising images of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors, as well as healthy brain tissues. This work demonstrates that EfficientNetB0 outperforms traditional CNN architectures in accuracy and efficiency. Using techniques like data augmentation, cross-validation with 10 folds, and optimizations of learning rates, we achieved an impressive 97.5% validation accuracy to address issues like overfitting and improving convergence. The results show that EfficientNetB0 is a more scalable solution to identify brain tumors in comparison to other traditional and makes it better for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Unified Safety Assurance Approach for Modern Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Modern railway systems are becoming more software concentrated than ever before. Majority of safety and security related functions are monitored and controlled using software. Traditionally safety assurance methodology was focused on hardware with more emphasis on operational aspects than its development process. With the introduction of software in many railway systems especially signalling system, the traditional safety assurance approach needs to be revisited. There are fundamental differences between hardware and software with respect to the failure mechanism and behaviors. The software safety assurance becomes a vital issue, as it has been found that the majority of system accidents happen just because of the failure of safety functions monitored and controlled through Software. Safety analysis of software-based safety functions must be revisited before putting them into operation. Software safety is still an open challenge to transportation industries including Railways. This paper attempts to explain the key issues and challenges towards safety assurance of software intensive railway systems. Paper proposed a unified safety assurance approach for modern railway systems. It utilizes the operational profile of the systems for safety analysis and accordingly combines traditional safety analysis techniques with operational profile. Paper also proposed a further layer of safety justification through the introduction of software safety case.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Time Equivalent SVPWM Approach for Nine Phase Inverter System at Load
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this study, a time equivalent SVPWM technique for nine step VSI at inductive load is analyzed through simulation in a MATLAB/SIMULINK system. 9-phase voltage source inverters power 9-phase machine drives, which are used in high-power applications. To get the desired effect, the output of the inverter must be controlled. Although a variety of control systems have been discussed in the past, time equivalent SVPWM exhibits the least amount of absolute harmonic distortion when compared to other PWM techniques. After outlining the complete method for the time equivalent SVPWM scheme for 9-phases, the author uses two indices-fundamental peak value and total harmonic distortion to evaluate the VSI's performance. Simulation in the MATLAB environment is used to validate the results.

articleTitle: Clustering Targets in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Huge numbers of sensors that monitor the environment, aggregate data, and communicate it to a server for post-processing are commonly seen in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). WSNs are thought to be extremely adaptable ad-hoc networks; nevertheless, because of the scale of the deployment and related quality issues like scalability, resource management, and dependability, network management has proven to be a significant difficulty. It is thought that topology management is a workable solution to these problems. In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), clustering is thought to be the most wellknown topology management technique. It involves grouping and managing nodes to carry out different distributed activities including resource management. While increasing energy consumption is the main benefit of clustering approaches, there are several quality-driven objectives that can be met as well.

articleTitle: Finding the Shortest Distance Between Villages Located in Mountainous Terrain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This research endeavors to develop a comprehensive approach for determining the shortest path between the central locations of two villages situated within a mountainous region. The proposed methodology integrates advanced geospatial data, elevation models, and sophisticated pathfinding algorithms to navigate the intricacies of the mountainous terrain. Elevation profiles and geographic features are meticulously analyzed to identify optimal routes that minimize travel distances while accounting for the challenging landscape. The research outcome aims to provide not only an efficient pathfinding algorithm but also a holistic solution that integrates seamlessly with the specific challenges presented by mountainous regions. Ultimately, the findings of this research contribute to the advancement of transportation planning in mountainous areas, facilitating improved connectivity between villages, promoting sustainable development, and addressing the unique geographical constraints for such regions.

articleTitle: Dissolved Gas Analysis of Mineral Oil - Based ZrO2 Nanofluids Under Thermal Fault
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Most commonly insulating fluid utilized for transferring heat as well as electrical insulation in oiled-immersed transformers is mineral oil. Nevertheless, because to their superior dielectric and thermal properties, oil-based nanofluids are gaining popularity in research fields. These nanofluids would be subjected to electrical and thermal strains when used in real transformers. The objective of this paper is to examine the structure of dissolved gas formation in nanofluids during accelerating aging condition and evaluate the suitability of conventional Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) methods in the event that oil-based nanofluids are utilized in transformers. Oil-based nanofluid samples have been prepared in a laboratory setting utilizing a magnetic stirrer and ultrasonic homogenizer and then subjected to simulated for accelerating aging in the laboratory using microprocessor-controlled oven. Utilizing zirconium oxide nanoparticles, nanofluids containing concentrations of 0.01 g/L, 0.02 g/L, and 0.03 g/L were created. The simulated faults produced gasses into the oil, which were analyzed and contrasted with pure aged MO. The results indicate that the quantity of gasses generated is influenced by the presence and concentration of nanoparticles. Therefore, this work is essential to ensure that conventional DGA methods may be used in transformers that use oil-based nanofluids to identify different kinds of faults. When conventional DGA methods are applied on nanofluids samples, S2 (0.01%+MO), S4 (0.03<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>+MO) and S4 (0.03%+MO), then we investigate partial discharge, thermal fault, corona type fault and carbonization of paper.

articleTitle: Lossless Compression Based Optimization of DICOM Images Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Modern medical knowledge and practice rely heavily on medical imaging. DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine) is the standard format used to store medical images after a patient's scan. However, DICOM files are large and require specialized viewers, which are not always available. This can be problematic when doctors need to share images quickly for treatment discussions. To address this, medical images can be converted to more accessible formats like JPG or PNG, which require less storage and are easily shareable and readable on various devices like smartphones, tablets, and computers. This paper explores the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms to optimize the compression ratio of medical images while maintaining high quality. Specifically, the Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN) is trained to predict the ideal compression ratio for CT scan images. Experimental results show that RBFNN outperforms other methods, achieving a 94 % recognition rate in the first scenario. In a second scenario, it achieves a 90 % accuracy with the optimal compression deviation set to 1, highlighting the effectiveness of ML for medical image compression.

articleTitle: Design of a 72.1% Tuning Range, Low Power Differential Ring VCO in 0.18 μM CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This manuscript presents the architecture of a four-stage differential ring voltage-controlled oscillator (DRVCO) with a unique delay stage. The proposed VCO employed a skewed delay technique to get an extensive tuning range, low power dissipation, and phase noise. The proposed VCO circuit results are obtained using the Mentor Graphics tool in 0.18 μm CMOS technology with a supply voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(V_{d d}\right)$</tex> of 1.8 V. The proposed VCO achieved a tuning range of 72.13% when the control signal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(V_{c}\right)$</tex> modulated between 0.1 V to 1 V, with frequency of 1.778 GHz to 3.784 GHz and a power dissipation range of 10.13 mW to 3.86 mW. The proposed VCO exhibits a −101.2 dBc/Hz phase noise. The VCO, as published, exhibits characteristics such as low power, an extensive frequency range, and minimal phase noise. Consequently, it is well-suited for use in low-power applications.

articleTitle: Water Quality Prediction Using Machine Learning A Case Study of Saryu River
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The work's primary goal to use machine leaning techniques to measure the quality of the water. The quality of a specific body of a water is assessed using a numerical expression called the water quality index (WQI). Water quality metrics were employed in this experiment to asses the total water quality in relation to the WQI. Physical parameters were as follows TDS (total dissolve solid), Ph Chemical Parameters Cl, CO3, Ca, K, Mg, Na, SiO2, HCO3. Biological Parameter DO (dissolve Oxygen). These parameters serve as a feature vector that depicts the quality of the water. In this research three kinds of classification algorithms, namely MLP (Multilayer perceptron), RNN (recurrent neural network, GNN (Graph neural network) were employed to predict the water quality class. The actual dataset used for the experiments included information from multiple locations in Ayodhya that was produced using randomly selected parameters. Three different classifier type were evaluated, and it was discovered that the RNN performs somewhat better than the others. The investigation demonstrate that machine learning methods are capable of accurately predicting the water quality index

articleTitle: Predictive Trend Analysis in Fashion: Leveraging Machine Learning for Forecasting Styles and Consumer Preferences
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: One of the areas through which the fashion industry should establish itself at the top line is by the incorporation of new techniques resulting from the fast shift in customer preferences and the emergence of trends. This paper takes an approach in the use of ML techniques in predictive trend analysis for estimating consumer preferences and the emerging or evolving trends in the fashion industry. Using machine learning algorithms that scan through vast databases of previous fashion trends, social media activities, retail sales, and the worldwide cultural transitions, we analyze the occurring underlying trends and predict further trends much more accurately. In this attempt to predict style preferences and assess customer feedback, we look into several machine learning (ML) algorithms, including decision trees, neural networks, and natural language processing (NLP) tools. The current study also discusses the idea of incorporating machine learning with traditional forecasting techniques that may allow it to generate useful insights for marketers, retailers, and designers. It also claims that this will result in better decision-making, tighter control over inventories, and a closer match between consumer want and supply from the fashion industry. Better Matches between Consumers and Fashion Industry Benefits of Growth and Innovation leading to this part are also expected by the Study.

articleTitle: MPPT Based DC-DC Converter for Fast Charging in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper reviews a bidirectional DC-DC converter for an electric vehicle charger. The bidirectional property of this converter allows us to find an ameliorate way to channel the reverse flow of energy. This converter is an updated version of the previous one which gives more optimized results, mainly including escalated switching speed and fast charging. For high power density along with a long battery life, the hybrid energy storage system or (HESS), in which the hybridization of battery along with ultracapacitor is used, meets the requirements of the EV, and the model predictive control concept is utilized. We have used the fuzzy logic approach which provides flexibility for interpretation. It may mimic human deductive reasoning, which is the method through which individuals draw inferences according to what they know. Experimental results are generated to verify the performance of the proposed ‘H-Bridge’ controlled transformerless buck-boost, DC-DC Converter using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: Deciphering Amino Acid Features in NRPS Sequences of Biosurfactant- Producing Bacteria: A Framework for Machine Learning Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Biosurfactant (BS) are recognized for their extensive exploration and various applications in fields of health, agriculture, pharmaceutical, food, and personal care products highlight. BS are safe, efficient, and ecofriendly substitutes for synthetic surfactants, which is the driving force behind this research in advancing creative and sustainable solutions for several industries. Research studies indicated a strong correlation between NRPS gene clusters and BS production, it has also been proven from earlier research studies that NRPS has a modular organization that can be further divided into domains representing the enzymatic units for catalyzing the synthesis of nonribosomal peptides. Furthermore, the applicability of NRPS sequences for biosurfactant production was assessed across 21 NRPS sequences within prokaryotes. Various insilico computational tools have been used to detect NRPS sequences, conserved domains, amino acid conservation and conserved motifs for BS production.

articleTitle: Smart Farming System Using IoT, Embedded Electronics, and Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The emerging field of “smart farming” leverages information and communication technologies through advanced machinery, equipment, and sensor networks to enhance farm management. The integration of innovative technologies such as cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to drive agricultural development, although it also presents significant challenges that disrupt conventional farming methods. This paper explores the tools and technologies used in wireless sensor networks within IoT -based agriculture, along with the anticipated obstacles in merging these technologies with traditional agricultural practices. Moreover, this technological approach offers benefits to farmers throughout the entire agricultural cycle, from planting to harvesting, with further potential in packaging and logistics.

Author Keywords: Internet of Things based agricultural system

articleTitle: Designing Procedure to Develop a Helical Antenna for SAW Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) devices are used in wireless communication systems, especially in RFID Tags sensors filters as they are more sensitive SAW Devices. In order to make a helical antenna viable, it is necessary to design a range of applications including SAW devices and space born devices because this type of radio frequency radiator offers circular polarization associated with robust gain over very wide bandwidth in quite short dimensions. In this work, we presented a design procedure to develop helical antenna for SAW devices starting from given initial parameters such as: radius, number of turns, spacing and ground plane dimension. This essentially allows us to calculate return loss (S11) and gain for different values of parameters. Simulated data is also demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality-Powered Footwear Customization Hub: Enhancing the Shopping Journey
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A Shoe Marketplace (Try & Buy featured) is an innovative venture that aims to transform the landscape of online shoe shopping by integrating cutting-edge augmented reality (AR) technology. This research paper focused on the design, development, and implementation of the platform, addressing the inherent challenges faced by customers in traditional online shoe shopping. The project's primary objectives include introducing an immersive AR-based virtual try-on experience, enhancing user engagement, offering a diverse collection of shoes, ensuring secure transactions, and providing user-friendly search options. The paper uses an extensive methodology that blends experimental and descriptive research techniques. The research holds great importance as it has the ability to transform the online shoe retail sector by providing users with an enhanced, interactive, and secure shopping experience. The study's findings establish new benchmarks for the effectiveness of augmented reality (AR) applications in the online retail space and further the ongoing progress of virtual try-on technologies.

articleTitle: Jellyfish Optimization for Enhanced Maximum Power Point Tracking of Solar PV Systems Under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this study, the Jellyfish Optimization (JFO) meta-heuristic method is utilized to track the Maximum Power from the solar PV system operating under different shading conditions. Jellyfish Optimization (JFO) is a relatively new algorithm inspired by the food-search behavior of jellyfish, which effectively balances exploration and exploitation by simulating active and passive movements in ocean currents. This study demonstrates that JFO tracks the MPP more accurately than conventional MPPT controllers such as PID, FA, PSO, and P&O. The proposed approach greatly improves tracking efficiency and optimizes the energy extraction from photovoltaic arrays. Results show that JFO achieves a high tracking efficiency of over 99.9%, with a short convergence time of less than 0.012 seconds, a maximum power output of 636.8 watts under PSC, and minimal power oscillations. To validate its superior performance, JFO was compared with other existing methods through simulations conducted in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Control Techniques for Path Control of Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper presents mobile robot navigating towards a target while subjected to random disturbance in the path of mobile robot. Various control strategies, including Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control, Adaptive Control, Sliding Mode Control (SMC) and Model Predictive Control (MPC) were implemented and evaluated. The results indicate significant differences in performance, with each control strategy exhibiting unique strengths and weaknesses in handling disturbances. This study contributes to the understanding of robotic control systems in uncertain environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reliability Allocation for a Component in Standby Redundancy System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this manuscript, we have analyze a dependable system, and a consideration has also been given to allocating the reliability of components, and any system with standby redundancy will be more reliable, while the modeling active redundancy is simpler. The reliability study of the standby arrangement is somewhat more dependable than that of the parallel operating units. However, to begin operating the next unit in the event that the first fails failure recognition is typically necessary for standby systems. This indicates that any numbers of units are operating and that the typical failure interval is significantly longer. More than one unit are operating while the functional equipment reliability is not working properly, as it is in this instance. Therefore, the life of a system can be efficiently increased by allocating redundant components, evaluating its dependability, collapse amount, and collapse density operates at different times, as well as the known associated risk measure and inverted risk rate commands, and talking about the components and eliminations according to a general distribution of life.

articleTitle: Targeting and Automating Recoveries from Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities Using Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: There is a growing need to develop more robust, automated methods to check for vulnerabilities in code and software. Large language models, due to their ability to engage with a wide variety of scenarios, provide a personalized framework for users to safeguard their devices. This paper focuses on using a LLaMa3.2 3B model as its base, pretrained on the DiverseVul dataset consisting of vulnerable code snippets in programming languages such as C, C++, and Python. Using QLoRa for PEFT-based fine-tuning, the model achieved an Accuracy of 93.75%, outperforming other models. The CLI application provides a seamless user experience by pinpointing user directories for vulnerability scanning and classification. Despite its promising results, the study identifies limitations, including challenges with obfuscated code, computational resource constraints, and generalization issues. This research contributes to advancing real-time detection capabilities and scalable solutions for cybersecurity.

articleTitle: From Rumors to Reality: Exploring Machine Learning Approaches for Fake News Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Before the Internet was even a known thing, there was malicious deception and fake news. The widespread acceptance of fake news on social media can be attributed to the proliferation of misleading articles and their ability to captivate readers. Both social media platforms and news publishers often share such misleading content to expand their audience and gain market traction. Clickbait increases the spirit of inquiry among people. It's a matter of notable concern to look upon it as it damages the national and social inbuilt powerhouse. The dissemination of false news within the modern digital environment affects more than just one particular demographic. In social media, material that is both credible and implausible is mixed together, confusing what is real. In other words, the truth won't likely be classified. There has previously been much investigation before it was discovered. This paper conducts a comprehensive examination of the existing literature pertaining to the identification of fake news. It also delves into the exploration of prominent conventional machine learning models with the aim of constructing a classification algorithm. This algorithm is designed to discern between authentic and counterfeit news by utilizing various tools including Python, PorterStemmer, Fuzzy-logic, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques for textual analysis. According to the experimental findings, the Passive Aggressive Classifier has a 96% accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Smart Home Energy Management System: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of home energy management system (HEMS) and their contribution to enhancing energy efficiency in smart homes. It discusses demand response (DR) programs, which helps reduce energy uses by scheduling appliance operations based on factors like cost, environmental impact, and user comfort. the review highlights the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and heuristic optimization techniques in controlling and scheduling household energy loads. The paper also explores the integration of green energy sources and energy reservoir's in building micro grids to enhance energy efficiency. Additionally, it addresses the broader challenges with respect to advanced energy solutions in smart city initiatives, focusing on the need for resilience, adaptability, and improve decision making through advance data acquisition and communication technologies. overall, the paper underscores the important of energy management system in reducing electricity consumption and enhancing sustainability in smart home and grids.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Based Pattern Reconfigurable Microstrip Antennas: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this research paper, a detailed study of the design and applications of various pattern reconfigurable Microstrip antennas (PRMAs) based on different methods, especially metamaterial structures and electronic switches like PIN diodes, varactor diodes and mechanical switches like actuators has been studied on the basis of their merits and demerits. The work done by researchers and scientists in the past based on directional and omnidirectional pattern reconfigurable mechanisms is reviewed here with various examples. In this paper, we review different metamaterial structures for PRMA and implementation techniques for implementing them.

articleTitle: Extraction and Study of Defatted Pearl Millet Flour for its Physicochemical and Functional Properties
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Extraction and study of defatted pearl millet flour (DPMF) were undertaken to evaluate its physicochemical and functional properties. This study sought to improve its storage stability while retaining its nutritional qualities. These findings suggest that DPMF can be utilized in bakery products, weaning foods, and other low-fat food formulations, offering both nutritional and functional advantages.

articleTitle: Leveraging Emoticon Scores for Improved Sentiment Detection in Social Media Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Social media has become a common platform for people to share their thoughts about products and individuals. There are different types of social media to analyzing specific sentiments in natural language is a challenging undertaking how to express their views, thoughts and emotions. These days, emoticons are commonly utilized and have become essential to written communication. The review frames a deliberate system for sentiment analysis, including information assortment, cleaning, order, and model preparation and testing. It utilizes freely accessible film audit datasets to analyse the circulation of positive and negative criticism across various dataset sizes. The centre of the exploration is information analysis, assessing different classifiers including Naïve Bayes, Multinomial Naïve Bayes, Logistic Regression, Bernoulli Naïve Bayes, Direct SVM/Straight SVC, and Nu SVM/Nu SVC. Calculated the emoticon on different datasets relapse arises as a hearty and powerful classifier across dataset sizes logistic regression techniques gives the best result in comparison to other techniques, while Direct SVM/Straight SVC shows a reliable expansion in exactness rates as dataset size develops.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Autonomous Mobile Robot for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) are machines that can move independently to achieve their goals. They belong to the category of autonomous guided vehicles (AGVs). The proposed work investigates an AMR specifically designed for various industrial applications and operates autonomously. It operates on tracks or predefined pathways under the regular supervision of an operator, making it one type of AMR. The developed AMRs are fitted with sensors and cameras. If they come across an unexpected hindrance object while navigating through their environments, they would use a navigation technique called collision avoidance to perform actions like slow down, stop, or change their path around the hindrance and then resume their task. Currently, industries frequently use autonomous mobile robots to support inventory locating, picking, and moving, freeing up employees to focus on critical tasks like customer service.

articleTitle: 5G Radio Access Network Management- The Potential of Smart Contract Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: There is a growing mobile traffic projected to reach 5016 Exabyte/month by 2030, which explains the rising need for mobile base stations, hence the need for expanding the 5G networks. However, the configuration management of Radio Access Networks (RAN) presents substantial challenges, aggravated by manual processes and multi-stakeholder involvement, which complicates efficient collaboration. This paper advocates for the integration of the smart contract Blockchain technology into network management systems (NMS) to streamline configuration processes, enhance automation, and improve stakeholder transparency and trust. Smart contracts themselves are a code consisting of executed agreements, and therefore NMS can leverage its self-executing features to reduce potential problems while easing network changes along with maintaining immutable transaction records. The system is equipped with some pre-defined concepts and sequences of the events that allow the network elements to change status in accordance with the rules, scenarios, and logic embedded in smart contracts. The framework is aimed at improving effectiveness and efficiency in operating and collaborating within the scope of multiple complex network environments.

articleTitle: An ISM Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Breast Cancer Detection Using Confocal Microwaves Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: We present the most efficient image reconstruction method for breast cancer detection by using ISM band antenna using confocal microwaves imaging technique. ISM band signal is transmitted and receives backscattered signal from tumor by single microstrip patch antenna and reconstructed the image which represent the exact location of tumor in breast by using confocal microwaves imaging technique. The antenna resonates at 2.45 GHz with small bandwidth with low gain 1.9 dBi and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>-52 below -10 dB represent better radiation and deep penetration of waves from antenna inside the breast to identified the tumor and create a high-resolution image with exact location of tumor by confocal microwaves imaging method with low noise and suppressing the clutter with minimum SAR value.

Author Keywords: 3D-Breast model with tumor simulated in CST
Confocal Microwaves Imaging technique in MATLAB

articleTitle: An Equivalent Single Spiking Neuron Model of the Working Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a biologically plausible computational working memory (WM) model implemented using a spiking neuron model representing a predictable WM mechanism in a single neuron. Empirical evidence from single neuron animal brain recordings has shown that WM is processed in a neuron model by encoding associations and exhibiting persistent activity. The model implemented using an adaptive exponential integrate and fire neuron model, was able to replicate the dynamics observed in WM tasks, such as the Delayed Match to Sample (DMS) paradigm. The input patterns were encoded as numbers, representing the spike train patterns in the neurons, and the frequencies of transient discharges of corresponding neurons were the outputs. By simulating this task, the model demonstrated how cognitive processes such as encoding, maintaining, and retrieving information during the delay period could be performed by single neurons. The model was examined by modifying parameters including the duration of delay, number of inputs, and retrieval probe count attributed to cognitive load. Through this soft computing-based approach, our simulations allow us to elaborate equivalents in emergent dynamics, including persistent neuronal activity during the delay period.

articleTitle: A Taxonomy of DDoS Attacks on Cloud Computing Environment and Approaches to Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Modern businesses and Governments rely on Cloud Computing for offering Internet based services to their users as the cloud offers a Reliable and Secure hosting platform complying with the CIA triad of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) is a threat to the availability pillar of the CIA triad which floods the infrastructure, network resources or websites with high volume of artificial traffic to overwhelm the Cloud resources preventing legitimate users from accessing the services leading to loss of revenue and reputation. As the attacks are distributed, the incoming flood of traffic appears to originate from numerous sources, making it practically impossible to deter the attacks by conventional methods of blocking source IPs. This article provides an overview of the impact and Taxonomy of DDoS attacks in the Cloud computing environment followed by various approaches for the identification of DDoS attacks and devising effective countermeasures for proactive mitigation of application layer attacks to secure the production environment from potential loss incurred towards service downtime.

articleTitle: Modularity and Lazy Evaluation in Nixos: A Functional Approach to Operating System Configuration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In contrast to traditional imperative models the Linux distribution known as NixOS takes a purely functional declarative approach to system configuration. Two important facets of NixOS that are essential to its distinctive design are examined in this work: modularity and lazy evaluation. Users can create reusable and adaptable modules by utilizing NixOS's modularity which enables a clear division of responsibilities in system configuration. A defining characteristic of functional programming is lazy evaluation which guarantees that only essential components are assessed resulting in effective resource management. These features provide substantial advantages in practical situations especially with regard to the systems repeatability dependability and maintainability. NixOS offers a deterministic and atomic method of software deployment for sectors that depend on massive dispersed systems like cloud infrastructure and continuous integration sectors. Reproducibility across environments is ensured allowing for reliable rollback procedures and downtime-free upgrades. This work also shows via real-world experience how the NixOS module system abstracts complicated configuration sets facilitating quick setups and streamlining the administration of complex systems. NixOS is very configurable for both development and production environments because configurations are arranged into readily accessible modules that allow users to quickly adapt to a variety of environments without requiring manual intervention. Through real-world use cases this work explores the architectural ideas underlying NixOS's modular and lazy configuration model. It also looks at how current industry issues like scalable infrastructure management continuous deployment pipelines and repeatable builds can be addressed by NixOS's functional design.

articleTitle: Predicting Optimal TAF Doses for Severe Renal Impaired Patients: An Integrated Pharmacokinetic and ML Based Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is a component of the HIV infection prevention regimen, particularly in high-risk populations like men having sex with men (MSM) and trans women. This paper reports the initiation of an evaluation of the pharmacological properties of PrEP with a particular focus on tenofovir alafenamide (T AF) and its use among patients with impaired renal function. TAF has greatly improved the safety profile of PrEP, primarily through the reduction of renal toxicity relative to older agents. Nevertheless, reduced renal clearance in the case of patients with impaired renal function presents significant concerns in the determination of an optimal dosing regimen ensuring the safety and efficacy of PrEP. While significant advances have been made in the understanding of the properties of TAF, there are still gaps to be addressed, particularly in the understanding of the pharmacodynamics when given in combination with P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inducers in this population of patients. For these reasons, this paper highlights the need to conduct further studies optimizing TAF dosing regimens among patients with impaired renal function and calls for the inclusion of state-of-the-art pharmacokinetic modeling together with machine learning to further clarify TAF's interaction with P-gp inducers to ensure safe and effective therapeutic outcome.

articleTitle: PV Energy Conversion System with Grid Interface Using Variable Step Size Modified Decorrelated NLMS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Adaptive system identification (ASI) topics have long been of interest to the research and commercial sectors. As another of the conventional techniques for ASI, Least mean square (NLMS) accuracy is unpredictable in the low signal-to-noise ratio domain. The proposed research uses an adaptive nonlinear control approach to develop an adaptable grid-interfaced solar energy generation system with three phases and two stages. The suggested system can extract peak power from a solar array and also perform reactive power compensation, harmonic current removal, grid current and adaptable dc-link supply managing regulation. With the aid of an adaptive observer, the harmonic information from the contaminated load current is accurately measured. The updating laws for an adaptive observer are derived in terms of a strictly positive real function. To reduce the switching losses in the voltage source converters (VSC) and prevent their tripping in distribution grids with sensitivity issues, the point of common coupling voltage has been employed to adaptively customize the DC-link voltage. To enhance system reaction in dynamic circumstances, a feed-forward loop for PV contribution is incorporated. Test and simulation results show how well the PV system performs with the aforementioned features. Better dynamic and steady-state performances are seen when using the suggested nonlinear adaptive estimation based control strategy. It is discovered that the total harmonic aberrations in grid currents fall well within the parameters of the IEEE-519 specification.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Patient Care: AI-Driven Wearable Technology for Continuous Remote Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) refers to the ability of healthcare professionals to be able to monitor the well-being of their patients remotely without having to keep them under continuous in-person observation. Wearable devices that are integrated with Artificial Intelligence are a blessing in disguise when it comes to remote health monitoring. PPG sensors, ECG sensors, accelerometers, pulse oximeter and EDA sensor are some of these AI integrated wearable devices used for continuous remote health monitoring which are discussed in this article. We delved into their specific working mechanism, how the data is collected, stored and transferred and how the use of artificial intelligence algorithms come into all of this. These devices have applications in fields such as cloud computing and big data analytics for health management which are discussed along with key innovations. Certain issues such as data accuracy, data privacy and regulations are also addressed along with future directions which can be pursued that may have the potential to revolutionize the field of remote health monitoring even more than its present advancements. The objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the role of AI-integrated wearable devices in remote patient monitoring (RPM), their mechanism of operation and significance in modern health care.

articleTitle: Advances in Crop Yield Prediction: From Traditional to Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Crop yield prediction moves from basic crop growth models to the newest, complex machine learning approaches as the world battles pressing issues such as food insecurity, climate change, and population growth. The paper critically reviews the transition from empirical models to advanced ML techniques such as Random Forest, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) that have been found to handle multi-scale relationships between environmental factors, soil properties, and crop management much better. The integration of remote sensing technologies with satellite-based indices of NDVI and EVI coupled with IoT-driven real-time data streams has helped further improve prediction accuracy at various scales. However, meanwhile, important challenges persist: data quality and availability, and the necessity for regional-specific models are relevant, given climatic variability as well as soil differences. Regional-specific models that consider climatic variability and differences in soil can be applied by using robust normalization techniques that blend well with a more comprehensive data processing strategy. This is something that unlocks the gates to real-time prediction capabilities and on-the-fly model optimization. Besides, as AI-driven models advance, these will aid in generating highly accurate yields that farmers can base decisions on them and also enable formulating effective agricultural strategies at national and global levels. This will potentially contribute greatly to improved agriculture throughout the world through improved yield forecasting. More accurate yield forecasts will become a strong management tool for dealing with the stresses mounting on the global food systems.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Privacy-Preserving Techniques in Health Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The utilization of computerized apparatus in healthcare has commenced an immense amount of data related to health and medical industry from multiple locations, like Electronic Health Records (EHRs), wearable devices, Health Related applications. The data can help change healthcare by enabling tailored treatment, elevating patient's reports, fostering medical studies and facilitating public health endeavours. The exclusive characteristic of this data breaches critical privacy concerns. If health data is abused it can give rise to grave predicaments such as identity theft or identity pilfering, disparity among patients by doctors or individuals and erosion of trust in healthcare systems. However, the vulnerable essence of such type of data has serious concerns that must be addressed. Thus, the acute need is there to produce and promote the utilization of methods that guard and facilitates insightful analysis of health data while upholding the privacy of the patient. This review article offers a comprehensive glance at the latest methods for conservation of privacy in analysis of health data. It inspects the practices that are currently being utilized and evaluate the efficacy, potential uses and shortcomings while stressing the surging necessity for data handling in a secure and trustworthy manner in healthcare. This article also proffers the evaluation of multiple approaches by assessment of their relevance, performance and shortcomings in genuine healthcare environments. This article recounts the significant facts of secured data processing.

articleTitle: Integrity in the Age of AI: Detecting Synthetic Text Across Platforms and Purposes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The widespread use of artificial intelligence (AI)generated synthetic text in the digital age presents serious threats to the accuracy of content on a variety of platforms. The goal of this review paper is to compile and analyze the variety of studies devoted to recognizing text produced by artificial intelligence. We examine numerous approaches and instruments designed to differentiate texts written by humans and artificial intelligence, assessing their efficiency, constraints, and suitability in diverse settings. Our study covers a broad range of use cases, such as copyright verification, academic integrity, and disinformation detection. This study aims to illustrate the crucial role that detection systems play in ensuring the authenticity of content by discussing important discoveries, technological developments, and continuing issues in the field. We also examine the possible societal effects and ethical issues of implementing such technologies. This review highlights the necessity for ongoing research, development, and interdisciplinary collaboration to improve the detection of synthetic text as AI's capabilities continue to grow. Only then can the integrity of digital material be guaranteed in an increasingly automated environment.

articleTitle: AI-Based Cancer Risk Assessment Models: Current Trends Overview
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Cancer risk assessment is crucial for early cancer detection and prevention, customized treatment plans, and and better results for patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed the healthcare sector in recent years by providing advanced techniques for improving cancer risk assessment. This review paper provides a thorough overview of the latest advancements in AI-based cancer risk assessment models. We examine a number of AI techniques, including deep learning and machine learning, and how they could be used to the analysis of imaging, genomics, and medical records, among other data sources. The article's primary focus is on significant advancements in AI models that improve workflow integration, interpretability, and predictive accuracy for healthcare settings. We also discuss the difficulties in implementing AI, such as data privacy issues, model biases, and the need for large annotated datasets. This study shows how artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform cancer risk assessment and open the door to more accurate and customized healthcare methods by looking at recent advancements and case studies. To focus continued efforts in this quickly developing field, future research areas and approaches to overcoming present obstacles are also highlighted.

articleTitle: Air Quality Prediction Using Machine Learning: An Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Using machine learning (ML)-based prediction models could significantly improve the precision and effectiveness of traditional air quality models. This article provides a comprehensive evaluation of the state-of-the-art in machine learning-based air quality prediction. It looks at the body of research on data sources and machine learning (ML)-based techniques for predicting air quality, with a focus on the several ML techniques and data sources used. Along with discussing the limitations and shortcomings of the current machine learning-based air quality prediction models, the paper also identifies areas that require additional research. This study is divided into four components. The first section provides an overview of air quality assessment and the need for air quality prediction. The second segment reviews the literature on machine learning techniques and studies on air quality assessment. The last section looks at limitations and future research paths as well as the shortcomings of the current machine learning-based air quality prediction models. The fourth component of the study concludes with a summary of the findings and recommendations for additional research.

articleTitle: Multilingual Sentiment Analysis: A Comprehensive Review for Indian Languages
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Unleashing the power of deep learning, text classification for Indian languages is experiencing a renaissance (2019–2024). Pre-trained language models like BERT and XLM-RoBERTa, along with transfer learning, are pushing accu- racy boundaries. Researchers are customizing these methods to conquer language-specific challenges like unique writing systems, complex grammar, and the ever-present code-mixing phenomenon. However, hurdles remain. Building massive, annotated datasets, especially for resource-constrained languages, and ensuring interpretability in deep learning models are ongoing battles. The future promises exciting advancements: improved handling of low-resource languages, conquering code-mixing, and integrating explainable AI to shed light on deep models' decision-making. By overcoming these challenges, text classification has the potential to transform how we interact with and analyze the rich tapestry of information within Indian languages.

articleTitle: Predicting Customer Quits in Bottled Water Subscription Models: A Data-Driven with AI Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: To sustain customer profitability and enhance business performance, it remains vital for firms developing subscription models within the bottled water organization to predict customer quits. Using related methods based on data and analysis of more complex artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, the organization can pinpoint its most vulnerable customers and develop adequate strategies for their retention to increase customer loyalty. This paper examines the factors that define churn and outlines a sound framework of how to use predictive analytics to enhance subscription models. In the cases of selling subscriptions, another important aspect is customer loyalty since the acquisition of new clients is frequently more expensive than their retention. This is particularly true in sectors that rely on customers' continued support and use, like bottled water services, which provide repeatable services. The study also shows how advanced analytics, such as feature engineering and machine learning, help in consumer analytics and churn modelling. Companies may enhance their client retention strategies, lower churn rates, and boost loyalty via the judicious use of supervised and unsupervised learning. The paper also presents other trends in the bottled water industry and how changes in consumers' behavior, especially the younger generation, affect the subscription business model. Businesses looking to adapt to changing market circumstances by honing their retention strategies and tactics may find this paper useful.

articleTitle: Transforming the Solid Waste Management Systems Through Artificial Intelligence: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: As we all know management of solid waste has become the biggest issue these days in both rural as well as urban areas. This has become not only societal issue even environmental issue also. This research study investigates the existing potential AI applications which are already used in the process of solid waste management systems. To improve the ability of waste segregation, enhance collection efficiency, and recycling processes in predictive maintenance of waste management are assessed by the AI technologies such as machine learning, computer vision and IOT-enabled data analytics. This study also includes the future issues and challenges for the use of AI in waste management process. The research study adopts mixed research methods. In this study we go in the depth of a relevant literature review study, research papers of Scopus based journals and conferences papers to identify the gaps in the current practices and explore the existing AI applications in driving the waste management solutions. This study will provide a valuable insight about the contribution of AI in creating more sustainable waste management practices and provides few of recommendations for the future improvements.

articleTitle: Optimizing Brain Tumor Prediction Through Multiparameter Analysis and Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for predicting brain tumors by integrating multi-parameter analysis with a Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). By considering diverse parameters including medical imaging features, patient demographics, and clinical data, the proposed methodology aims to enhance prediction accuracy and reliability. The dataset is collected and preprocessed, incorporating information from MRI and CT scans, alongside demographic and clinical records. Feature extraction techniques are applied to extract pertinent features for analysis. The Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) is employed as the decision-making mechanism due to its ability to handle uncertainties inherent in medical datasets. Fuzzy logic rules, derived from expert knowledge, enable the model to interpret ambiguous input parameters. The FLC fuzzifies input variables, applies fuzzy inference rules, and defuzzifies outputs to generate predictive outcomes. Experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately predicting brain tumor occurrences. Comparative analysis showcases its superiority over existing methods. This integration of multi-parameter analysis with Fuzzy Logic Controller offers a promising framework for early detection and personalized treatment planning, ultimately improving patient care and clinical outcomes in neuro-oncology.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting for Virtual Power Plants Using Time Series Analysis and Open Energy Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Short-term load forecasting is helpful and useful in the management and operation of Virtual Power Plants, management of distributed renewable energy sources and stability of the power grid. This paper presents a dual-model time series forecasting approach where different models like ARIMA, Prophet, and LSTM have been introduced for forecasting the aggregated load of VPPs accurately. In the work, datasets of open energy consumption are used to train and test the proposed models; such datasets reflect various and often quite intricate patterns of consumption. The feature selection combines the merits of statistical analysis and machine learning providing near-optimal results for modelling of seasonality, trends and other non-linear relationships in load data. These real-life scenarios make an important aspect of the analysis in order to evaluate its effectiveness with varying penetration levels of renewable energy sources and consumer demand matrices. Such improvement of forecasting accuracy and its enhancement can be considered as valuable for VPP operators and stimulate further development of smart grid technologies. The results highlights the applicability of fusing output from various time series models and the use of open source energy data in improving short-term load forecasting of VPP thus resulting in a more robust energy system.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning and Self-Administered Tests to Predict Covid-19: an Olfactory and Gustatory Dysfunction Assessment Through Crowdsourced Data in India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Olfactory and gustatory dysfunction are common manifestations associated with COVID-19 infection, typically identified through medical evaluations or self-reports. However, self-reports are often complicated by the common confusion between these senses. In this study, we explored whether practical smell and taste tests using household items could help assess these sensory losses. Participants completed an online survey, performing smell and taste tests with everyday items. We also collected demographic data, health. These authors have equally contributed to this work. information (including COVID-19 diagnosis), and current symptoms. Using various combinations of these factors, we built multiple random forest models to predict COVID-19 diagnosis. Incorporating data from the smell and taste self-tests enhanced the predictive accuracy of the models. Certain household items like clove for smell and lemon juice for taste demonstrated statistically significant capability in distinguishing infected ones from non-infected ones. This study demonstrates that simple smell and taste tests using household items can help predict COVID-19 infection, offering a potential home-based method to identify cases and limit transmission.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms and Nlp for Anxiety and Depression Detection Using Twitter Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: According to a study published in the Journal of Medical Internet Research, individuals with depression are more likely to use language indicative of sadness, loneliness, and negative emotions on social media platforms. The rise of social media has given us new channels to better understand and combat mental health concerns like depression and anxiety. Many individuals with anxiety or depression may not seek help due to stigma or lack of awareness about their mental health condition. By identifying potential signs through social media, various machine learning methods can facilitate early detection and intervention, potentially preventing the escalation of mental health issues. Here, we apply eight machine learning methods, namely Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting Machine and AdaBoost for the automated detection of depression and anxiety through Twitter data. We evaluate the performance of different models and compare their accuracies on the task using datasets (DATD_Rand_training and DATD_training) of Twitter posts for depression and anxiety detection. Various model evaluation parameters like precision, accuracy, F1 score, and recall are used to evaluate these machinelearning models. For the first dataset (DATD+Rand_training), the highest accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores achieved were 0.926,0.927,0.926 and 0.926, respectively, by the Random Forest Algorithm, and the highest AUC achieved was 0.963 by the Decision Tree Algorithm and Logistic Regression algorithm. For the second dataset (DATD_training) the highest accuracy, recall and F1-score were 0.912,9.12,0.871 by Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine, precision was 0.871 by K-Nearest Neighbours, AUC was 0.703 was Support Vector Machine. These findings suggest that some models outperform others by a significant margin in detecting depression and anxiety from usergenerated tweets.

articleTitle: Adjudicate the Manufacturing Firm's Awareness of Green Human Resource Management Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Today, we live in a perilous era in which our environment is polluted. Our youngsters cannot breathe clean air or move freely, especially in our capital city, New Delhi. As a result, the government, various organizations, and corporate concerns are taking considerable steps to safeguard the environment. Everyone in society is working to establish green habits that will help conserve our environment and provide a bright future for our children and grandchildren. Green human resource management provides environmentally friendly products and operations, facilitating programs to protect the environment. Green HRM techniques include green employee design, green health and safety, green performance evaluation, waste management, etc. In particular, staff understanding of green practices is critical to ensuring successful adoption in organizations. The research proposes to assess employee understanding of green activities, with a particular emphasis on green HRM practices. A sample of 120 employees is drawn from the manufacturing sector in Coimbatore. According to the report, 90 percent of employees are inculcated with the practices that allow us to rely on businesses for a better green future.

articleTitle: Optimizing Withdrawal Risk Assessment for GMWB in Insurance Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The valuation and pricing of GMWB which is a key value-added component of VA helping administrators control for longevity risk to retirees. GMWB provides systematic withdrawal options to policyholders and safeguard its clients against market volatility making it a significant product for retirement planning. In this research, provide a comprehensive overview of the structure of GMWB, outlining its cost expense and tax features and put forward a new analytic methodology to evaluate the risks of insurers that use such guarantees. The paper extends prior research by investigating current pricing frameworks of GMWB, while differentiating agents fixed and temporal withdrawal patterns. This paper discusses how occurrence factors such as market fluctuations, interest rates, and mortality assumptions influence GMWB pricing and risk. Unfortunately, the current pricing models have limitations, such as their inability to fully represent the characteristics of the financial markets and the stochastic behavior of policyholders. It seems that most used models presuppose certain rather trivial conditions that hardly may be met in practice. Future research should focus on developing more sophisticated stochastic models, incorporating advanced risk factors, and improving the computational efficiency of pricing algorithms to better reflect the complexities of GMWB products and ensure more accurate risk management for insurers and retirees alike.

articleTitle: Leveraging Invariant and MultiScale Features for Parkinson's Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The moment most common neurological affliction - Parkinson's Disease (PD), effects the brain, giving rise to challenges related to movement, including issues such as rigidity, slowness, imbalance, and involuntary shaking, with the severity progressing with time. There is no established cure for the disease but AI based solutions have been continuously evolving proving their efficiency and accuracy in PD diagnosis. However, a few issues exist which needs to be addressed for PD detection: a. there is dearth of invariant modelling of features, b. there is lack of study on combined use of multiscale and invariant features and c. there is a lack of models which are able to make predictions on different types of hand drawings. The proposed model addresses these issues in three ways: first, a dataset having different types of hand drawn images like circle, meander and spiral is used. Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF) is exploited for extracting scale and rotation invariant features. A transfer learning model is also used for multiscale feature extraction in proposed hybrid model. Finally, a dense layer in employed to give the output as Healthy or Patient. The NewHandPD dataset has been used in carrying out the experiment which gives an accuracy of 99.34% outperforming all the existing works on the same dataset.

articleTitle: ZigBee-Enabled Long-Range IoT-Based Monitoring and Data Acquisition System for Real-Time Flow and Temperature Monitoring in Oil Pipelines with Cloud-Based Data Visualization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The reliable and cost-effective monitoring of critical infrastructure, such as oil pipelines, is essential for addressing operational challenges, economic losses, and environmental risks caused by issues like blockages, leaks, and temperature fluctuations. There is a growing need for comprehensive, scalable monitoring solutions with predictive capabilities. Advances in wireless communication and IoT platforms have enabled wireless sensor networks to provide continuous data collection and transmission across large areas, enhancing operational efficiency and safety. This paper presents a novel architecture for long-range monitoring of pipeline flow and temperature via wireless communication. The system facilitates real-time data collection, storage, and cloud-based visualization, allowing operators to detect abnormalities, prevent disruptions, and improve the reliability of oil transportation.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligent Systems for Dynamic Business Process Verification: A Continuous Corporate Audit Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Corporate auditors have to critically appraise thousands of documents, verify compliance with regulation, and give assurances about governance and security. Earlier, big data and costly manual work forced auditors to resort to sampling. In today's data driven world, corporates and their auditors both use next generation technologies like analytics, automation and artificial intelligence (AI). Though computers altered the range and techniques of examination, new technology has expanded its reach, reduced time, effort, and expense, and pushed the advantages of performing the task. The use of AI enables performance of repetitive tasks, better insights into the huge data and more efficient and quality audit work. Auditors' skills, professional knowledge and judgement can now be put to better use. Due to the incessant evolution of AI and automation, it is possible to bring in professional standardization to continuously monitor quality. AI is a combination of different types of technological innovations that enhances and modifies the audit process. Machine learning can be applied to go beyond sampling, appraising all available information simultaneously to invite attention to high-risk documents. Current research does not provide a roadmap for systematic adoption of AI to audit. This purpose of this study is to propose a conceptual framework for application of AI towards transformation of audits.

articleTitle: Towards Safer Networks: An HPLC Inspired Wormhole Detection Mechanism for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The rapid surge in the usage of wireless sensor networks in various fields like healthcare, military, etc has also engendered various threats and attacks targeted at these systems, one of them being wormhole attacks. Not only the wormhole nodes created during this attack are hard to detect, they can significantly deteriorate network performance and data integrity. The existing techniques for wormhole attack detection either have high false positives or suffer from high computation overload. To overcome this, this paper introduces a novel lightweight HPLC-inspired mechanism to identify wormhole nodes in wireless sensor networks to amplify the security and reliability of these networks. The performance of this mechanism is analysed based on the detection rate, false positive rate and F1 score.

articleTitle: Threat Detection in IoT Systems Using Deep Learning Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In today's world, Internet of Things (IoT) has gained a lot of popularity for some very good reasons: it introduced unprecedented connectivity and convenience in our lives. However; with the benefits of IoT also comes its fair share of security challenges. Switching into the IoT world has opened up new avenues for cyber-threats, and have witnessed an unprecedented increase in IoT based cyber-attacks which would require something more than the conventional security measures that we have at present. On this note, the Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a critical role in protecting data by pinpointing and addressing suspicious behaviours. However, the issue lies with the fact that; conventional IDS mechanisms have encountered their share of struggles with the relatively complex IoT landscape. On the other hand, Deep Learning (DL) mechanisms have demonstrated potential in effectively identifying and thwarting cyber-attacks on Internet of Things (IoT) devices. This paper dives into the intrusion detection methodologies tailored to IoT security, leveraging Deep Learning as its foundation using GAN. We go through the various types of IDS specific to IoT, emphasizing the importance of deep learning algorithm in this field. Additionally, we also discuss the hurdles in implementing DL for IoT security along with the scope of future work. This review aims to steer researchers and industry professionals towards embracing DL strategies in IoT security and intrusion detection initiatives.

articleTitle: Large Language Model Based System for Clinical Decision Support
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The vast amounts of medical data are accessed to support healthcare professionals in better diagnosing and treating their patients. Large language models (LLMs) are incorporated into clinical settings so that they can offer better expectations and enhance decision-making in the bid to eventually benefit patient outcomes from healthcare systems. This paper presents the role of LLMs in clinical decision support using natural language processing (NLP). The paper focuses on implementing LLM with the help of the proposed algorithm using NLP in clinical decision support by tokenization of clinical data. The paper also discusses challenges in the design and implementation of LLMs for healthcare. The accuracy of the system is measured using a confusion matrix and an accuracy of 85% was observed. The major challenges that still have to be addressed better include the need to guarantee accuracy, interpretability, and ethical deployment.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Recommender Systems and Digital Twins for Agile Decision-Making in Energy Startups: A Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Energy startups play a key role in improving renewable energy solutions. However, they face many challenges due to changing energy markets. They also require timely decisions based on data. AI-enabled recommender systems work with Digital Twins to offer innovative solutions. These AI systems use real-time data from different sources. They suggest the best strategies.
