Digital Twins are digital versions of real-life assets. They give predictive insights using both real-time and past data. This powerful combination helps startups decide better. They use resources well and increase energy production. Unpredictable environments make this essential. Digital Twins simulate different operational scenarios. Startups predict possible problems and reduce downtime. The overall reliability of systems gets better. AI recommender systems give clear advice on energy management. They help adjust production, storage and grid connections early. These technologies help startups organize processes and handle risks well. They also help these businesses grow fast in tough energy markets. This paper studies how AI systems and Digital Twins help energy startups decide quickly and work smoothly. It looks at the problems these startups might encounter when using these technologies. These include infrastructure and regulatory barriers. It explores the future of using AI and Digital Twins in the larger energy industry.

articleTitle: Adaptive Demand Response Optimization Using Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced Grid Stability and Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper provides an advanced work in DR modeling and optimization by applying RL techniques. Its major goal is to improve the utilization of RL methods to boost the performances of DR in power systems. Smart meter data, electricity prices, and customer load profiles from the public sources are utilized for the model creation and evaluation. It aims at studying how various advanced RL schemes such as the Q-learning and policy gradient methods can be employed for dynamic optimization of DR schemes. Stable-baselines and Ray RLlib are two Python based libraries that help in the implementation and training of these algorithms. The use of the proposed RL-based framework will enable the identification of the optimal manner in which customer load can be managed throughout the day in order to provide stability to the grid and with the least level of expense. Simulation results show that RL is a great way of automating and improving the DR strategies with the cost of implementation that is attainable for modern power systems.

articleTitle: Predicting Lung Cancer with Artificial Neural Network: Analyzing Performance and Feature Importance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Lung cancer is the primary cause of cancer-related deaths globally. This cancer is majorly observed in smokers, increasing air pollution has also begun to affect non-smokers. Research indicates that exposure to polluted air significantly raises the risk of developing lung cancer, posing a major threat to public health. Despite advancements in medical technology, the mortality rate from lung cancer remains high, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis. Machine learning and deep learning offer promising solutions for early and accurate prediction through advanced data analysis. In our study, we utilized a dataset with 26 attributes for discern lung cancer, categorizing cases into three risk levels: high, medium, and low. We applied various algorithms and develop an Artificial Neural Network (ANN), comparing the overall performance with various machine-learning and deep-learning models. Our results show that the ANN achieved a high accuracy of 94.9% using the Adam optimizer, making it an effective model for lung cancer prediction.

articleTitle: Improving Coronary Artery Disease Prediction: The Role of GAN-Simulated Genetic Variants in Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of global mortality through the narrowing of coronary arteries from plaque buildup, which restricts blood flow to the heart. Recent studies indicate the genetic underpinnings of CAD and how complex genetic variations affect its occurrence. However, the scarcity and heterogeneity of genetic datasets make it difficult to predict CAD with a high degree of accuracy, particularly for rare critical variants. The combination of patient medical history, clinical variables, and genetic information through machine learning algorithms enhances the prediction of CAD. However, techniques such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM have the potential but are limited in their predictive capabilities due to data quality and representation issues. This work proposes the use of GANs as a solution to overcome these inherent difficulties - generating synthetic genetic variants that can capture the nuances in real - world data. The GAN-simulated data closely mimics true patterns of genetic variants and hence reveals complex genetic interactions. Addition of the GAN-simulated data to the CAD prediction model significantly improves the generalization capability across different populations, reducing bias and allowing an improved estimation of risk. In conjunction with explainable AI techniques, this GAN-based approach would enable prevention for individuals at higher risk of developing CAD. Though GANs offer a lot of promise, overcoming challenges like overfitting and mode collapse as well as ethics associated with using synthetic data calls for a judicious approach for their proper application in the clinic.

articleTitle: Sink Vulnerability Type Prediction Using Small Language Model (SLM)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A 2024 report on the cost of data breaches estimates the average cost of a breach at USD 4.88 million, with 4.33% of these breaches attributed to unpatched vulnerabilities 1. Beyond data breaches, such vulnerabilities can lead to unauthorized access or even total system compromise. A sink vulnerability is a security flaw where untrusted or unvalidated input is passed directly to a “sink” in a system, creating opportunities for attackers to exploit the system. This paper proposes a supervised machine learning approach for classifying sink vulnerabilities into specific categories based on method signatures. The experi- mental results demonstrate that fine-tuning a Small Language Model (SLM) using Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) significantly outperforms traditional boosting algorithms employing TF-IDF for the task of sink vulnerability classification. The fine tuned SLM can be applied to identify, categorize, and thereby take quick efficient remedial actions to patch these vulnerabilities. The experiments demonstrate that CodeT5+ 220M, a SLM that can be used without a Graphic Processing Unit (GPU) is highly effective for the sink vulnerability type prediction.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Early Detection of Cardiac Arrest Risk Factors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: An interruption in the heart's electrical rhythm can result in cardiac arrest, which is potentially fatal. Effective management depends on accurately identifying high-risk patients, providing quick clinical care, and performing successful resuscitation. (ML) Researchers have used systems that are excellent at analyzing complex data to forecast the risk of cardiac arrest. Using real-time datasets from Kaggle, this study assessed four Machine Learning (ML) algorithms: Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), and Extreme Gradient Boost (XGBoost). The testing results showed that the RF-based ML technique displayed greater accuracy than existing algorithms. This demonstrates how can forecast the danger of cardiac arrest. ML algorithms can find patterns and risk factors that a human clinician might not be able to see. Healthcare professionals can build individualized preventive measures and interventions by utilizing these algorithms to acquire insightful information about a person's propensity for cardiac arrest.

articleTitle: Innovative Solutions for COVID-19 Prevention: Automated Multi-Functional Sanitization Chamber
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has emphasized the critical need for effective health safety measures in public spaces. This paper introduces a sensor-based automatic multifunctional sanitization system designed to automate hand sanitization, body temperature detection, and whole-body disinfection. Utilizing an Arduino microcontroller and various sensors, the system operates seamlessly in high-traffic areas like hospitals, offices, and malls. Key processes include touch-free hand sanitization, temperature screening (<100°F), and sodium hypochlorite fogging for comprehensive disinfection, achieving an average process time of 10–15 seconds per user. The system incorporates audio and visual indicators for completion, ensuring continuous operation without human intervention. Experimental evaluations demonstrate high accuracy in thermal screening (±1°C) and effective disinfection coverage, with minor limitations in sensor performance under extreme environmental conditions. These results highlight the system's efficiency and potential for scalable implementation in public health safety.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques for Early Detection of Liver Disease: A Comparative Study of Predictive Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Liver diseases are one of the most severe threats happening nowadays globally about health, in which millions of people suffer from such critical conditions and becomes life-threatening if not diagnosed earlier. The traditional models showcased limited accuracy, because earlier diagnostic methods were relying on statistical analysis and medical experts“ evaluation, which might not capture complex patterns in the data. In this research paper, machine learning techniques are used for predicting liver disease based on patient data obtained in terms of liver enzyme levels, bilirubin, and demographic features. The focus is on creating and comparing different ML models, such as Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Decision Trees and Logistic Regression, in the context of early diagnosis. In preprocessing data, handling missing values and dealing with issues of class imbalance, several steps are very significant for improving model performance. Some of the evaluation metrics, namely F1-score, precision, accuracy, recall, and AUC- ROC, have been used to measure the effectiveness of the models built. This work clearly suggests overfitting and interpretability, mainly in the context of medical data, but the results show that more sophisticated ML techniques can drastically improve prediction in the case of liver disease, especially very important insights for early intervention and clinical support systems in healthcare.

articleTitle: Smart Waste Management System: A Comprehensive Approach to Automated Waste Segregation and Air Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Environmental degradation, health hazards, and inefficiencies stem from outdated waste management methods unsuitable for modern urban environments. This paper proposes an intelligent waste management system incorporating IoT and advanced sensors for a fully automated solution. Ultrasonic sensors measure waste volume, soil moisture sensors distinguish wet from dry waste, and metal detectors identify metallic waste. Air quality is monitored using MQ-135 sensors to track pollution levels around bins. An automated conveyor belt system ensures precise segregation of recyclables at the source. A web-based interface facilitates real-time tracking of bin status and environmental conditions across various locations. The system employs a dynamic routing algorithm to optimize waste collection paths, reducing travel distances, fuel consumption, and carbon emissions. Initial tests indicate superior waste classification accuracy, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and enhanced resource utilization compared to conventional methods. This scalable, modular system is adaptable to both small communities and large cities. Future enhancements may integrate machine learning to predict waste volume, improving collection efficiency. By fostering automation and sustainability, the system contributes to waste overflow prevention and a reduced carbon footprint in waste collection processes.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Disaster Recovery Strategies for SAP S/4HANA in the Cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study presents a detailed investigation into the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies for disaster recovery in SAP S/4HANA systems deployed in cloud environments. The research emphasizes three primary aspects: proactive failure prediction, automated response mechanisms, and the optimization of Recovery Time Objectives (RTO). By employing advanced machine learning models, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation, the study highlights the potential for transforming disaster recovery strategies in dynamic and complex SAP landscapes. Key findings indicate that AI driven approaches significantly enhance system resilience and reduce downtime by enabling early anomaly detection, adaptive workload distribution, and efficient data replication techniques. Predictive models demonstrated accuracy rates exceeding 90% in identifying potential failures, while AI-optimized strategies achieved up to 62% improvement in recovery times. Furthermore, the integration of AI with cloud-native solutions and emerging technologies, such as edge computing and federated learning, offers promising directions for addressing the challenges of scalability, data security, and system complexity. The study underscores the need for continuous refinement of AI models to adapt to evolving SAP environments and calls attention to ethical considerations in autonomous decision-making. These advancements, coupled with quantum computing and other innovations, are poised to redefine disaster recovery practices, enabling businesses to maintain robust, flexible, and resilient IT infrastructures.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Brain MRI Scans Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The rise in Alzheimer's disease cases has become a challenge to global healthcare systems, hence making it mandatory to develop proper accurate diagnostic tools. This paper introduces an aggressive deep learning model using CNNs (Convolutional neural network) to classify Alzheimer's disease into four stages: Non-Demented, Really Gentle Demented, Light Demented, and Reasonable Demented. This variant leverages the well-balanced preparation approach and novel ways of data generation to overcome class imbalance and enhance generalization altogether. The design and practice schedule with monitoring metrics like correctness, AUC, and F 1 rating ensures optimal performance and robustness. The classification ability of the proposed design was observed to be truly remarkable and surpassed conventional tactics both in the dimensions of accuracy and sensitivity. These findings expand the prospects in CNN-based systems directed at the early and accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer's, as they become relevant for medical practice and as a basis for further innovation in medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Multi-Attribute Optimization of Hot Machining Using Grey Relational Analysis and PCA Technique – A Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: High manganese steel machining with coated carbide inserts has been accomplished for hot machining processes. To maximize the multi-performance characteristics the principal component analysis (PCA) has been coupled with grey relational approach (GRA). To verify that the grey relationship grade results, a confirmation test has been conducted.

articleTitle: Implementation and Evaluation of a FaceNet Inspired Model for Facial Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The facial recognition technology has greatly improved with models like FaceNet reaching a higher level of accuracy. Still, the original FaceNet model is complex and requires a lot of computational power to build and train the model making it challenging for resource constrained environments. This paper introduces a simplified version of the FaceNet model that is designed to be less complex and remain accurate for facial recognition tasks while retaining the core concepts of FaceNet with a simpler architecture of a convolutional neural network that reduces the computational burden while maintaining robustness in learning facial features. Our approach consists of the use of multiple layers of convolution layer with ReLU activation, batch normalization layer, max-pooling layer, and dropout layer to prevent overfitting. We propose a two-stage training procedure with triplet loss by first using random negatives and then introducing semi-hard and hard negatives. This method ensures that, even with a simplified structure, the model captures effective discriminative features by focusing on challenging examples. The proposed model was trained on CASIA WebFace dataset and was tested on Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW) dataset. Experiments suggest that the simplified model gains competitive accuracy in face recognition tasks while significantly reducing computational requirements and can be efficiently used in lieu of much complex designs while suffering minimal loss of accuracy.

articleTitle: Role of AI in Breast Cancer Detection through Medical Image Analysis: Overview, Methods, and Unresolved Problems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Breast cancer is a major global health concern, and the key to excellent treatment outcomes is early and accurate detection. Because they provide non-invasive, high-resolution insights into the presence, extent, and development of the illness, medical imaging techniques have completely changed the way breast cancer is diagnosed and treated. The early identification and diagnosis of breast cancer depend heavily on a number of medical imaging modalities, including digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, positron emission tomography (PET), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), mammography, and molecular imaging. These modalities are thoroughly examined in this review work. The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of each imaging technique, accounting for accessibility, sensitivity, specificity, and cost-effectiveness. Additionally, it looks at the most recent advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning, which have significantly increased the accuracy and efficacy of image interpretation and assisted doctors in making wise decisions[16]. The study explores multimodal imaging for targeted therapies and personalized medicine, addressing challenges as well as advancements in breast cancer. It provides a comprehensive overview of emerging medical imaging techniques to enhance patient outcomes and reduce mortality.

articleTitle: IoT-Web Smart Waste Management System for Environmental Sustainability in Smart Cities: An Integrated Approach Under Swachh Bharat Mission
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Waste management commonly employs the Internet of Things (IoT) to enhance and refine the processes of waste collection, disposal, and recycling. The present work introduces an IoT-Web Smart Waste Management System (SWMS) under the ‘Swachh Bharat Mission’ for smart cities. This study aims to promote sustainable waste management practices that maintain a clean, eco-friendly environment. We achieve this by integrating robust FRP (fiber-reinforced plastic) with laser sensors (VL53LOX) for accurate garbage level monitoring, load sensors for weight measurement, and microcontrollers (Node-MCU2ESP32 and Arduino) for various tasks. Additionally, an MQ-2 gas sensor identifies unhealthy and flammable gases, signaling the need to clean the bin. The bin lives with a servomotor (MG995), battery, and buzzer. When in operation mode, the lid automatically opens upon an approaching person and closes upon the proper placement of waste. It also prevents overflow by staying shut when it is full. Operators can access real-time data remotely by channelizing and hosting the smart bin on a web server. This cloud-based web application makes it convenient for users to track waste levels, receive alerts when the bin is full, and take timely action, all from the comfort of their home. This IoT and web approach improves waste management by allowing users to make proactive decisions on live data. This model can also be implemented in commercial applications such as schools, colleges, universities, railways, airports, shopping malls, car parks, hospitals, and other public places. This model not only engages children but also makes waste disposal more exciting, thereby promoting better waste management practices. This study is to present an IoT-Web Smart Waste Management System to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Dynamic Graph Representation for WSI Classification: A Knowledge-Aware Attention Mechanism for Enhanced Computational Pathology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Computational pathologists are now concentrating on developing methods for histopathological WSI analysis using deep learning. Methods using Transformer as a foundation are widely debated in the present paradigm, which is largely built on multiple instances learning (MIL). By using WSI sequence tokens to represent patches; these methods transform WSI tasks into sequence tasks. Gigapixel scale and high heterogeneity both contribute to feature complexity, which in turn causes Transformer-based MIL to struggle with issues including sluggish inference speed, large memory usage, and poor performance. Furthermore, the intricate structural relationships bet to en biological entities (such as the varied interactions bet to en various cell types) in the WSI cannot be mined using graph-based approaches. The research suggests a solution by outlining an ideal algorithm for dynamic graph representation that views WSIs as a subset of the knowledge graph structure. In particular, the research uses the head-tail interactions bet to en instances to build directed edge embeddings and neighbours dynamically. Afterwards, to come up with a knowledge-aware attention mechanism that can refresh the features of the head node by acquiring the combined attention score of every neighbour and edge. At last, the Puma optimiser algorithm performs the fine-tuning, and thanks to the updated head's global pooling process, to have an embedding at the graph level that can be used as an implicit illustration for WSI classification. Our system significantly outperforms state-of-the-art tactics on multiple tasks, as shown by extensive testing on three public TCGA benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Decentralized Intelligence: The Convergence of AI and Edge Computing for Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: By combining edge computing with AI, technology is now experiencing a revolution - and data is being processed and decisions are being made where the data “lives” instead of having to rely on distant servers. This research explores how this trend is completely remaking industries like those in healthcare, manufacturing, and autonomous vehicles. The closer to the user's service is the information processing, the better the experience for the user in critical situations, and it also improves data security and bandwidth consumption. Edge based AI devices are improving patient monitoring and diagnostics while shortening critical care responses in healthcare. It is helping to streamline production in manufacturing through real time analysis and predictive maintenance. Edge computing is key to fast decisions in autonomous systems for vehicles and drones without continuous internet. In this study, we explore the state of art on using AI on the edge, current and future practical applications, challenges and future trends and their impact on industries undergoing digital transformation.

articleTitle: Review on Error Dynamics in Predicting Modes of Oscillation Indian Monsoon and/or Allied Phenomena
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The Indian monsoon is a very complex coupled ocean atmospheric system which exhibits variability beyond different time scale, it is very challenging task for making accurate prediction. The modes of oscillation are predicted like intra seasonal and inter annual variability is crucial for concerning the behavior of Indian monsoon and/ or allied phenomena. Using different climate models error dynamics involved in forecasting the oscillatory mode of the Indian monsoon is explored. By analyzing error propagation, model biases and unpredictability in initial condition this study tells about how expand over time and affect the accuracy of prediction. the Madden- Julian Oscillation (MJO) and the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) are the special case which influence monsoon dynamics. Through the help of linear regression and Fast Fourier Transform and various machine learning algorithm the prediction of error dynamics will be processed. This research focuses on elucidating the dynamics of errors that arise from the interaction of various meteorological factors and the statistical models employed. The study employs a multi-faceted approach, incorporating data from meteorological observations, satellite imagery, and historical climate records. Statistical models, ranging from traditional time series analyses to advanced machine learning algorithms, are employed to assess their efficacy in capturing the nuances of monsoonal behavior. The findings will be valuable for meteorologists, climate scientists, and policymakers in developing more robust and accurate forecasting systems, with implications for regional disaster preparedness, agriculture, and water resource management. This review paper synthesizes the current state of knowledge regarding error dynamics in statistical forecasting models for the Indian monsoon and related phenomena. It examines key concepts, methodologies, challenges, and recent advancements in understanding and improving forecast accuracy. In methodology section the paper discusses about the comparative analysis of simple linear regression, FFT and derived advantages and disadvantages of the methods

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Secure and Collaborative Power System Data ANALYSIS: Balancing Accuracy and Privacy in Decentralized Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The level of digitization in the current power systems has seen the generation of large volumes of data which provide a customer more options for enhanced visualization. Nevertheless, the proposed data is highly sensitive, which triggers multiple privacy issues to share this information among various utilities and stakeholders. This research aims at exploring the use of federated learning, a decentralized machine learning model, to overcome these in power system data analysis. Due to its ability to train machine learning models on several data sources co-operatively, federated learning helps to manage privacy by keeping data localized. They pointed out that the proposed method uses the properties of power system data, in particular temporal and spatial dependencies, also does not violate strict privacy requirements. The study shows that federated learning can improve the efficiency of utilities' cooperation and advance the power system operation and planning while preserving the data privacy. Such work is a remarkable progress in the integration of ML with power systems, providing a solid solution to the privacy issues that challenge this important area.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of Rotor Bars Using Vibration and Current Signals via Artificial Intelligence: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper implemented Motor Current Signature Analysis to diagnose broken rotor bar faults, with the aid of an experimental setup, it then looks into BRB fault diagnosis using bearing vibration signals. However conventional diagnostic techniques such as vibration analysis and Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) have encountered some difficulties in identifying rotor bar faults early on. In order to improve the accuracy of fault detection and enable real-time monitoring, this paper aims to apply AI techniques for rotor bar condition monitoring by integrating both vibration and current signals. With the ability to automatically detect faults and improve sensitivity, the use of AI and machine learning (ML) technologies for condition monitoring has grown in popularity in recent years. By using SVM in the integration of the two signal modes to improve the accuracy of the signals and the robustness of the fault conditions monitoring. The present work has been compared to Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and findings show that SVM performs better than ANN in terms of diagnostic efficiency and accuracy.

Author Keywords: Condition Monitoring of Broken Rotor Bar

articleTitle: Parkinson's Diagnosis Through the Use of AI Throught Speech and Gait
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Parkinson's disease is a chronic movement disorder that primarily affects movement and speech and much of patients' quality of life. Yet even with the second most common neurological disorder after Alzheimer's the diagnosis in initial stages and with a high level of accuracy still remains an issue. Exploiting speech and gait data offers tremendous potential for increasing diagnostic precision of the used tools. This research aims at incorporating the use of complex self-organising techniques and Feature selection as a means of improving early diagnosis of PD. Through the study of both speech and gait data, we employ an array of classifier models, including Random Forest, SVM, and Gradient Boosting, and use SHAP and LIME for feature importance determination. Such a model not only discriminates as to whether a person develops Parkinson's disease or not with very high accuracy but also identifies which features are most crucial in that decision. Multimodal's approach along with the strong features selection and classification leads to enhancement of the early and accurate diagnosis for Parkinson's disease which enables an early critical interferences of the patients.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Approaches for Identifying Misinformation in Social Media Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The proliferation of social media and online information dissemination has led to a significant worry regarding fake news. False news detection is a difficult problem requiring a multidisciplinary approach combining natural language processing, machine learning, and social network research. This article provides a comprehensive review of the major area by classifying the research on false news identification into three categories: feature-based approaches, machine learning methods, and social network analysis methods. We look into many feature types in news, such as textual, social context, and metadata characteristics, that are utilized to identify bogus news. We look at various machine learning techniques, including supervised learning and unique algorithm approaches that have been applied to detect bogus news. Furthermore, we delineate plausible remedies for the issues and limitations of the existing false news identification system.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Nasdaq-100 Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study focuses on leveraging machine learning algorithms to predict and analyse the performance of the NASDAQ-100 index in financial markets. Our objectives encompass developing accurate predictive models, identifying the growth of the index, and determining the trends. Through extensive data preprocessing and model evaluation, our findings indicate that the index possesses great potential for a long-term investment. This research holds significance for people involved in related sectors and also provides guidance for further exploration in this field.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Crop Disease Detection and Identification: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: High dependence for global food security and reduced agricultural economic losses are driven by the rapid identification and detection of crop diseases and pests. Deep learning and the application of convolutional neural networks hold considerable potential in the automatization of this process with high accuracy. The study evaluates two deep learning models: first, EfficientNet; and second, ResNet50 and EfficientNet ensemble model. These studies were applied on the PlantDoc dataset and directed towards development improvements in detection abilities in challenging conditions, such as varying resolutions for image, complexity of backgrounds, and the fluctuation of illumination conditions. Both models were subjected to fine tuning with optimized hyperparameters to ensure robust detection of diseases and pests on different plant species. Based on the previous discussions, the best performance was seen in the ensemble model composed of ResNet50 and EfficientNet with a precision of approximately 90%. Thus, this study focuses on the potential of the CNN-based approaches in crop disease detection based on the impact deep learning can bring into agricultural early and accurate management.

articleTitle: Microgrid System for Rural Electrification using Standalone Solar PV and Batteries to Promote Green Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This research paper comprehensively analyzes a standalone microgrid system utilizing zero-emission technology for rural electrification. Through meticulous assessments of load profiles., resource availability., and solar irradiance., the study elucidates seasonal variations affecting photovoltaic (PV) array performance. Utilizing PV syst software., detailed analyses of power generation., ohmic losses., and mismatch losses are conducted. Moreover., evaluations of battery performance in terms of state of charge (SOC) are presented. The study uncovers significant variations in mismatch losses across different months., peaking at 7208 kWh in April and bottoming out at 4320 kWh in January. Similarly., ohmic wire losses exhibit variability., ranging from 4560 kWh in April to a minimum of 2003 kWh in December. PV array losses at nominal production are found to be 15.8%. in this study., power production is totally dependent on renewable energy source therefore it reduces 1.,098.,614 kg/yr of carbon dioxide., 4.,763 kg/yr of sulfur dioxide., and 2.,329 kg/yr of nitrogen oxides to zero GHG emissions. Notably., the study underscores the necessity for optimization strategies to minimize energy losses and enhance overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Machine Learning Approaches for Phishing Website Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Website phishing, a notable cybercrime, involves deceiving individuals by impersonating legitimate websites. URL spoofing, a common technique in website phishing, involves creating website names. The primary objective of this paper is to accurately differentiate between legitimate and phishing sites using relevant URL attributes and different binary classification machine learning algorithms. This study compares simple, bagging, and boosting algorithms across performance analysis metrics. The best-performing models are selected for an ensemble approach. Additionally, various hyperparameter tuning techniques are assessed for the Random Forest Classifier, and Explainable AI methods like LIME and SHAP are used to interpret findings. The experiment yields optimal parameters, achieving 89. % accuracy with an ensemble model with K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, XG Boost, and Cat Boost. These findings highlight the significance of ensemble models and hyperparameter tuning in machine learning.

articleTitle: Enhancing Renewable Energy Management with Neural Networks and Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Given the ever-increasing dependence on renewable energy as the main source of electric power across the globe, efficient tackling of its associated challenges and unpredictability is very vital. The paper proposes a new solution to improve the control, supervision and decision-making on the production of renewable energy through the integration of neural network analysis and blockchain system. Solar and wind energy system data from the large and extensive database were gathered and sorted through the state- of-art of neural networks to enhance the quality and accuracy of the data. In order to guarantee the correctness, confidentiality, and usefulness of this data, it is written down on a blockchain in the process of its generation, which makes data management multisession and mutually beneficial for all the participants. Besides it presents a new approach for utilizing the renewable energy data and demonstrates that the neural networks when linked with the blockchain provide the opportunity to make automatic and accurate decisions. Potential works, it what follows, will consider scalability, real-time data processing, environmental effects of blockchain for increasing the efficiency of the suggested system.

articleTitle: Revealing Confidential Information: The Function of Data Analytics for Participants in Contemporary Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: A new era of energy management with varied energy sources, changing customer wants, and environmental concerns has been brought about by the Energy Internet. In the uncertain world of today, data analytics aids in problem solving and opportunity seizing for all. The complexity of data analytics is examined in this essay along with its significance for Energy Internet workers. In this essay, the significance of data analytics for energy experts is emphasised. A novel method is created by combining Time Series Forecasting, Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection, and Predictive Analytics for Renewable Energy Integration. Combining these algorithms creates a data-driven system to address the main challenges facing the energy sector. To thoroughly examine the process, a comparative analysis was conducted. This study outlines the advantages and disadvantages of the suggested approach and compares it to corporate norms. The MAE, RMSE, F1-Score, Precision, and Recall metrics are used to gauge how effective certain methods are. According to the investigation, the suggested method achieves a reasonable balance between precise forecasts and outliers. It continuously enhances system stability, renewable energy use, and energy demand forecasting.

articleTitle: TotalSol: A Multi-Layer Static Analysis Method for Vulnerability Detection in Ethereum Based Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Blockchain was originally developed for digital currency, but the capability of technology extends quite far beyond cryptocurrency. The Smart Contracts, self-executing and unalterable digital agreements, further extended the capability. While smart contracts offer various possibilities, they are also vulnerable to a variety of attacks such as integer overflows, reentrancy attacks and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. This research paper reviews the currently available tools that are used to detect these vulnerabilities, such as fuzz testing and static code analysis. Limitations of these tools such as scalability issues, high false positives, high false negatives and difficulties in handling large and complex contracts are highlighted. To address all these problems, this paper introduces a tool named ‘TotalSol’, a new tool that combines various analysis methods into a single comprehensive solution with a scalable platform. Using analysers like Slither, Aderyn and SmartCheck, TotalSol solves the accuracy, speed and scalability problems while minimizing false negatives and false positives. It creates a platform for developers and researchers to add new methods and detection tools in their underlying architecture without much alteration. A smart contract downloader tool is proposed to gather real-time contract data for better analysis. This research targets to deliver a more effective and an automated way to analyse the smart contracts. This ensures high security standards and reduces the risks involved with vulnerabilities in the decentralized applications.

articleTitle: ML-Enhanced Predictive Maintenance for Motor Drives: A Time Series Forecasting Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: New features in predictive maintenance have greatly boosted the reliability and effectiveness of motor drives, which are compounds in industry machines. This paper introduces a novel approach that uses sophisticated artificial neural network algorithms such as LSTM and the Prophet algorithms in predicting the maintenance requirements and the useful life of those motor drive components. The overall sensors information with vibration, temperature, and current harmonics' data obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and IOT industrial platforms is used which enhance the performance and brings high accuracy of proposed method for accurate early failure predictions and maintenance scheduling. The incorporation of these machine learning models in a time series framework assists in the timely detection of these faults and scheduling of the maintenance actions hence extending the use of motor drives. The results show great potential of this methodology and should stimulate growth of interest in predictive maintenance among industries that need to improve the efficiency and reliability of their motor drive systems.

articleTitle: Contactless Monitoring of Vital Signs Using Thermal Facial Imaging and Machine Learning for Health Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Measuring critical health data such as heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation (SpO2) from a distance is an area of research, especially when normal methods do not work well. This paper presents a new method to predict these health metrics by using thermal videos of faces taken by a thermal camera. The proposed system would use ResNet50 as a feature extractor for the thermal video frames and then Support Vector Machine (SVM) regression for the prediction of the key physiological metrics, which include heart rate, blood pressure, and SpO2 levels. The system would process extracted thermal video frames of some physical exercises, like cycling or treadmill activities, aligned to the corresponding physiological data. This is the trained SVM model, which estimates all vital parameters, hence enabling a non-invasive and continuous monitoring of the health status of a person. Results The results achieved demonstrate a Mean Absolute Error of 3.5 BPM in heart rate estimation and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.85, showing the reliability of the system. This is an excellent model with a very robust contactless solution for clinical and fitness applications. This work opens the door to the development of non-wearable systems for continuous health assessment, with a high potential for clinical and personal health management.

articleTitle: Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm for Dynamic Traveling Salesman Problem Optimization Leveraging Real-Time Gis Data Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Applying ML techniques into smart grid architectures has transformed the predictive maintenance to a level that can predict equipment failures before they occur. This approach reduces the power system downtimes and also results to a very low maintenance cost hence make the power systems more reliable and efficient. The paper examines a variety of the supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches appropriate for processing petabytes of data collected through smart grid sensors and monitoring systems. These algorithms enable the study to find out such patterns and abnormal signs that signify that a piece of equipment is likely to break down soon thus preventative measures are taken. They include: higher models that can predict the failures with higher accuracy and also the causes of the failures that can enable the right approach to be made. These studies reveal that for the improvement of the operational reliability of smart grids, it is indispensable to use ML, thereby signalling a paradigm shift from reliability-centred maintenance to reliability enhancement centring on smart maintenance. In this study, we provide the further understanding of how advanced analytical tools can enhance the practical implementation of smart grid, and general aspect of energy industry.

articleTitle: Visual Understanding and Navigation for the Visually Impaired Using Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Visually impaired people face problems with independent navigation due to limited visual information. Facing significant challenges, they often travel with an assistant or their relative. This project introduces an approach, increasing the independence of a blind user by developing new software solutions. The proposed system employs DenseNet201 for feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for generating accurate, context-aware captions. These captions are converted into real-time auditory descriptions using the gTTS library, enabling users to interpret and navigate their environment confidently. Evaluated on the Flickr8k dataset, the system achieved a BLEU score of 0.721, demonstrating its ability to generate high-quality captions. The system's architecture is designed to balance accuracy, efficiency, and user accessibility. Additionally, the system incorporates a modular architecture optimized for computational efficiency and scalability. Future work includes exploring wearable technology for continuous real-time feedback, integrating advanced natural language processing (NLP) models for richer contextual understanding, and enhancing its applicability in complex indoor and outdoor environments. This approach represents a significant step toward empowering visually impaired individuals with improved mobility and environmental awareness.

articleTitle: Adaptive Machine Learning Models for Enhanced Renewable Energy Forecasting and Grid Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: As the contribution of renewable energy sources especially solar and wind energy increases its feed to the grid stability is threatened due to the variability and intermittency of the energy sources. This research proposes fresh ways of improving the accuracy of renewable energy forecasting using improved machine learning algorithms such as deep learning and ensemble models. The methods introduced in a paper prove to perform better when predicting short-term energy output by integrating large scaled historical data with instant meteorological data. The above-discussed improvements in the forecasting models do help in managed uncertainty related to renewable energy generation while at the same time offer better data to the grid operators for utilising dynamic grid management. This results to better control of the power grids, efficient management of the available resource and enhanced incorporation of renewable energy into the power system. The conclusions emphasise the significance of machine learning in fighting the concerns posed in the case of renewable energy prediction and thus, contribute to the shift towards the development of a more sustainable and strong energy network.

articleTitle: Microbial Safety Aspects of Street Food and Rapid Detection of Foodborne Pathogens Using Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The microbial safety of street food is a crucial factor that needs to be carefully considered. Microorganisms in food can cause serious, even fatal, food-borne illnesses such Salmonellosis, Listeriosis, Campylobacteriosis, Botulism, Cholera, Escherichia coli infection, and Hepatitis. Street food has a higher risk of contamination because it is frequently sold in public places close to markets and streets. Street vendors are frequently lack basic knowledge and skills related to food safety. As a result, poor handling and preparation of food can occasionally lead to contamination. Therefore, detection and identification of microbes which cause food-borne illnesses is also a matter of concern when it comes to food safety. Once the pathogen is detected and identified, the illness can be treated and further preventive measures can be implemented. The conventional approaches for detecting foodborne microbes are time-consuming and requires intense labor. Hence, rapid detection methods utilizing biosensors such as optical, electrical, and mass-based biosensors and their subtypes, have been developed. These methods have also proved to be reliable and are now widely employed in food industries. This article emphasizes the significance of street food safety and the ways in which rapid detection techniques can support it.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Environmental and Operational Performance of Electric Trucks in Indian Food Supply Chains Using Advanced Data Analytics and Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: With increasing pressure to adopt sustainable logistics solutions, electric trucks have emerged as a key player in reducing carbon emissions and enhancing energy efficiency within food supply chains. This study builds upon prior cost-benefit analysis by incorporating a multi-dimensional optimization model for those factors in not only the total cost of ownership but also the environmental impacts, operational efficiency, and renewable energy integration. A dataset of 13 Electric trucks is used to simulate various fleet configurations, with a focus on renewable energy-powered charging stations, real-time route optimization using AI algorithms, and battery performance under diverse operating conditions. A novel hybrid total cost of ownership and environmental impact model is developed to evaluate the potential of electric trucks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and optimize costs under different charging strategies (solar, grid, hybrid), usage scenarios, and future energy prices. This research offers strategic insights for fleet managers and policymakers aiming to create a resilient and green food supply chain. Monte Carlo simulations and sensitivity analyses are employed to forecast the financial and environmental benefits of Electric truck adoption, offering a dynamic perspective on future adoption rates. The paper concludes by recommending policy incentives and strategic deployment plans for maximizing Electric truck adoption in Food supply chains.

articleTitle: Fuel Cell Vehicles: Technology, Challenges & Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: According to the report, the annual cost of environmental humiliation globally is around about $5 trillion. The International Energy Agency (IEA 2020) stated that transportation accounts for 24% of worldwide CO2 emissions. The European Environment Agency (EEA 2020) reports that the transportation sector is liable for approximately 27% of CO2 releases, with vehicles donating to over 70% of releases. To reduce CO2 releases and other GHGs, several developed countries are focusing on the use of FCVs. This paper discussed several FC technologies, such as AFCs, PEMFCs, SOFCs, PAFCs, MCFCs, and DMFCs, hydrogen production technology, storage of hydrogen, and the use of AI to store and transport. After this, many challenges are faced in the adoption of FCVs because of the lack of hydrogen filling stations, durability, low range, high cost, and energy sources. Some recommendations are discussed to overcome these challenges and then talked about its future. In conclusion, FCV is capable of changing the entire automobile industry. FCVs are zero-emission and ecofriendly vehicles. Researchers and developers are trying to improve efficiency, and performance and reduce the cost. It is a sustainable transportation system, which helps to keep the environment clean and green.

articleTitle: From Sensor to Insight: A Comprehensive Overview of Data Acquisition Methods in IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized data collection by enabling ubiquitous sensing and real-time monitoring across various domains. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of data acquisition techniques and methods employed in IoT deployments. We begin by outlining the core components of an IoT data acquisition system, including sensors, signal conditioning units, and Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs). We then delve into various data acquisition methods, categorized by factors like data type (analog vs. digital) and transmission protocols (wired vs. wireless). Common techniques explored include direct sensor readings, image/audio capture, and RFID tags for identification. Furthermore, the paper addresses considerations specific to the IoT environment, such as resource constraints on devices and energy efficiency. We discuss data filtering and compression techniques to optimize data transmission and storage. Additionally, the importance of data security and privacy in the context of large-scale data acquisition is highlighted. This overview paper aims to equip readers with a foundational understanding of the diverse data acquisition techniques that empower the vast potential of the Internet of Things. By exploring these methods, we can unlock the power of real-time data for intelligent decision-making and innovation across various industries.

articleTitle: Advancing Predictive Maintenance in Smart Grids with Machine Learning Techniques Through Comparative Analysis of SVM and CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Applying ML techniques into smart grid architectures has transformed the predictive maintenance to a level that can predict equipment failures before they occur. This approach reduces the power system downtimes and also results to a very low maintenance cost hence make the power systems more reliable and efficient. The paper examines a variety of the supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches appropriate for processing petabytes of data collected through smart grid sensors and monitoring systems. These algorithms enable the study to find out such patterns and abnormal signs that signify that a piece of equipment is likely to break down soon thus preventative measures are taken. They include: higher models that can predict the failures with higher accuracy and also the causes of the failures that can enable the right approach to be made. These studies reveal that for the improvement of the operational reliability of smart grids, it is indispensable to use ML, thereby signalling a paradigm shift from reliability-centred maintenance to reliability enhancement centring on smart maintenance. In this study, we provide the further understanding of how advanced analytical tools can enhance the practical implementation of smart grid, and general aspect of energy industry.

articleTitle: Advanced AI Techniques for Restoring Historical Documents and Photographs with Generative Adversarial and Diffusion Models for Cultural Heritage Preservation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: It is becoming the leading solution for bringing back the lost or damaged digital images, which are crucial for keeping history and culture alive. In this work, the state-of-art Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), including CycleGAN and Pix2Pix, as well as diffusion models, have been explored for the first time in the area of historical image enhancement. The datasets are collected from the public domain; they are the Library of Congress and Old Picture repositories for training and testing the models. As illustrated by the framework under consideration, the fine details are reconstructed and noise is minimized when compared to other major approaches, thus the legibility and aesthetic quality of historical items are improved. The approach combines up-to-date machine learning algorithms with conventional image processing techniques thus maximizing the amount of the original content to be restored while at the same time maximizing the restoration quality. TensorFlow and PyTorch significantly help in the building of complex network structures and shorten the time for restoration. Thus, this work is relevant in this context as it discusses a professionally oriented scalable and robust realisation of digital archiving and restoration and opens up future ways to develop an integration of AI-based methodologies into the preservation of cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Selection of Key Muscles and Gestures for Reliable Control in EMG-Based Wrist Prosthetics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Electromyography (EMG)—powered wrist prosthetics have emerged as a pivotal advancement in biomedical engineering, potentially restoring functional independence for individuals with upper limb amputations. This paper investigates the identification and selection of optimal muscles and gestures for EMG-based wrist prosthetics, a critical step toward achieving precise and reliable control of prosthetic movements. Key considerations include the quality of EMG signals, electrode placement feasibility, and the system's capacity to accurately interpret various wrist motions. With recent progress in upperlimb prosthetic technology, integrating EMG signals to control artificial wrist and hand movements has demonstrated significant promise. This study employs a systematic approach to identify muscles involved in specific wrist and hand actions, such as flexion, extension, and grip patterns, to enhance the responsiveness and precision of the control system. We are using different classifiers to determine the accuracy of the selected gestures The research emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate muscle groups and gestures, as these choices directly impact the prosthetic system's ability to differentiate between intended movements, minimizing misinterpretations and improving user experience. The findings underscore the essential role of muscle and gesture selection in advancing the design and functionality of EMG-based prosthetic devices.

articleTitle: Face Sketch Construction and Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: As the crime rate increases rapidly, law enforcement organizations are facing the urgent task of quickly and properly identifying suspects. This paper proposes an innovative way to improve crime detection using new facial recognition technologies by describing a newly designed technology that allows users to create precise facial drawings using a user- friendly drag-and-drop interface. In which it will completely eliminate the need for expert forensic artists. This paper allows to create face drawings that can be effortlessly matched to huge police databases by utilizing the powerful deep learning algorithms and cloud infrastructure. By combining these modern technologies this tool speeds up the identification process by overcoming the problems and issues of typical handdrawn drawings. It will not only enhance the speed and accuracy of suspect identification, but it will also give law enforcement officers an efficient resource thereby, it will enhance the overall investigative effectiveness and responsiveness.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Slam Techniques for AMRs in Warehouse Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The tremendous growth of the logistics sector has been driven by just in time principles, mass customization, omni channel distribution and a growing world population. These changes have led to the need for more flexibility and faster speed in supply chain operations encouraging the development of smart warehouse technologies. In this review article, we discuss the latest advance in warehouse automation with the emphasis on the importance of SLAM (Simultaneous localization and mapping) in improving the efficiency and scale of autonomous warehouse robots. Effective warehouse movement would rely upon autonomous systems that can map new areas while determining their pose, and SLAM provides this capacity. This work investigates various SLAM implementations based on Visual SLAM (VSLAM), LIDAR based SLAM, and Multi sensor SLAM, and describes their merits in different warehouse scenarios. We cover challenges and recent breakthroughs in SLAM, including its deployment in a number of settings, task completion autonomously while reacting to changes in environment, and its utility for performing complicated exploratory tasks without prior knowledge or human intervention. Additionally, the importance of order picking optimization is stressed, admitting it as one of the most important warehouse processes. This analysis discusses how the SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) technologies are allied with AGVs (Autonomous Ground Vehicles) and AMRs (Autonomous Mobile Robots) to give precise navigation, suitable order picking and overall improvement of warehouse operations.

articleTitle: Review of Artificial Intelligence Methods in Handwriting Identification Using CNN-RNN for Textural Features
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This review discusses the developments in handwriting recognition and optical character recognition (OCR) systems, with a focus on the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing accuracy, precision, and scalability. Modern methods include convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), hybrid CNN-RNN frameworks, and transformer-based architectures. These methods have been evaluated to address a wide range of tasks including handwritten text recognition (HTR), signature verification (SV), and multilingual text analysis. The impressive results have been achieved across a variety of datasets with 99.98 %-digit recognition and more than 97 % online handwritten word recognition. This involves high-end models such as hybrids CNN-RNN and transformer architecture, which have shown their effectiveness in capturing spatial and temporal features and adapting to handwriting variability in writing and linguistic contexts. The review underlines the importance of texture and structural feature analysis to progress with AIbased handwriting systems while emphasizing the extraction of fine-grained details such as pen pressure and stroke dynamics. Despite these advances, the issue of managing handwriting variability, dynamic styles, and underrepresented scripts like non-Latin languages still persists. Some open areas of research include robustness improvement, fine-tuning models to better adapt to variability, and interdisciplinary applications in forensic analysis, education, and medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Bone Cancer Prediction Using Regression Algorithms and Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Bone cancer is an aggressive disease that is often difficult to diagnose and treat and can be very dangerous for the patient. Bone cancer needs to be predicted in time and accurately for successful treatment and good patient care. This study aims to introduce a bone cancer prediction model that combines regression algorithms and machine learning techniques. The model reads data from patient medical records, such as age, sex, or genetic markers, and trains on it to predict the probability of bone cancer. We have tested linear regression, logistic regression, random forest multiple regression algorithm artificially neural networks, and support vector Machine Learning. We used an extensive bone cancer cases and controls dataset from different research centers and hospitals. 6 Our preliminary results show that the new method is more accurate in predicting bone cancer than traditional methods. Regrettably, regression algorithms and machine learning techniques are good enough to model many variables at once while detecting intricate patterns in the data, so as a result, the ability to predict is enhanced. Their model can help healthcare professionals identify PD earlier and make well-informed early treatment choices to improve patient outcomes and quality of life. This is a critical goal given the progressive nature of manystage synucleinopathies. However, more studies and validation are needed before implementing the model clinically.

articleTitle: Users' Acceptance, Behavioural Intention, and Adoption of Reward Points in India-A Systematic Literature Review Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The research examines the adoptions of consumers regarding acceptability and behavioral characteristics of reward points in India regarding the Millennial and Generation Z populations. This knowledge of the kind of incentive points program that responds to user influence is the premise of this research work with guidance from two theories “Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with a synthesis model and Theory of Planned Behavior”. The current study of a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach to compile and synthesize previous works on Behavioral intention towards reward points in India. Research articles are published in scientific journals, conference papers and academic papers from Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science. The literature was then combined according to the guidelines provided by the UTAUT and TPB models to compare the main themes and areas of future development in the current literature. The antecedent variables include “performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, price value, and habit”. Another set of constructs integrated into the model was identified to affect only behavioral intention and the relative importance of attitudes varied across the studies; it was also ascertained that some contextual variables are relevant to Indian Market. The research showed sensible holes in the current literature on the retention and loyalty of consumers in reward points schemes. The findings are useful for marketers and program designers interested in improving the impact of reward points schemes. It is recommended that organizations understand more about Millennials and Gen Z to have an idea of how to reward their consumers effectively. This paper offers one of the initial systematic literature reviews examining the use of reward points in India on young people. The paper is helpful in practice and academic literature indicates directions for further investigations which will benefit businesses and communities.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Determining Factors of Insomnia Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Insomnia is a widespread sleep disorder that has significant impact on individual's quality of life. Various factors can play a role for an individual receiving diagnosis for illness. However, fuzzy analysis can serve as a significant aid in identifying the contributing factors, where the root cause of this disorder is unpredictable. The primary goal of this report is to convey to the readers the salient feature that can have greater influence on an individual using fuzzy methods. We have employed three fuzzy methods in accordance with this report, AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process), Fuzzy TOPSIS (Technique for Order Performance by Similarity to Ideal Solution), Fuzzy Synthetic Evaluation that are categorized under Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM), which uses fuzzy logic. Instead of exact reasoning, Fuzzy logic deals with rough reasoning. It can also deal with uncertain and imprecise data. We have established MCDM to develop an effective approach towards decision making of various factors at many levels in predicting people with insomnia disorder. Our study suggests that the fuzzy methods can be a beneficial aid in early prediction, facilitating the path for additional research and application in the sleep treatment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fraud Detection with Gradient Boosting Algorithms in Credit Card Transactions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The paper shows the trade-offs between interpretability, computation cost and accuracy of many algorithms for fraud detection from machine learning perspective which provides important clues in this field and potential improvement paths. Linear model logistic regression is pitted against the gradient-boosting methods CatBoost and LightGBM, with excellent ability to handle complex connections in the data. To assess how well the models are performing, confusion matrices and visualizations such as ROC curves, accuracy comparisons are performed. While Logistic Regression results are respectable, as can be noticed from the higher AUC-ROC values and better F1 scores, gradient-boosting methods like CatBoost, LightGBM have a slight edge when it comes to predictive performance. The paper further mentions the trade-offs between performance and simplicity in its conclusion - including gradient-boosting models' usability for running on complex datasets like those present in credit card fraud detection use-cases. The results showed that while Logistic Regression performs reasonably on basic data, two gradient-boosting models, CatBoost and LightGBM, performed better overall, as evidenced by higher AUC-ROC values and F1 score.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Potential of Time Series IoT (Internet of Things) Data: The Transformative Role of AI and Machine Learning in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) within urban environments is reshaping how cities operate, yet the vast data generated often remains underutilized due to significant barriers to effective data management. Despite the widespread use of IoT devices, more than 75 percent of businesses do not follow a data-driven methodology. This is mainly due to obstacles such as the complexity of data integration, a lack of standardization, and insufficient technical skills. This paper examines the obstacles and highlights the transforming impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in converting IoT data into actionable insights that improve decision-making processes across diverse industries in smart cities. By addressing the complexities of data integration, AI and machine learning (ML) offer scalable solutions enabling real-time analytics, predictive modeling, and effi- cient resource management. This paper discusses specific applications of AI and ML in different industries, such as manufacturing, healthcare, energy, and agriculture. For example, AI-powered predictive maintenance in manufacturing helps reduce maintenance costs by up to 25 percent, while intelligent energy management in buildings can optimize energy consumption, enabling reduced costs by up to 30percent. In healthcare, AI-powered monitoring improves patient outcomes, and in agriculture, data-driven precision techniques can increase agricultural yields by 15percent. These figures indicate how important the role of Machine Learning is expected to be across verticals of the industry in the next few decades. The IoT trends indicate that implementing edge an-alytics further enhances the capabilities and efficiency of AI and ML. It allows for quick decision-making at the main source of data, therefore reducing latency and bandwidth demands. This paper is concluded by discussing the importance of AI and ML in unlocking the full potential of IoT investments, driving efficiencies, reducing costs, and improving the quality of urban living. Using these latest technologies the future of smart cities can be further adaptive, efficient and sustainable.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Heavy Rainfall Days in the Northern Himalayas: A Case Study of Shimla, Srinagar and Kargil
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In regions vulnerable to heavy rainfall, such as the north Himalayan region of India, which includes the states of Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Union Territory of Ladakh, an effective disaster management and ecosystem protection are especially important. Forecasting days with heavy rainfall accurately is crucial because these occurrences not only interfere with agricultural operations, but also cause landslides and flash floods, which cause serious damage to the environment and a large loss of life and property. Although traditional and conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) models are widely used, problems with accuracy and operational efficiency are common with such models. The present study incorporates a machine learning technique known as the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to analyze long-term nonlinear time series rainfall data and to encapsulate temporal dependencies in the data. The study uses daily climatological rainfall data from the Indian Meteorological Department in Pune for a period of 123 years (1901 to 2023). The extensive data set has enabled the LSTM model to be trained to forecast rainfall categories such as Rather Heavy Rain and Heavy Rain, as specified by the India Meteorological Department (IMD). This study also investigates the model's ability to forecast days with relatively rather heavy and heavy rainfall in the districts of Shimla, Srinagar and Kargil of Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh respectively.
