The research study examines the implementation of HR analytics, tracing its origins in industrial and organizational psychology and highlighting its current position as a pioneering field that is shaping the future of work. Furthermore, the prevailing HR analytics trends and predictions have an impact on the performance and decisionmaking of a business.

articleTitle: Intelligent IoT Driven Ecosystem for Real-Time Air and Noise Pollution Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The high speed of urbanisation and industrialisation necessitate keeping track of environmental parameters like air quality and noise pollution for the sustainability of ecology as well as the health of the environment and public health. By facilitating real-time data collection, analysis, and management, the Internet of Things (IoT) addresses challenges in an efficient way. The present work introduces an IoT based smart system for the real-time detection of both air and noise pollution. The developed system employs strategically placed sensor nodes to gather data on air quality parameters (e.g., particulate matter (PM2. 5, PM10), carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen dioxide (NO 2), sulfur dioxide (SO 2), and ozone (O 3), along with sound levels measured in décibels (dB). These nodes have inexpensive sensors and wireless communication modules, sending the data to a central server for data processing.

articleTitle: Geospatial Analysis and Machine Learning for Site Suitability of Geothermal Energy Plants
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The use of geospatial data and machine learning have upturned the evaluation of site suitability for geothermal energy plants. This purpose of this study is to determine the conditions of geothermal energy production using statistical and Resilience analysis models. Large datasets of geophysical and thermal properties can be found in the public domain and Geopandas and Rasterio libraries in Python allow working with such large datasets to create prediction models. Random Forests and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) prefilter further improves the accuracy by exploring the spatial distribution and thermal signature of the sites. The methodology discussed in this study can be seen to have a strong potential of enhancing the level of accuracy in the identification of geothermal sites hence minimising the uncertainty that may be encountered in exploratory drilling. The study advances the knowledge in the field of renewable energy by including a rich context for geospatial analysis as well as a framework for using machine learning to categorize the geothermal prospects of different regions. The findings therefore call for multi-disciplinary studies in enhancing the viable renewable energy sources, and promoting sustainable energies.

articleTitle: Digital Twins for Predictive Maintenance in Renewable Energy Grids with Tokenized Transactions: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: With the remarkable growth of the renewable energy sector, the management of distributed energy resources (DERs) like solar panels, wind turbines, and battery storage systems has become highly complex and increasingly significant. Conventional grid management methods are insufficient to handle the variability and unpredictability of renewable energy sources (RES). This research paper explores the integration of digital twins and tokenization as an innovative and creative solution to efficiently perform the operation, maintenance, and trading within renewable energy systems. Digital Twins are virtual models of physical assets, that enable real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and dynamic optimization of energy production. Real-time data from sensors is can be collected, analysed, and embedded in RES so that Digital Twins provides grid operators with important information about the performance and potential failures, which allows for efficient data-driven decision-making to enhance the energy output and grid stability. Tokenization, powered by blockchain technology, provides a decentralized and secure path for energy trading. Peer-to-peer (P2P) markets allow small-scale producers and consumers to trade energy directly using tokenized energy credits without relying on traditional utility companies. The combination of Digital Twins and tokenization enables a transparent, efficient, and resilient system where the extra generated energy is effectively traded, and assets are maintained at optimized performance levels. The research paper discusses the outcomes of this integration, particularly its efficiency to decrease its operational costs, improve energy efficiency, and contribute to global sustainability goals by encouraging the adoption of renewable energy sources. Through this technological merger, renewable energy integrated grids can become more adaptive, scalable, and sustainable, which will help to meet the increasing demand for clean energy.

articleTitle: Decoding Depression: An In-Depth Review of Multimedia-Based Detection on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Depression is one of the most common mental illness conditions, affecting millions of people in today's world, which can be generally described by persistent sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in daily activities. With the rapid adoption of social media, more and more people now express their feelings through various forms of multimedia, text, images, and audio, thereby creating a vast digital footprint that can be very useful for monitoring mental health with automated systems. This paper analyses the use of multimedia content on social networks in the detection of depressive behaviors. It discusses AI and deep learning techniques that include sentiment analysis, NLP, image recognition, and voice emotion recognition which might be useful to identify depressive signs from such multimedia inputs. The review has covered several issues on challenges that arise in multimedia-based detection, such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the ethical repercussions of mental health diagnosis by a system of automation. Its mention of concerns surrounding user confidentiality, reducing bias in AI models, and making proper balances between human oversight and automation is very important. Finally, the paper presents possible future work that could ensure the accuracy, timeliness, and ethical standards of depression detection systems toward more responsible technology-driven mental health care.

articleTitle: Enhancing GPT-2 Text Generation Through Reinforcement Learning and Token-Based Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This study investigates the use of the Gym library to combine reinforcement learning with a pre-trained language model, GPT-2 to generate text in a customised setting. Using reward-basedlearning, the model is trained to optimise text creation. The environment's goal is to produce text from user input while adhering to distinct actions that represent token from the GPT-2 tokeniser. Throughout training, the model is prodded to get better and better inside this random reward system. We describe in detail how to use the Adam optimiser and train and test the model in this context. We also put up a testing mechanism that will yield performance metrics on text production through pre-programmed prompts. The model's output from the experiment shows highly repetitive behaviour, which highlights the need for more intricate reward systems and exploration strategies. Subsequent future work will focus on refining the reward function, utilising advanced exploration strategies and expanding the approach to larger language models.

articleTitle: Ontology Modelling of AI-Chatbot for Communicating Credential Responses
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: When evaluating the authenticity of a resource person offering a package for a workshop or training, there are many challenges encountered if the professional profile of the resource person is not public or available with only limited details. A few issues are verifying credentials, lack of public reviews or testimonials, limited online presence, misrepresentation of past work, lack of transparency about contents, over-promising outcomes, upfront payment requests, chances of cyber frauds, etc. In this case, it is required to check the background from authentic sources in least amount of time. The paper presents the ontology design and implementation of a chatbot to verify the credentials along with the technical potential, together with any previous equivalent event records if available. The proposed chatbot is trained on a university website and manual data entry. It may be helpful to develop the audience's confidence in the resource person and help the user to proceed further. This proposed system is concerned with checking the authenticity of a resource person from academia or IT industry providing some training. The audiences can use the chatbot associated with organization website of university or college to verify the resource person's details.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Brinjal (Solanum Melongena) Leaf Diseases Detection and Classification: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Agrarian output is the aspect that our country's economy most strongly depends. The practice of growing crops, which leverages a range of artificial intelligence learning-based technology and detectors, is becoming more and more popular in agriculture as advancement in research and technologies. Research assessments reveal that infections that sprout on plant foliage are causing 56% of major losses to the agriculture sector. Monitoring the disease's development and increasing agricultural production are essential. Initially, there is need to identify the diseases early and take steps to stop its propagation. Consequently, might be able to resolve this issue by implementing specific algorithms for identifying diseases on leaflets. Combining image processing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence-based techniques, this research gives an analysis of recent developments in the field of identifying brinjal leaf diseases. This study highlights the current scenario of the agriculture sector in India related to brinjal crops (solanum melongena), the taxonomy of brinjal crop diseases, existing machine learning computational methods employed for the identification of brinjal leaf infections and their comparison, challenges, and discussion with future scope. Implementing these ML-based techniques allows for continuous monitoring of phytosanitary conditions, giving farmers immediate real-time insights into crop conditions. This enhances long-term sustainability as farmers can proactively manage their fields and make informed decisions that contribute to farming systems' ability to endure climate change and other challenges.

articleTitle: Investigation of Diverse ML and DL Algorithms Toward the Segmentation and Classification of Mammographic Breast Density
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Breast cancer is a deadly disease that usually affects women. Since a higher mammographic density is linked to a higher risk of developing breast cancer, it is crucial to consider this factor when determining an individual's risk for the illness. This makes it possible to guarantee thorough breast cancer screening and detection. With a focus on their possible applications in breast cancer prediction, this work investigates machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods for categorizing and segmenting mammography breast density. We demonstrate their applicability in therapeutic scenarios by comparing the performance of different algorithms. Its methods for categorizing and dividing mammographic breast density have shown to be incredibly effective. By offering accurate and consistent evaluations, these techniques can help radiologists make well-informed decisions. This survey summarizes the most recent state-of-the-art methods and covers developments in ML and DL algorithms for breast density segmentation and classification.

articleTitle: An Approach to Control Safety Message Congestion in IoV Using Metaheuristic Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: In Internet of Vehicle (IoV), the effective dissemination of safety messages is crucial for enhancing road safety, particularly given the dynamic nature of vehicle mobility and frequent link breakages. This problem is addressed by Cluster-Based MAC (CB-MAC) protocol designed to optimize safety message broadcasting by organizing vehicles into smaller clusters. Another strategy of vehicle ID based MAC protocol reduces the likelihood of transmission collisions by ensuring that vehicles possess distinctive identical back-off numbers. Each vehicle generates CAMs that include a unique vehicle identifier (ID), which is incorporated into a vehicle-specific random backoff mechanism. The protocol also avoids consecutive transmission by any vehicle by eliminating the risk of selecting zero as initial back-off number. To further enhance communication efficiency, our study amalgamates metaheuristic method for cluster formation, cluster head election, and cluster merging, allowing for effective intra- and inter-cluster communication along with CB MAC and vehicle id- based algorithms.

articleTitle: Establishing a Resilient Domestic Infrastructure for In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) to Enhance India's Biotechnology Capacity and Economic Resilience
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The surge in demand for In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) kits in India, driven by rapid healthcare sector expansion, has highlighted a substantial reliance on imported high-value components, including conjugated antibodies, antigens, and specialized enzymes. This reliance restricts India's path to achieving self-sufficiency and realizing its full economic potential. This research presents a strategic framework to establish a robust domestic infrastructure for producing high-quality IVD components. By deploying cutting-edge biotechnologies, establishing advanced research centers, and promoting cross-sectoral collaboration, India can enhance its biotechnology capabilities and develop timely, cost-effective diagnostic solutions. The economic impact of a localized IVD production ecosystem is significant: reducing import dependency could yield annual savings of approximately USD 400 million, strengthening foreign exchange reserves and buffering against global supply chain disruptions. Furthermore, a secure supply of cost-effective diagnostic resources would elevate public health resilience, equipping India to address health crises with greater self-reliance. This paper emphasizes the transformative potential of shifting to domestic production, in alignment with national programs like ‘Make in India’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat.’ By fostering a culture of innovation, stringent regulatory adherence, and excellence in research, India can position itself competitively within the global IVD landscape. The roadmap proposed here supports sustained growth, addressing both national healthcare needs and India's potential contributions to global health improvements. Additionally, this shift is anticipated to invigorate the Indian economy by decreasing dependency on imports, generating employment, and positioning India as a pioneering force in biotechnological innovation.

articleTitle: Synthetic Realities: A Critical Review of Deepfake Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Deepfakes involve the manipulation of visual content using various techniques, initially intended for enjoyment, but potentially resulting in detrimental effects for economic, political, and societal objectives, including money fraud and identity fraud. Deepfakes, or hyper-realistic generated pictures and videos, are now feasible due to the fusion of deep learning and computer vision methodologies such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and autoencoders. Individuals with malicious intent or even non-technical users of machine learning can manipulate a photograph or video by modifying the data, resulting in a new image or video that is undetectable to both humans and machines. Public trust in digital media material has decreased due to deepfakes, since individuals can no longer believe the authenticity of the images they see. Research on deepfake detection is essential to maintain public trust in digital multimedia. This article explores multiple deepfake detection strategies to deal with deepfake and present a literature analysis to give an up to date summery of research activities in the field of deepfake detection. This paper provides a thorough examination of deep-fake phenomena and emphasizes several methods for creating and identifying deepfakes.

articleTitle: Cognitive Intelligence and Big Data: A Symbiotic Approach to Predictive Analytics in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The paradigm of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems to mimic human thought processes and enhance decision-making is titled Cognitive Intelligence. When employed in conjunction with Big Data Analytics to process vast volumes of structured and unstructured data, it unlocks ingenious possibilities in Predictive Analytics. Predictive Analytics leverages historical data to forecast future healthcare outcomes, enabling early diagnosis, personalized treatment, and better resource allocation. This paper investigates the convergence of Cognitive Intelligence, Big Data, and Predictive Analytics, highlighting their transformative potential in the healthcare sector. The intersection of these technologies empowers healthcare providers with data-driven insights, benefitting patient care and operational efficiency. The objective of this study is to demonstrate how integrating Cognitive Intelligence with Big Data enables the development of predictive models that enhance decision-making and outcomes in healthcare. With an overview of the applications of these technologies, a comprehensive discussion on the methodological frameworks for their integration, and key findings from case studies like ARDA, the results from this paper indicate that this synergy significantly enhances predictive accuracy and healthcare outcomes, marking a new era in personalized medicine and clinical decision support.

articleTitle: QuantiSA: Quantified Service Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Microservices architecture has acquired significant popularity in modern application development because of its emphasis on independence, scalability, robustness, agility, and faster deployment cycles. This architectural style contrasts with the traditional monolithic architecture, where applications were built as single, indivisible units. The monolithic approach simplifies development and deployment, but at the same time, they become cumbersome when planning to scale. Deployment of new changes and technology integrations are also very challenging. Microservices addressed these limitations by way of designing the applications in such a way that applications are loosely coupled to each other and deployable independently to serve specific business needs. This approach enhances scalability, maintainability, and development speed. However, Microservices also introduced its own set of challenges. This paper explores the fundamental principles, advantages, and challenges of both monolithic and microservices architectures. Further, it proposes a novel architecture named as QuantiSA (Quantified Service Architecture), which aims to combine the strengths of both monolithic and Microservices architectures. QuantiSA is designed to meet the needs of large-scale enterprise applications, and will be discussed and compared in context of its performance, cost of development, delivery, infrastructure, maintenance, scalability, and security implementation.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Driven CNN Architectures for Automated Defect Detection in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Recent innovations in electronics manufacturing have created demands for timely an accurate defect during production of printed circuit board (PCB). The following paper gives a solid approach to PCBA defect detection using CNN, especially by transfer learning. In this method, the experts used pre-trained models like ResNet and EfficientNet besides retraining them on PCB defect datasets that are available to the public; this boosted the defect recognition process greatly. The method involves using TensorFlow/Keras based frameworks in the implementation and optimization of the CNN models and use OpenCV for a broad image preprocessing. Said integration of transfer learning with current most advanced neural architectures enables the achievement of very high detection rates even where domain-specific information is scarce. This study reveals the promising idea of using open datasets and developing practical CNN approaches to detect the defects for scaled electronics manufacturing.

articleTitle: Effects of Power System in the Tourism Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: The prime objective of the study is to find out the importance and effect of digital marketing in the tourism sector of Bangladesh and also understand the behavioural aspect of tourists' perceptions of digital marketing based on the data collected through the survey from the perspective of Bangladesh. An in-depth literature review was done to understand the significance of digital marketing. Primary data is mainly used to observe the behavioural aspect of tourists regarding digital marketing in the tourism sector of Bangladesh. Data was collected from 173 respondents through purposive sampling. The valid response rate was 72.08%. Frequency., reliability tests., and standard deviation methods were used to analyze data regression. Among the nine hypotheses., five were supported. The research shows that digital marketing strategies influence tourist minds and behaviour., which are highly needed to create a strong tourism brand in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Eavesdropper-Aware Optimization of Cooperative Relaying Networks in the Presence of Heterogeneous Interference
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: To improve the secure communication performance in untrusted heterogeneous interference environments, this paper designs an eavesdropper-aware optimization model for CRNs. By using a combination of sophisticated optimization approaches, the model updates resource distributions and relay deployments on the fly boosting secrecy rates and slashing outage probabilities in one fell swoop. Extensive simulations show that the model is effective at reducing these effects under the varying nature of interference attacks (including co-channel and jamming) while keeping the performance of the system. A comparative analysis with existing models shows the improved capability of this method to provide unbeatable security along-with increased throughput and less energy. This research lays a foundation for investigation in secure communications, bringing advantages of enhanced robustness against diversified eavesdropping threats at different tiers within sophisticated networks.

articleTitle: A Framework for Security Enhancement and Anomaly Detection in IoT Based Smart Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) represents the future of developing countries and networking technology, by integrating advanced communication protocols, automation, and data analytics to get better efficiency, reliability, and capabilities of various systems. IoT refers to adaptive and highly automated systems designed to manage intricate communication environments. By leveraging modern technologies, these networks boost efficiency, reliability, and scalability, all while minimizing human intervention. Despite their powerful capabilities, IoT networks face several challenges, including issues related to scalability, interoperability, reliability, energy efficiency, security, and privacy. Among these, security remains a primary concern. There are various technologies like block chain, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and fog computing etc which are being used for enhancing security and privacy in Smart Networks. The focus of this research paper is to investigate security challenges within smart networks based on IoT networks and to propose a framework to enhance security and privacy of smart networks by developing authentication scheme and detecting anomalies using Machine Learning Technique.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Algorithm for Brain Tumor Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Tumor detection and cialis generique prediction are critical parts of medicine as they require medical professionals to diagnose the affected regions correctly. Given the complexity associated with brain structures and dynamism, this is very hard. Hybrid algorithms have gained popularity in recent years and take the best from each technique to improve the correctness and competence of brain tumor prediction. This study aims to analyze three different hybrid algorithms, namely Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Ant Gathering Optimization for brain tumor prediction. The brain MRI images are processed using the image processing methodology to extract significant features from this dataset. Combining these features is used as input for hybrid algorithms to predict brain tumor presence. These outcomes reveal that the Hybrid GA-PSO model performed better than the two others, having an accuracy rate of 95%. The prediction accuracy is improved via the genetic operators of GA, which are incorporated into PSO and use its fast convergence to execute the GA-PSO algorithm. The execution time of GSO is more rapid than ACO, which enables real-time predictions by using it.

articleTitle: A Study on the Integration of Haptic Feedback for Optimizing Telerobotic Surgery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: This paper aimed at conducting a comprehensive discussion on haptic feedback and force based teleoperation in the domain of surgical robots similar far-reaching significance of haptic feedback based operation in eradicating telerobotic surgery problems of sensory feel and motor skills for surgeons. Nonetheless, although the utilization of haptic feedback in the field of telesurgery has been demonstrated to have a plethora of benefits including enhanced realism during the interaction of tissue as well as the over-proportionate enhancement of surgical results, haptic feedback's adoption into commercial telesurgical systems remains limited. This paper categorizes the common technical barriers that have prevented broader use of haptic devices, such issues to do with fidelity, stability, and force feedback. Moreover, it also investigates strategies that are being investigated to address these problems, including the improved control algorithms, the use of machine learning techniques as well as combination of force reflection techniques. The paper also aims to review the ergonomics of haptic systems and their contribution to medical education particularly in surgery, the implications of haptic systems on patient outcomes is also considered. In concert with this, this study aims at presenting a research and development agenda for haptic integration in telesurgical operations through an elaborate review and synthesis.

articleTitle: Identification of Acute Preictal Signatures in EEG Using Univariate Linear Analysis and Unsupervised Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Cognitive Computing in Engineering, Communications, Sciences and Biomedical Health Informatics (IC3ECSBHI)
abstract: Epilepsy, a neurological disorder marked by sudden, excessive brain activity, significantly increases the risk of premature death, largely due to sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). Detecting the preictal phase of seizures (PIPS) is essential for seizure-prevention systems that could enhance patient safety and autonomy. This study presents a methodology that combines univariate linear analysis with automated noise removal to accurately cluster acute PIPS events occurring 5 minutes before seizure onset. Our findings show that, while filtering improves cluster separation, unfiltered data reveal a higher concentration of acute PIPS events (Unfiltered - 60 (31.67 - 100), Filtered - 51.67 (31.67 - 86.67), P < 0.01). Additionally, using unsupervised methods to search for preictal patterns in EEG data suggests that it is possible to identify seizure-specific preictal signatures for certain seizures and patients.
